cards.front:
The six classical 'simple machines' include: lever, pulley, inclined plane, wedge, screw and:

(A) Gear
(B) Wheel and axle
(C) Spring
(D) Piston
cards.back:
(B) Wheel and axle

Mechanics & Motion — The six simple machines — lever, wheel and axle, pulley, inclined plane, wedge, screw — were defined by Renaissance scientists; earlier Greek / Roman thinkers recognised five. A wedge is effectively a moving inclined plane (axe, knife). A screw is a wrapped inclined plane. Gears, springs, pistons are NOT simple machines — they are compound or later additions.

cards.front:
A 200 N load is lifted with an effort of 50 N using a pulley system. The mechanical advantage is:

(A) 2
(B) 4
(C) 6
(D) 0.25
cards.back:
(B) 4

Mechanics & Motion — MA = Load / Effort = 200 / 50 = 4. So a system of 4 pulleys (or an equivalent block-and-tackle) that halves the force twice over would do this. Trap answer 0.25 is Effort / Load (inverted formula). The student needs to lift the rope through 4× the distance the load rises — standard trade-off.

cards.front:
An axe used to split wood is best classified as a:

(A) Lever
(B) Wedge
(C) Pulley
(D) Wheel and axle
cards.back:
(B) Wedge

Mechanics & Motion — An axe — sharp edge narrowing to a point — is a wedge. It concentrates a large downward force into a small cross-section, splitting the wood fibres apart. Other wedges — knives, chisels, nails, pins. Wedges are effectively 'moving inclined planes'. The narrower (longer) the wedge, the greater the mechanical advantage — but the more strokes you need.

cards.front:
Which of the following is a SCALAR quantity?

(A) Displacement
(B) Speed
(C) Velocity
(D) Acceleration
cards.back:
(B) Speed

Mechanics & Motion — SCALAR — magnitude only (no direction). Examples: speed, distance, mass, time, temperature, energy, work, power, charge, density. VECTOR — magnitude + direction. Examples: displacement, velocity, acceleration, force, momentum, torque, electric/magnetic field. Speed = |velocity|; distance ≥ |displacement| (path length vs straight-line displacement). Vectors follow vector-addition (parallelogram, triangle); scalars add algebraically.

cards.front:
A car travelling at 20 m/s decelerates uniformly at 4 m/s² and comes to a stop. Distance travelled before stopping:

(A) 25 m
(B) 50 m
(C) 80 m
(D) 100 m
cards.back:
(B) 50 m

Mechanics & Motion — Use v² = u² + 2as. Final v = 0, initial u = 20, a = −4 (deceleration). 0 = 400 + 2·(−4)·s → 8s = 400 → s = 50 m. Time to stop: v = u + at → 0 = 20 + (−4)t → t = 5 s. Or use s = ut + ½at² = 20(5) + ½(−4)(25) = 100 − 50 = 50 m ✓.

cards.front:
An object is in projectile motion. At the highest point of the trajectory, its:

(A) Velocity is zero in both x and y
(B) Vertical (y) velocity is zero, but horizontal (x) velocity remains constant
(C) Total speed is maximum
(D) Acceleration is zero
cards.back:
(B) Vertical (y) velocity is zero, but horizontal (x) velocity remains constant

Mechanics & Motion — Projectile motion = independent x + y. x-component: a_x = 0 (no horizontal force, ignoring air drag) → v_x = u·cosθ constant throughout. y-component: a_y = −g (downward) → v_y = u·sinθ − gt. At highest point, v_y = 0 (rising stops) → t = u·sinθ/g; H_max = (u·sinθ)²/(2g); Range R = u²·sin(2θ)/g. Maximum range at θ = 45°. Acceleration is g (downward) at all times — never zero. Total speed at top = u·cosθ (horizontal only).

At highest point, v_y = 0 (rising stops) → t = u·sinθ/g; H_max = (u·sinθ)²/(2g); Range R = u²·sin(2θ)/g. Maximum range at θ = 45°. Acceleration is g (downward) at all times — never zero. cards.front:
If two forces of 3 N and 4 N act on a body at right angles, the magnitude of the resultant is:

(A) 1 N
(B) 5 N (Pythagoras: √(3² + 4²))
(C) 7 N
(D) 12 N
cards.back:
(B) 5 N (Pythagoras: √(3² + 4²))

Mechanics & Motion — For two perpendicular vectors: |R|² = |A|² + |B|² → |R| = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5 N. Direction tan θ = 4/3 → θ ≈ 53° from the 3-N vector. For non-perpendicular: |R|² = |A|² + |B|² + 2|A||B|·cosα, where α is the angle between them. Max R = A + B when α = 0; min R = |A − B| when α = 180°. For 3 + 4 vectors, range is 1 N to 7 N.

cards.front:
A body moves around a circle of radius r at constant speed v. Its acceleration is:

(A) Zero
(B) v²/r — directed towards the centre (centripetal)
(C) v/r outwards
(D) v²·r
cards.back:
(B) v²/r — directed towards the centre (centripetal)

Mechanics & Motion — Even at constant SPEED, the velocity vector changes direction continuously → acceleration is non-zero. Centripetal acceleration a_c = v²/r, always pointing towards the centre. Force F = m·v²/r is the net inward force (provided by gravity for satellites; tension for a stone on a string; normal/friction for a car on a curved road). Without this force, body would move tangentially (Newton's 1st law). Centrifugal 'force' is a pseudo-force in rotating frame — not a real force.

cards.front:
A ball is thrown vertically upwards with initial velocity 20 m/s (g = 10 m/s²). Time to reach maximum height:

(A) 1 s
(B) 2 s
(C) 4 s
(D) 10 s
cards.back:
(B) 2 s

Mechanics & Motion — At maximum height, v = 0. Use v = u − gt (taking up positive, g acts down): 0 = 20 − 10t → t = 2 s. Maximum height: h = u·t − ½g·t² = 20·2 − ½·10·4 = 40 − 20 = 20 m. Total time of flight (up and back down) = 4 s. By symmetry, time up = time down = 2 s; the ball returns with same speed (20 m/s, but downward).

cards.front:
A man walks 4 km East then 3 km North. His total DISPLACEMENT (straight-line distance from start) is:

(A) 7 km
(B) 5 km (Pythagoras: √(4²+3²) = 5)
(C) 12 km
(D) 1 km
cards.back:
(B) 5 km (Pythagoras: √(4²+3²) = 5)

Mechanics & Motion — DISTANCE traversed = 4 + 3 = 7 km (scalar, path length). DISPLACEMENT = vector from start to end = √(4² + 3²) = 5 km in direction NE (tan⁻¹(3/4) ≈ 37° North of East). Distance ≥ |displacement| always. Equal only when motion is in a single direction. The 3-4-5 right-triangle is the most familiar Pythagorean triple — useful pattern to recognise instantly.

cards.front:
Work done by a constant force F over a displacement d in the same direction is given by:

(A) F × d²
(B) F × d (force × distance)
(C) F + d
(D) F / d
cards.back:
(B) F × d (force × distance)

Mechanics & Motion — Work W = F · d cosθ (where θ = angle between force and displacement). When F is in same direction as d, θ = 0, cosθ = 1, so W = F × d. SI unit: joule (J) = newton·metre. If force is perpendicular to displacement (θ = 90°), W = 0 — e.g., gravity does NO work on a horizontally-moving object; centripetal force does NO work in circular motion.

cards.front:
Kinetic energy of an object of mass m moving at speed v is:

(A) m·v
(B) ½ m·v² (half mass velocity-squared)
(C) m·v²
(D) m·g·h
cards.back:
(B) ½ m·v² (half mass velocity-squared)

Mechanics & Motion — Translational kinetic energy KE = ½mv² — joules in SI. m in kg, v in m/s. Doubling velocity QUADRUPLES the KE (a key safe-driving message). m·v is momentum (linear); m·v² is twice the KE; m·g·h is gravitational potential energy. Rotational KE = ½ I ω² (I — moment of inertia, ω — angular speed). Total KE for an object that translates AND rotates = sum of both.

cards.front:
Potential energy of a body of mass 5 kg raised to a height of 10 m above ground (g = 10 m/s²) is:

(A) 100 J
(B) 500 J
(C) 50 J
(D) 1000 J
cards.back:
(B) 500 J

Mechanics & Motion — Gravitational PE = m·g·h = 5 × 10 × 10 = 500 J. Sign convention — usually positive if h measured up from a reference; can be negative if below reference. Alternative — elastic PE = ½kx² for a spring stretched by x. Conservation of mechanical energy: KE + PE = constant (in absence of friction). Free-fall: PE→KE conversion. At a pendulum's lowest point, PE→0, KE max; at extremes, KE→0, PE max.

cards.front:
Power is defined as:

(A) Force per unit area
(B) Rate of doing work; energy per unit time (P = W/t)
(C) Mass × acceleration
(D) Force × distance
cards.back:
(B) Rate of doing work; energy per unit time (P = W/t)

Mechanics & Motion — Power P = W/t = energy/time. SI unit: watt (W) = J/s. 1 horsepower (hp) = 746 W ≈ 0.75 kW. Bulb rated 60 W consumes 60 J/s. 1 kWh (kilowatt-hour) = 3.6 × 10⁶ J = 1 unit of electricity (the billing unit). For circuits: P = V·I = I²·R = V²/R. The car horsepower is a good intuitive comparator — a 100-hp car can do 100×746 J = 74.6 kJ of work per second.

cards.front:
A pump delivers 1500 J of energy in 5 seconds. Its power output is:

(A) 30 W
(B) 300 W
(C) 750 W
(D) 7500 W
cards.back:
(B) 300 W

Mechanics & Motion — P = W/t = 1500 / 5 = 300 W. Power = energy delivered per second. Compare household appliances: tube light ~40 W, ceiling fan ~70 W, fridge ~200 W (steady state), microwave ~800 W, AC ~1500 W (per ton).

cards.front:
By the work-energy theorem, the net work done on a moving object equals:

(A) Change in its mass
(B) Change in its kinetic energy
(C) Change in temperature
(D) Total displacement
cards.back:
(B) Change in its kinetic energy

Mechanics & Motion — Work-Energy Theorem: W_net = ΔKE = ½m(v² − u²), where u and v are initial and final speeds. Positive work → KE increases (object accelerates); negative work (e.g., friction, brakes) → KE decreases. Foundational to all energy problems in mechanics. Implies if you know force × distance, you can find final velocity without doing kinematics. Doesn't depend on path — only initial / final states (path-independence is true for conservative forces only).

cards.front:
A 100 W bulb operating for 10 hours consumes electrical energy equal to:

(A) 1 kWh (= 1 'unit')
(B) 10 kWh
(C) 0.1 kWh
(D) 100 kWh
cards.back:
(A) 1 kWh (= 1 'unit')

Mechanics & Motion — Energy = power × time = 100 W × 10 h = 1,000 Wh = 1 kWh = 1 'unit' on your electricity bill. At ₹6/unit (typical residential), that costs ₹6. LED bulb of equivalent brightness consumes ~10 W → 90% energy saving. India's CFL/LED rollout (UJALA scheme since 2015) has saved billions of kWh.

cards.front:
ARCHIMEDES' PRINCIPLE states that the UPTHRUST on an object submerged in a fluid equals:

(A) The object's weight
(B) The weight of the fluid DISPLACED by the object
(C) The object's density
(D) Pressure × volume of fluid
cards.back:
(B) The weight of the fluid DISPLACED by the object

Gravitation & Fluids — Archimedes' Principle — upthrust (buoyant force) = weight of displaced fluid. If object's weight < weight displaced, it FLOATS. If equal, object is SUSPENDED. If weight > displacement, it SINKS. Explains ships staying afloat (steel, but overall density low).

cards.front:
An object FLOATS on water if its density is:

(A) Greater than that of water
(B) Less than that of water (≤ 1 g/cc)
(C) Much greater than water
(D) Unrelated to water density
cards.back:
(B) Less than that of water (≤ 1 g/cc)

Gravitation & Fluids — Object floats if its AVERAGE density < density of fluid (water = 1 g/cc). Wood floats (~0.6 g/cc). Iron sinks (~7.8 g/cc) — but iron ships float because overall density (inc. hollow air-filled interior) < 1.

cards.front:
It is EASIER to swim in SEA WATER than in RIVER water because:

(A) Sea water is colder
(B) Sea water has HIGHER DENSITY (from dissolved salts) → greater buoyant force
(C) Sea water has more oxygen
(D) Rivers flow faster
cards.back:
(B) Sea water has HIGHER DENSITY (from dissolved salts) → greater buoyant force

Gravitation & Fluids — Salt content makes sea water denser (~1.025 g/cc) vs fresh water (~1 g/cc). Greater fluid density → greater upthrust per unit volume submerged → object floats more easily. Dead Sea (~30% salinity, density ~1.24 g/cc) — people float effortlessly.

cards.front:
The SI unit of PRESSURE is:

(A) Newton
(B) Pascal
(C) Joule
(D) Bar
cards.back:
(B) Pascal

Gravitation & Fluids — Pressure = Force / Area. SI unit: Pascal (Pa). 1 atm ≈ 101,325 Pa ≈ 1.01 bar. Tyre pressures often in 'bar' or 'psi'. Atmospheric pressure decreases with altitude — hence planes pressurise cabins. 1 Pa = 1 N/m².

cards.front:
A HYDRAULIC LIFT works on the principle of:

(A) Archimedes' principle
(B) Pascal's law
(C) Bernoulli's principle
(D) Newton's 3rd law
cards.back:
(B) Pascal's law

Gravitation & Fluids — Pascal's law (1653) — small force on small piston creates same pressure everywhere in the fluid; a large piston with 100× area exerts 100× the force. Used in hydraulic lifts, brakes, jacks, presses. Amplifies force, not energy (same work done). pressure applied on a confined fluid is transmitted equally in all directions.

cards.front:
BERNOULLI'S PRINCIPLE explains:

(A) Why objects fall
(B) Why faster-flowing fluid has lower pressure
(C) Why hot air rises
(D) Why objects float
cards.back:
(B) Why faster-flowing fluid has lower pressure

Gravitation & Fluids — Bernoulli's principle (1738) — in flowing fluid, speed and pressure trade off: higher speed → lower pressure. Applications: aeroplane lift (curved top of wing makes air flow faster → lower pressure above → lift), spinning ball curves in sports (Magnus effect), venturi flow meter. and how aeroplane wings generate lift.

cards.front:
DENSITY of pure water at 4°C is approximately:

(A) 0.5 g/cc
(B) 1 g/cc
(C) 2 g/cc
(D) 10 g/cc
cards.back:
(B) 1 g/cc

Gravitation & Fluids — Water — maximum density at 4°C = 1 g/cc (or 1000 kg/m³). Water is UNUSUAL — it is LESS dense as ice (~0.92) than liquid → ice floats. This is because water molecules form a more open hexagonal lattice when freezing. Crucial for aquatic life (water bodies freeze from top).

cards.front:
Archimedes' principle states that the buoyant force on an object equals the weight of:

(A) The object itself
(B) The fluid displaced by the object
(C) The fluid in the container
(D) The air above the fluid
cards.back:
(B) The fluid displaced by the object

Gravitation & Fluids — Archimedes — the upward buoyant force equals the weight of the fluid displaced. An object floats if it can displace an amount of fluid equal to its own weight without being fully submerged. Iron ships float because their hollow hull displaces far more water than their metal weight. Hydrogen balloons rise because air displaced weighs more than the balloon + gas inside.

cards.front:
Hydraulic lifts and car brakes work on the principle of:

(A) Archimedes' principle
(B) Pascal's law
(C) Bernoulli's principle
(D) Newton's third law
cards.back:
(B) Pascal's law

cards.front:
The atmospheric pressure at sea level is approximately:

(A) 1 Pa
(B) 101 kPa
(C) 10 kPa
(D) 1,000 kPa
cards.back:
(B) 101 kPa

cards.front:
The first mercury barometer, a device to measure atmospheric pressure, was invented by:

(A) Galileo Galilei
(B) Evangelista Torricelli
(C) Blaise Pascal
(D) Robert Boyle
cards.back:
(B) Evangelista Torricelli

Gravitation & Fluids — Torricelli — Italian physicist, student of Galileo — invented the mercury barometer in 1643. A sealed glass tube inverted in a dish of mercury stands with the mercury column ~760 mm high at sea level — held up by atmospheric pressure pushing on the exposed mercury. The unit 'torr' (1 mmHg) is named after him. Pascal later replicated the experiment and showed pressure falls with altitude.

cards.front:
The reason why an aircraft wing generates lift is most directly explained by:

(A) Archimedes' principle
(B) Bernoulli's principle
(C) Pascal's law
(D) Hooke's law
cards.back:
(B) Bernoulli's principle

Gravitation & Fluids — Bernoulli — faster-moving fluid has lower pressure. An aircraft wing (aerofoil) is shaped so that air moves faster over the top and slower underneath → pressure on top is lower than on the bottom → net upward lift. Angle-of-attack and Newton's third law (wing redirects air downward → reaction upwards) also contribute. Archimedes is for static buoyancy in fluids; Pascal's law is for transmitted pressure in confined fluids.

Water pressure at the bottom of a 10-metre-deep tank of still water is approximately (ρg ≈ 10,000):

(A) 10 kPa
(B) 100 kPa
(C) 1,000 kPa
(D) 1 kPa

cards.front:
NEWTON's LAW OF UNIVERSAL GRAVITATION states that the gravitational force between two masses is:

(A) Proportional to sum of masses + distance
(B) F = G·m₁·m₂/r²
(C) Depends only on mass of larger body
(D) Proportional to r (not r²)
cards.back:
(B) F = G·m₁·m₂/r²

Gravitation & Fluids — NEWTON's LAW OF UNIVERSAL GRAVITATION (1687, published in PRINCIPIA MATHEMATICA) — every particle in universe attracts every other with a force directly proportional to product of their masses + inversely proportional to square of distance between centers. FORMULA: F = G·m₁·m₂/r². (1) F = gravitational force (Newtons); (2) m₁, m₂ = masses (kg); (3) r = distance between centers (m); (4) G = UNIVERSAL GRAVITATIONAL CONSTANT = 6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg². G measured by HENRY CAVENDISH (1798, 'Cavendish Experiment') using torsion balance — famous 'weighing the Earth' experiment; gave first accurate G value + hence Earth's mass + density. PROPERTIES: (1) ALWAYS ATTRACTIVE (no repulsive gravity known, unlike EM force). (2) INVERSE-SQUARE law (F ∝ 1/r²) — identical mathematical form to Coulomb's electric force. (3) Acts over ANY DISTANCE (infinite range). (4) Independent of medium. (5) Mutual (Newton's 3rd law — Earth attracts Moon; Moon attracts Earth same magnitude opposite direction). APPLICATIONS: (1) PLANETARY MOTION — Kepler's 3 LAWS (1609, 1619) elegantly derived from Newton's law — (a) Law 1 (ellipse): planets orbit Sun in ellipses with Sun at one focus. (b) Law 2 (equal areas): line from Sun to planet sweeps equal areas in equal times (conservation of angular momentum). (c) Law 3 (harmonic): T² ∝ r³ (period squared proportional to semi-major axis cubed). (2) TIDES — Moon + Sun gravity causes tidal bulges; 2 high tides per day (Moon side + opposite side); SPRING TIDES (new + full moon, Sun + Moon aligned) + NEAP TIDES (quarter moons, 90°); impacts on coastal life, marine creatures, fisheries. (3) SATELLITE MOTION — artificial satellites orbit by centripetal gravity balance (gravity = mv²/r). LEO (altitude 200-2000 km, period 90-120 min); MEO (2,000-35,786 km; GPS ~20,200 km, 12 hr period); GEO / GEOSTATIONARY (35,786 km altitude, 24 hr period — 'sidereal day'; appears stationary over equator — used for communications, weather satellites); HEO (highly elliptical). (4) ESCAPE VELOCITY — v = √(2GM/R) = 11.2 km/s for Earth (to escape Earth's gravity). From Moon ~2.4 km/s. From Sun ~42 km/s at Earth distance. LIMITATIONS of Newton: fails at strong fields + near speed of light. REPLACED by EINSTEIN'S GENERAL RELATIVITY (1915) — gravity is CURVATURE OF SPACETIME by mass-energy; predicts gravitational lensing, gravitational waves (LIGO 2015 direct detection; Nobel 2017), black holes, cosmological expansion, time dilation (GPS satellites' clocks corrected for relativistic effects daily). Newton's law remains ACCURATE ENOUGH for most engineering + everyday uses.

FORMULA: F = G·m₁·m₂/r². (1) F = gravitational force (Newtons); (2) m₁, m₂ = masses (kg); (3) r = distance between centers (m); (4) G = UNIVERSAL GRAVITATIONAL CONSTANT = 6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg². PROPERTIES: (1) ALWAYS ATTRACTIVE (no repulsive gravity known, unlike EM force). (2) INVERSE-SQUARE law (F ∝ 1/r²) — identical mathematical form to Coulomb's electric force. (3) Acts over ANY DISTANCE (infinite range). (4) Independent of medium. (5) Mutual (Newton's 3rd law — Earth attracts Moon; Moon attracts Earth same magnitude opposite direction). APPLICATIONS: (1) PLANETARY MOTION — Kepler's 3 LAWS (1609, 1619) elegantly derived from Newton's law — (a) Law 1 (ellipse): planets orbit Sun in ellipses with Sun at one focus. (b) Law 2 (equal areas): line from Sun to planet sweeps equal areas in equal times (conservation of angular momentum). (c) Law 3 (harmonic): T² ∝ r³ (period squared proportional to semi-major axis cubed). (2) TIDES — Moon + Sun gravity causes tidal bulges; 2 high tides per day (Moon side + opposite side); SPRING TIDES (new + full moon, Sun + Moon aligned) + NEAP TIDES (quarter moons, 90°); impacts on coastal life, marine creatures, fisheries. (3) SATELLITE MOTION — artificial satellites orbit by centripetal gravity balance (gravity = mv²/r). LEO (altitude 200-2000 km, period 90-120 min); MEO (2,000-35,786 km; GPS ~20,200 km, 12 hr period); GEO / GEOSTATIONARY (35,786 km altitude, 24 hr period — 'sidereal day'; appears stationary over equator — used for communications, weather satellites); HEO (highly elliptical). (4) ESCAPE VELOCITY — v = √(2GM/R) = 11.2 km/s for Earth (to escape Earth's gravity). From Moon ~2.4 km/s. From Sun ~42 km/s at Earth distance. LIMITATIONS of Newton: fails at strong fields + near speed of light. REPLACED by EINSTEIN'S GENERAL RELATIVITY (1915) — gravity is CURVATURE OF SPACETIME by mass-energy; predicts gravitational lensing, gravitational waves (LIGO 2015 direct detection; Nobel 2017), black holes, cosmological expansion, time dilation (GPS satellites' clocks corrected for relativistic effects daily). Newton's law remains ACCURATE ENOUGH for most engineering + everyday uses.

cards.front:
Acceleration due to gravity (g) on Earth's surface is approximately:

(A) 3.7 m/s²
(B) 9.8 m/s² (average)
(C) 100 m/s²
(D) 1 m/s²
cards.back:
(B) 9.8 m/s² (average)

Gravitation & Fluids — ACCELERATION DUE TO GRAVITY (g) on Earth — the rate at which free-falling objects accelerate due to Earth's gravity. AVERAGE g ≈ 9.8 m/s² (or 9.81 m/s² approximate). STANDARD VALUE = 9.80665 m/s² (exactly, by SI convention). FROM NEWTON's LAW: g = GM/R² where M = Earth's mass (5.972 × 10²⁴ kg), R = Earth's radius (~6371 km). Calculation: 6.674e-11 × 5.972e24 / (6.371e6)² = 9.82 m/s². VARIES WITH LOCATION: (1) EQUATOR: 9.78 m/s² — LOWEST. Reasons: (a) Earth is OBLATE SPHEROID (bulges at equator due to rotation; radius 21 km more at equator than poles; greater r → smaller g; (b) centrifugal 'pseudo-force' due to Earth's rotation reduces effective gravity (~0.034 m/s²); (c) latitude effect. (2) POLES: 9.83 m/s² — HIGHEST; no centrifugal + closer to center. (3) ALTITUDE: g decreases with height (g' = g(1-2h/R) approximately for small h). Mt Everest (8848m): g ~9.77; ISS altitude (400 km): g ~8.7 m/s² (astronauts are in FREE FALL, not zero gravity — 'microgravity' more accurate). (4) DEEP WITHIN Earth: g decreases (only mass BELOW you contributes); at center g = 0 (all mass surrounds you, cancels out). (5) LOCAL anomalies — gravimetry used for MINERAL EXPLORATION (dense ore bodies increase local g; GRACE satellite mission). VALUES of g on OTHER PLANETS (Earth g = 9.8 is reference ≈ 1 g): (a) MERCURY 3.7 m/s² (~0.38 g); (b) VENUS 8.87 (~0.9 g); (c) MOON 1.62 (~0.16 g — why Apollo astronauts bounce); (d) MARS 3.71 (~0.38 g); (e) JUPITER 24.79 (~2.53 g — enormous); (f) SATURN 10.44 (~1.07 g); (g) URANUS 8.69 (~0.89 g); (h) NEPTUNE 11.15 (~1.14 g); (i) SUN 274 (~28 g — crushing; can't stand). EXPERIMENTS: (1) Galileo's LEANING TOWER OF PISA (legend, ~1590) — cannonballs of different mass fall in same time (independent of mass). Actually done by Stevin + Adrian 1586 Delft; Galileo with inclined planes. (2) Galileo's INCLINED PLANE — showed s ∝ t² for uniformly accelerated motion. (3) Apollo 15 (1971) on MOON — Commander Dave Scott dropped a hammer + a feather (in vacuum): both hit lunar surface at SAME TIME — Galileo vindicated. (4) FREE-FALL experiments: s = ½gt² (falling distance), v = gt (speed after time t), v² = 2gs. FORCES + EQUATIONS: Weight W = mg (force due to gravity on mass m at surface). Mass (invariant scalar) vs Weight (location-dependent vector force). Your mass is constant; your WEIGHT on the Moon is 1/6 of on Earth. varies 9.78 (equator) to 9.83 (poles) due to Earth's oblate shape + rotation; STANDARD g = 9.80665 m/s².

cards.front:
ESCAPE VELOCITY from the surface of EARTH is:

(A) 3 km/s
(B) 11.2 km/s
(C) 100 km/s
(D) 1 km/s
cards.back:
(B) 11.2 km/s

Gravitation & Fluids — ESCAPE VELOCITY (Ve) — minimum speed needed for an object (without propulsion) at a specified distance from a body to escape its gravitational pull completely + never return. For EARTH SURFACE: Ve = 11.186 km/s (~11.2 km/s = ~40,270 km/h). FORMULA: Ve = √(2GM/R) where G = grav constant, M = Earth's mass, R = Earth's radius. Equivalently, Ve = √2 × orbital velocity. DERIVATION: Kinetic energy ½mv² = Gravitational PE −GMm/R → v_min = √(2GM/R). VALUES from DIFFERENT BODIES: (a) MOON surface: 2.4 km/s (much lower → easy lunar ascent — LUNAR MODULE had small fuel); (b) MARS surface: 5.03 km/s; (c) JUPITER surface (no solid surface; from cloud tops): 59.5 km/s; (d) SATURN: 35.5 km/s; (e) SUN surface: 617.5 km/s. Earth-at-solar-distance from Sun: 42.1 km/s (to escape the Sun entirely from Earth's orbit — needed for Voyager + New Horizons). From NEUTRON STAR: up to 100,000 km/s (c/3). From BLACK HOLE event horizon: c (speed of light) — definition. PRACTICAL SIGNIFICANCE: (1) Rockets carry enough fuel to reach SPEEDS above Ve for interplanetary missions (Apollo, Voyager, Mars missions). (2) Orbital mechanics — Ve is upper bound; LOWER ORBITAL velocity (~7.8 km/s at LEO 200 km) needed for circular orbit (satellites). Going faster than orbital but less than Ve = elliptical orbit. (3) SATELLITE LAUNCH requires achieving orbital velocity (for LEO) or trans-lunar injection velocity (for Moon) or higher. (4) GRAVITY ASSIST / SLINGSHOT — spacecraft uses a planet's gravity to gain energy — e.g., Voyager 1+2 used Jupiter + Saturn gravity; Cassini used Venus-Venus-Earth-Jupiter swingbys. ORBITAL VELOCITY of Earth satellites: (a) ISS (400 km altitude): 7.66 km/s (circular orbit; period 90 min). (b) GPS (20,200 km): 3.87 km/s. (c) GEOSTATIONARY (35,786 km): 3.07 km/s, period 24 hr. (d) Moon (384,400 km): 1.02 km/s. ROCKETS in INDIA (ISRO): PSLV can deliver 1.75 tonne to 600 km SSO (orbital velocities achieved); GSLV Mk-II + III (LVM3) can deliver to GTO (geostationary transfer orbit); Chandrayaan-3 (2023) achieved lunar transfer (~11 km/s near Earth escape); Mars Orbiter Mission (2013) achieved HELIOCENTRIC orbit via 6 earth-orbit raising manoeuvres then hyperbolic trans-Mars trajectory. V₂ ROCKET (1944 Nazi Germany) — FIRST rocket to CROSS KÁRMÁN LINE (100 km, boundary of space); reached 1.6 km/s (sub-orbital). SOYUZ / FALCON 9 / SATURN V etc. designed for 7.8-11.2 km/s depending on destination. FIRST spacecraft to achieve solar-system escape: PIONEER 10 (launched 1972; last signal 2003). VOYAGER 1 left heliosphere 2012 (first to enter interstellar space). minimum speed to escape Earth's gravity without further propulsion; formula v = √(2GM/R); ~40,270 km/h.

cards.front:
KEPLER's THIRD LAW of planetary motion states that:

(A) All orbits are circles
(B) T² ∝ r³
(C) T ∝ r²
(D) Orbits never change
cards.back:
(B) T² ∝ r³

Gravitation & Fluids — KEPLER's LAWS of PLANETARY MOTION — 3 empirical laws formulated by JOHANNES KEPLER (1571-1630, German astronomer + mathematician) based on TYCHO BRAHE's precise naked-eye observations (1546-1601). Kepler worked for decades to deduce them. (1) FIRST LAW (Law of Ellipses, 1609) — planets move in ELLIPTICAL ORBITS with the SUN at one FOCUS (not center). Broke the 2000-year circular-orbit dogma of Aristotle + Ptolemy. (2) SECOND LAW (Law of Equal Areas, 1609) — line joining planet to Sun SWEEPS EQUAL AREAS in EQUAL TIMES. Consequence: planets move FASTER at PERIHELION (closest to Sun) + SLOWER at APHELION. Fundamental: conservation of angular momentum L = mvr (constant). (3) THIRD LAW (Harmonic Law, 1619) — T² = (4π²/GM) × a³; commonly T² ∝ a³ where T = orbital period + a = semi-major axis. FOR Earth, T = 1 year, a = 1 AU = 1.496 × 10⁸ km. For ANY planet, T² (in years²) = a³ (in AU³). DERIVATION: from Newton's gravitation + centripetal force. MASS of central body M = 4π²a³/(GT²) — this lets ASTRONOMERS measure Earth's mass, Sun's mass, stars' masses! Examples: Earth T = 1 yr, a = 1 AU → T² = 1, a³ = 1 ✓. Mars: T = 1.88 yr, a = 1.524 AU → T² = 3.53, a³ = 3.54 ✓. Jupiter: T = 11.86 yr, a = 5.20 AU → T² = 140.7, a³ = 140.6 ✓. NEPTUNE: T = 164.8 yr, a = 30.07 AU → T² = 27,170, a³ = 27,200 ✓. NEWTON (1687) EXPLAINED Kepler's laws mathematically using his inverse-square gravitation law. SOLAR SYSTEM structure: (A) ROCKY planets: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars (inside Main Asteroid Belt between Mars + Jupiter). (B) GAS GIANTS: Jupiter, Saturn (hydrogen + helium). (C) ICE GIANTS: Uranus, Neptune (water + ammonia + methane ices). (D) DWARF PLANETS: Pluto (reclassified 2006 by IAU; Kuiper Belt object), Eris, Haumea, Makemake, Ceres (asteroid belt). (E) KUIPER BELT (30-50 AU, icy bodies) + OORT CLOUD (1-100k AU; source of long-period comets). PLANET LINE-UP (by distance from Sun, 'My Very Educated Mother Just Served Us Noodles'): MERCURY (0.4 AU), VENUS (0.7), EARTH (1), MARS (1.5), JUPITER (5.2), SATURN (9.5), URANUS (19.2), NEPTUNE (30.1). (Pluto used to be 9th — reclassified 2006 as 'dwarf planet' by IAU at Prague because it hadn't 'cleared its orbital neighborhood'.) EXOPLANET discoveries explosion since 1995 (51 Pegasi b, Nobel 2019 to Mayor + Queloz) — 5,700+ confirmed exoplanets known (Dec 2024); Kepler + TESS space missions + JWST characterising atmospheres. 'GOLDILOCKS ZONE' / habitable zone around stars where liquid water possible. square of orbital period is proportional to cube of semi-major axis (orbital radius); enables mass-distance determination in celestial mechanics.

cards.front:
A GEOSTATIONARY SATELLITE orbits at approximately what altitude above Earth's equator?

(A) 400 km (LEO)
(B) 35,786 km
(C) 1,000,000 km
(D) 100 km
cards.back:
(B) 35,786 km

Gravitation & Fluids — GEOSTATIONARY ORBIT (GEO) — circular orbit at ~35,786 KM ALTITUDE (42,164 km from Earth's center) with period equal to Earth's SIDEREAL DAY (23 hours 56 minutes 4 seconds). Satellite moves east at same angular speed as Earth → appears STATIONARY from ground. Discovered as theoretical concept by Herman Potočnik (1929) + popularised by ARTHUR C. CLARKE (1945 WIRELESS WORLD article 'Extra-Terrestrial Relays') — hence 'CLARKE ORBIT' / 'CLARKE BELT'. FIRST geostationary satellite: SYNCOM 3 (NASA, 1964). USES: (1) COMMUNICATION — 3 GEO satellites at 120° apart cover entire Earth (near equator); fixed dishes + no tracking needed (consumer DTH like Tata Sky + Airtel Xstream + Dish TV in India). (2) WEATHER — INSAT series (India), GOES (USA), Meteosat (Europe). (3) BROADCASTING — TV, radio. (4) MILITARY communications. ~500+ satellites in GEO currently. GEO congestion is growing — INTERNATIONAL TELECOMMUNICATION UNION (ITU) allocates slots. INDIA's GEO satellites: (a) APPLE (1981 — first Indian 3-axis stabilized; launched by Ariane-1). (b) INSAT series — 1A, 1B, 1C, 1D (communications + weather, 1980s-90s). (c) INSAT-3 + INSAT-4 series (2000s-10s — COMMUNICATION + Ku band). (d) GSAT series (GSAT-1 to GSAT-30+; heavy geo-communication, internet, broadcast, ISRO-Defence). (e) CARTOSAT (Earth observation in SSO, not GEO). OTHER TYPES of ORBIT: (1) LOW EARTH ORBIT (LEO) — 200-2,000 km altitude; period 90-120 min. Examples: ISS (400 km), HUBBLE (540 km, retired 2025?), Starlink constellation (~550 km), OneWeb (1,200 km); Earth observation, space stations, spy satellites. (2) MEDIUM EARTH ORBIT (MEO) — 2,000-35,786 km. Examples: GPS (20,200 km, 12 hr), Galileo, GLONASS, NavIC (partially MEO, partially GSO). (3) GEOSTATIONARY (GEO) — 35,786 km, 24 hr, equatorial, 0° inclination. (4) GEOSYNCHRONOUS (GSO) — same period as Earth but inclined orbit (not above equator); appears as FIGURE-8 in sky (analemma). (5) POLAR ORBIT — ~90° inclination; each orbit covers different longitude as Earth rotates — for Earth observation, weather, remote sensing; e.g., Landsat, NOAA, INSAT-3D, Cartosat. (6) SUN-SYNCHRONOUS ORBIT (SSO) — polar orbit synchronized with sun; passes each latitude at same LOCAL time — constant illumination angle for Earth imaging; altitude 600-800 km. (7) HIGHLY ELLIPTICAL ORBIT (HEO) — Molniya (Russia — 12 hr, good for polar high-latitude coverage), Tundra (24 hr). (8) MOON ORBIT: ~384,400 km; 27.3-day period. (9) LAGRANGE POINTS (L1-L5) — balance points in 2-body system. L1 Earth-Sun (1.5M km — SOHO, DSCOVR, Aditya-L1); L2 Earth-Sun (opposite — JWST, Gaia, Herschel). KESSLER SYNDROME — space debris cascading collisions; concern for future of LEO. period 24 hours matching Earth's rotation; appears STATIONARY over fixed equatorial point; ideal for communication + broadcast.

(7) HIGHLY ELLIPTICAL ORBIT (HEO) — Molniya (Russia — 12 hr, good for polar high-latitude coverage), Tundra (24 hr). (8) MOON ORBIT: ~384,400 km; 27.3-day period. (9) LAGRANGE POINTS (L1-L5) — balance points in 2-body system. L1 Earth-Sun (1.5M km — SOHO, DSCOVR, Aditya-L1); L2 Earth-Sun (opposite — JWST, Gaia, Herschel). KESSLER SYNDROME — space debris cascading collisions; concern for future of LEO. period 24 hours matching Earth's rotation; appears STATIONARY over fixed equatorial point; ideal for communication + broadcast.

cards.front:
Why do ASTRONAUTS appear WEIGHTLESS on the International Space Station?

(A) There is no gravity in space
(B) They are in CONTINUOUS FREE-FALL around Earth
(C) Air pressure lifts them
(D) Magnets in suit
cards.back:
(B) They are in CONTINUOUS FREE-FALL around Earth

Gravitation & Fluids — MICROGRAVITY on ISS — astronauts + ISS are in CONSTANT FREE-FALL around Earth. Gravity at ISS altitude (~400 km) is still ~8.7 m/s² (only 11% less than surface) — NOT zero. HOW: ISS orbits at 7.66 km/s tangentially; Earth's gravity pulls it downward, but its forward speed makes it 'miss' Earth — it keeps falling AROUND Earth (elliptical/circular orbit). INSIDE the ISS, both structure + astronauts accelerate at SAME RATE toward Earth (~8.7 m/s²) → no relative acceleration → astronauts FLOAT relative to ISS → 'weightlessness'. EQUIVALENCE PRINCIPLE (Einstein's insight): free-fall is indistinguishable from being in zero gravity (locally). BASIS for General Relativity 1915. DEMONSTRATED: (1) Elevator thought experiment — if cable cuts, you float inside falling elevator. (2) VOMIT COMET / Reduced Gravity Aircraft — KC-135 / A300 'Zero-G' planes fly parabolic trajectories giving ~25 seconds of weightlessness; used for astronaut training + microgravity research + filming (Apollo 13 movie 1995 filmed aboard KC-135). MICROGRAVITY RESEARCH: (1) PROTEIN CRYSTALS — better crystallization in microgravity → drug design (insulin, anti-cancer, HIV). (2) COMBUSTION — flames behave differently (spherical, cooler, no convection). (3) MATERIAL SCIENCE — alloys, ceramics form without gravity-induced separation. (4) FLUID DYNAMICS — surface tension dominates; droplets + bubbles form unusual shapes. (5) BIOLOGY — cell growth differs (bone loss studies; muscle atrophy — astronauts lose ~2% bone + muscle mass per month, exercise 2 hrs/day to combat). (6) PLANT GROWTH — direction without gravity; photosynthesis studies. (7) HUMAN PHYSIOLOGY — fluids shift to upper body (puffy faces), vision changes (Space-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome), sleep disruption. ISS: International Space Station, est. 1998 (first module Zarya); continuously inhabited since 2000. 16-nation collab led by NASA + Roscosmos + ESA + JAXA + CSA. 73m × 109m × 20m. 420 tonnes. Orbits every 92.68 min → 15.54 orbits/day. India has sent 1 astronaut (Rakesh Sharma, 1984, Soyuz T-11 — didn't visit ISS since ISS hadn't existed; visited Salyut 7). Sunita Williams (Indian-American, NASA) — 7 spacewalks; 3 ISS missions (2006-07, 2012, 2024-25 Boeing Starliner Crew Flight Test — stranded + returned via SpaceX Crew 9 Mar 2025). Rakesh Sharma STILL the only Indian to space via an Indian-selected path (Gaganyaan coming 2025-26 for Indian rocket). CHANDRAYAAN-3 (2023) simulated microgravity on Moon (1/6 g) — Pragyan rover + Vikram lander. ISS RETIRE planned ~2030; CHINESE TIANGONG station operational since 2021 + INDIA'S BHARATIYA ANTARIKSH STATION (BAS, 5-module) targeted 2035. gravity pulls ISS + astronauts equally, so they float inside; this is 'MICROGRAVITY', not zero-gravity.

cards.front:
GRAVITATIONAL WAVES were FIRST directly detected on 14 September 2015 by:

(A) ISRO
(B) LIGO
(C) Hubble Space Telescope
(D) James Webb Telescope
cards.back:
(B) LIGO

Gravitation & Fluids — GRAVITATIONAL WAVES (GW) — RIPPLES in SPACETIME caused by accelerating massive objects (like merging black holes + neutron stars). Predicted by EINSTEIN's GENERAL RELATIVITY (1916). Travel at SPEED OF LIGHT. Incredibly WEAK — detection required century of tech development. FIRST DIRECT DETECTION: 14 SEPTEMBER 2015 at 5:51 AM UTC by LIGO (Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory) — dual detectors at Hanford, Washington + Livingston, Louisiana. Signal named 'GW150914'. Source: merger of 2 BLACK HOLES (~29 + 36 solar masses → 62 solar mass BH, 3 solar masses converted to GW energy) about 1.3 BILLION light-years away. Merger event lasted ~0.2 second in Earth's detectors; peak amplitude ~10⁻²¹ (spacetime stretched/compressed by 1/1000 proton diameter over 4 km arm). Announced 11 FEB 2016 — breakthrough of the century. NOBEL PHYSICS 2017 to RAINER WEISS + KIP THORNE + BARRY BARISH (pioneers of LIGO). LIGO TECHNOLOGY: (1) Two 4-km-long L-shaped arms; (2) Laser interferometer — splits laser, reflects off mirrors at end of each arm, recombines; gravitational wave changes arm length differentially → interference pattern shifts. (3) DETECTOR SENSITIVITY: can measure length changes of 10⁻¹⁹ m (1/1000th of proton diameter!); uses sophisticated vibration isolation, vacuum, quantum-squeezed light. (4) COINCIDENCE detection (2 detectors, 3,000 km apart) — essential to rule out local noise. SUBSEQUENT DETECTIONS: Over 90 GW events catalogued (O1 + O2 + O3 + O4 observing runs). Mergers of BH-BH, NS-NS, BH-NS. (a) GW170817 (17 Aug 2017) — BINARY NEUTRON STAR merger; first GW event with ELECTROMAGNETIC counterpart (gamma-ray burst + kilonova seen across spectrum) — proof of 'MULTI-MESSENGER ASTRONOMY'. Nobel groundwork. (b) GW190521 — heaviest known BH merger (142 solar mass intermediate BH). NETWORK: LIGO (USA), VIRGO (Italy, 3 km), KAGRA (Japan), LIGO-INDIA (UNDER CONSTRUCTION at HINGOLI, MAHARASHTRA — 4km, joint IndIGO + LIGO Caltech — Cabinet approved 2023 ₹2,600 cr, operational target 2030). LIGO-INDIA will significantly improve source localization (triangulation from 4 detectors). FUTURE: LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna, ESA+NASA, launch 2035) — space-based LIGO; 3 spacecraft separated 2.5M km forming equilateral triangle; sensitive to LOW-frequency GW from supermassive BH mergers + galactic binary stars. EINSTEIN TELESCOPE (Europe underground, planned 2035) + COSMIC EXPLORER (USA, 40-km arms, 2040). PULSAR TIMING ARRAYS (NANOGrav, 2023 detected stochastic GW background from supermassive BH mergers in galaxy cores). Gravitational-wave astronomy is a NEW TELESCOPE on universe — seeing invisible events like BH mergers. CP Ramanujan, Sanjeev Dhurandhar (IUCAA Pune, India), Sanjeev Krishnagiri, Tarun Souradeep, Bala Iyer — Indian contributors. Hanford + Livingston detectors; from binary black hole merger 1.3 BILLION years ago; Nobel Physics 2017; Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory, USA.

cards.front:
A BLACK HOLE is a region of space where:

(A) Light has no energy
(B) GRAVITY is so strong that NOTHING, not even LIGHT, can escape once past the 'EVENT HORIZON'; formed by collapse of massive stars; first image captured Apr 2019 (M87*) by EHT
(C) There is no matter
(D) Temperature drops to zero
cards.back:
(B) GRAVITY is so strong that NOTHING, not even LIGHT, can escape once past the 'EVENT HORIZON'; formed by collapse of massive stars; first image captured Apr 2019 (M87*) by EHT

Gravitation & Fluids — BLACK HOLE — region of space where gravity is SO STRONG that escape velocity exceeds speed of light → NOTHING (not even light or information) can escape once past the EVENT HORIZON (boundary of no return). Predicted by Schwarzschild from Einstein's GR (1916) within weeks of its publication. NAME coined 1967 by John Archibald Wheeler. FORMATION: (1) STELLAR collapse — massive star (>~20 solar masses) runs out of fuel, core collapses; outer layers blow off in SUPERNOVA; remnant core >3 solar masses CANNOT be stabilized by neutron degeneracy → collapses indefinitely to SINGULARITY (point of infinite density). (2) PRIMORDIAL BHs — hypothetical, from density fluctuations in very early universe. (3) SUPERMASSIVE BHs (SMBH) — at centres of galaxies; millions to billions of solar masses. Formation still debated; possibly direct collapse of massive gas clouds or hierarchical mergers. PARTS: (1) SINGULARITY — central point of infinite density + zero volume. (2) EVENT HORIZON — boundary; Schwarzschild radius Rs = 2GM/c² (for non-rotating BH). For Sun: 3 km. For Earth: 9 mm. For 4 million solar-mass SMBH Sagittarius A*: 12 million km. (3) ACCRETION DISK — in-falling matter heats to millions of K, emits X-rays. (4) PHOTON SPHERE — where photons can orbit. (5) ERGOSPHERE (rotating Kerr BH only) — frame-dragging region. TYPES: (1) Stellar BH (5-100 solar masses, from star deaths). (2) Intermediate BH (100-1000 solar mass; recently confirmed). (3) Supermassive BH (millions-billions). (4) Possibly primordial micro-BHs (unconfirmed). DISCOVERY milestones: (1) CYGNUS X-1 (1964) — first strong stellar BH candidate via X-ray; confirmed 1990s. (2) SAGITTARIUS A* — SMBH at Milky Way center; 4.1 million solar masses; 26,000 LY away; orbits of stars like S2 (16 yr orbit) prove its existence. ANDREA GHEZ + REINHARD GENZEL + ROGER PENROSE got 2020 Nobel Physics for Sgr A*. (3) GRAVITATIONAL WAVE DETECTION (LIGO 2015) — indirect BH confirmation via mergers. (4) FIRST IMAGE of BH: 10 APRIL 2019 — EVENT HORIZON TELESCOPE collaboration imaged M87* (supermassive BH at centre of Messier 87 galaxy, 55 million LY away; 6.5 billion solar masses); iconic orange-ring image. KATIE BOUMAN (MIT) algorithm enabled reconstruction. (5) 2022 — EHT imaged SAGITTARIUS A* (our galaxy's). (6) JWST since 2022 finding SMBHs even at cosmic dawn (~300 Myr post-Big Bang) — challenging formation models. HAWKING RADIATION (Stephen Hawking 1974) — quantum effect near horizon causes BH to SLOWLY EVAPORATE over cosmic timescales; smaller BHs evaporate faster. NOT yet observed but fundamental prediction. INFORMATION PARADOX — quantum information seemingly destroyed → violation of unitarity. Active research (holography, AdS/CFT, firewalls). 'NO HAIR THEOREM' — BH defined by only 3 parameters: Mass, Charge, Angular Momentum.

cards.front:
WEIGHT of a person on the MOON compared to EARTH is approximately:

(A) Same
(B) 1/6th
(C) Twice
(D) Zero
cards.back:
(B) 1/6th

Gravitation & Fluids — WEIGHT of PERSON on MOON = 1/6th of Earth weight (approximately; actually 16.5%). MOON's GRAVITY = 1.62 m/s² (compared to Earth's 9.8 m/s²). Reason: Moon is much less massive (7.3 × 10²² kg vs Earth's 5.97 × 10²⁴ kg; ratio 1/81) + slightly smaller (3,474 km diameter vs Earth's 12,742 km). By g = GM/R²: Moon g = 6.674e-11 × 7.3e22 / (1737000)² = 1.62 m/s². MASS vs WEIGHT: (1) MASS — measure of AMOUNT of matter; INVARIANT (kg); same anywhere in universe. (2) WEIGHT — FORCE due to gravity = m × g; LOCATION-dependent (N or kgf); varies with g. EXAMPLES: A 60-kg person (Earth) — weighs ~590 N on Earth (60×9.8); ~97 N on Moon (60×1.62); ~223 N on Mars (60×3.71); ~221 N on Mercury (60×3.7); ~1487 N on Jupiter (60×24.79 — crushing 2.5× Earth weight!); mass remains 60 kg everywhere. WEIGHT on OTHER PLANETS (for 60 kg Earth person): Moon 10 kgf (~97 N); Mars 22.8 kgf (~223 N); Mercury + Mars similar; Venus ~54 kgf (~533 N, 90% of Earth); Saturn 64 kgf (1.07 g); Jupiter 152 kgf (2.53 g); Uranus 53 kgf (0.89 g); Neptune 68 kgf (1.14 g); Sun 1680 kgf (28 g — would crush human; surface equivalent 280x earth gravity). MOON's special features due to lower gravity: (a) Apollo astronauts could 'bounce-walk' (low-g hopping gait used less energy than walking). (b) Jump heights 6× higher (Alan Shepard's 1971 6-iron golf shot on Apollo 14 travelled much farther). (c) Rockets ascending from Moon need much less fuel (lunar module used ~2,500 kg for Moon-orbit vs Saturn V's 2.3 million kg for Earth launch). (d) Escape velocity 2.4 km/s (vs Earth's 11.2). PHYSICAL EFFECTS of reduced gravity on humans: (1) Bone density loss 1-2% per month — astronauts need calcium + vitamin D + exercise; some permanent loss even after return. (2) Muscle atrophy — 2 hours of exercise per day on ISS to combat. (3) Cardiovascular deconditioning — fluid shifts upward + heart pumps less (LAB RAT). (4) Vestibular disorientation — balance-eye-ear confusion (motion sickness). (5) Vision changes. (6) Immune system disturbance. LONG-DURATION Mars missions (~2.5 years round trip) major health challenge. Apollo 11 (20 July 1969) LANDED on Moon — Neil Armstrong + Buzz Aldrin walked; Michael Collins orbited. 6 manned lunar landings (1969-72, Apollo 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, 17 — 12 astronauts walked on Moon). ARTEMIS program (NASA + ESA + JAXA + CSA + CSA + ISRO via Artemis Accords) — to return humans to Moon + establish sustainable presence; Artemis I (2022 uncrewed), II (2026 crewed flyby), III (2027+ crewed landing). Lunar Gateway station planned. Indian Gaganyaan post-LEO extension to Moon on slow timeline. Moon's gravity (1.62 m/s²) is ~16.5% of Earth's (9.8 m/s²); mass is invariant, weight is location-dependent.

cards.front:
EINSTEIN's GENERAL RELATIVITY (1915) reinterprets GRAVITY as:

(A) An electromagnetic effect
(B) CURVATURE OF SPACETIME by mass-energy
(C) A quantum effect only
(D) Friction between objects
cards.back:
(B) CURVATURE OF SPACETIME by mass-energy

Gravitation & Fluids — GENERAL RELATIVITY (GR) — ALBERT EINSTEIN's masterpiece theory of gravity; published 1915 (presented Nov 25, 1915 at Prussian Academy); 'the most beautiful theory in physics'. KEY IDEA: GRAVITY is NOT a force (per Newton) but the CURVATURE of 4-D SPACETIME caused by MASS-ENERGY. FAMOUS JOHN WHEELER QUOTE: 'Matter tells spacetime how to curve; spacetime tells matter how to move.' BASED on 2 PRINCIPLES: (1) PRINCIPLE OF RELATIVITY — laws of physics are same in all reference frames (from SR 1905). (2) EQUIVALENCE PRINCIPLE — gravitational + inertial mass are identical; observer in free-fall cannot distinguish from floating in zero gravity. Thought experiment: falling person in elevator vs. drifting in space — locally same. FIELD EQUATIONS: Gμν = 8πG/c⁴ × Tμν. Left side (Gμν) = Einstein tensor (curvature of spacetime); right side (Tμν) = stress-energy tensor (matter + energy distribution). 10 coupled non-linear PDEs. PREDICTIONS + VERIFICATIONS: (1) PERIHELION ADVANCE of MERCURY — 43 arcsec/century unexplained by Newton; GR gave EXACT match (announced 1915 before general observation). (2) LIGHT BENDING — light path curves near massive objects; PREDICTION (1.75 arcsec for Sun's edge). VERIFIED by ARTHUR EDDINGTON at SOLAR ECLIPSE 1919 (Principe Island + Sobral Brazil) — HEADLINES ACROSS WORLD; made Einstein a global celebrity. Also 'GRAVITATIONAL LENSING' — now a routine astronomy tool (Einstein rings, dark matter mapping, exoplanet detection via microlensing). (3) GRAVITATIONAL TIME DILATION — clocks tick SLOWER in stronger gravity. Confirmed in atomic clocks (Hafele-Keating 1971 atomic clock flights); CRUCIAL for GPS (satellite clocks tick FASTER by ~38 microseconds/day than ground — GPS software corrects; without correction, navigation errors 10 km/day). 'Biggest blunder' Einstein's cosmological constant (Λ) — introduced to give static universe, removed after expansion found; NOW REINSTATED as dark energy driving accelerating expansion (Nobel 2011 to Perlmutter + Schmidt + Riess). (7) FRAME DRAGGING — rotating masses drag spacetime; Gravity Probe B (NASA 2004-11) confirmed. LIMITATIONS: doesn't work at QUANTUM scales; UNIFICATION with quantum mechanics = HOLY GRAIL of physics (string theory, loop quantum gravity, causal dynamical triangulation — competing approaches; none complete). Would reconcile gravity with other 3 fundamental forces (electromagnetic + strong + weak nuclear). EINSTEIN never got Nobel for GR (got 1921 Nobel for photoelectric effect + QM foundation). GR is a pillar of modern cosmology + astrophysics — tested to extreme precision.

cards.front:
Newton's UNIVERSAL law of gravitation says the force between two masses is:

(A) Inversely proportional to product of masses
(B) Proportional to (m₁m₂) / r² between them
(C) Directly proportional to distance r
(D) Independent of the distance entirely
cards.back:
(B) Proportional to (m₁m₂) / r² between them

Gravitation & Fluids — Newton's universal gravitation (1687, Principia): F = G(m₁m₂)/r². Force is DIRECTLY proportional to product of masses, INVERSELY proportional to SQUARE of distance. G = 6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg² (Universal Gravitational Constant — measured by Cavendish, 1798, with torsion balance). For two 1-kg masses at 1 m: F = 6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N (very tiny). Inverse-square law also for: electric force (Coulomb), light intensity, sound intensity. Distractor 1 — confused direct/inverse. Distractor 3 — wrong dependence on r.

(B) 11.2 km/s (~40,300 km/h)
(C) 300 km/h, very moderate speed
(D) Speed of light, the universal limit
cards.back:
(B) 11.2 km/s (~40,300 km/h)

Gravitation & Fluids — Escape velocity v_esc = √(2gR) = √(2 × 9.8 × 6.4 × 10⁶) ≈ 11.2 km/s = ~40,300 km/h. Speed needed to escape Earth's gravity without further propulsion (ignoring air drag). Beyond this, object follows hyperbolic trajectory. Moon escape velocity = 2.4 km/s; Sun = 618 km/s; Black hole = c (speed of light) at event horizon. Independent of object's mass. ORBITAL velocity at surface ≈ 7.9 km/s (less than escape; circular orbit). Rockets must reach escape velocity to leave Earth.

cards.front:
An astronaut feels WEIGHTLESS in orbit because:

(A) Gravity is zero in space at orbit
(B) He / she + the spacecraft are in free fall
(C) Air pressure is zero in vacuum of space
(D) Centrifugal force balances gravity
cards.back:
(B) He / she + the spacecraft are in free fall

Gravitation & Fluids — Common misconception — astronauts feel weightless NOT because there's no gravity (gravity is still ~89% of surface value at ISS altitude of 400 km). They are in CONTINUOUS FREE FALL toward Earth — but their horizontal velocity is so high they 'miss' the Earth, falling around it. Both spacecraft + astronaut accelerate at the same rate → no relative acceleration → feels like zero weight. Same effect: in a free-falling elevator, you'd feel weightless. Distractor 1 — wrong. Distractor 4 — partly true in rotating frame (centrifugal), but free-fall description is more fundamental.

cards.front:
WEIGHT differs from MASS in that:

(A) Mass changes with location, weight is constant
(B) Weight changes with location, mass is constant
(C) Both stay constant always everywhere
(D) Mass is measured in newtons (force unit)
cards.back:
(B) Weight changes with location, mass is constant

Gravitation & Fluids — MASS = amount of matter (kg). Constant everywhere (unless extreme — Einstein's relativity). WEIGHT = gravitational force on mass (N): W = mg. Changes with location: surface of Earth (g ≈ 9.8 m/s²) → 60-kg person weighs ~588 N. Surface of Moon (g ≈ 1.62) → same person ~98 N (1/6th). In FREE FALL or orbit (effective g = 0) → weightless. Mass is INERTIAL property; weight is gravitational FORCE. Common usage 'I weigh 60 kg' really means 'mass 60 kg'.

cards.front:
If Earth were to SHRINK to half its present radius (without mass change), the value of g at its surface would:

(A) Halve, become 4.9 m/s² instead
(B) Quadruple (4×), become ~39.2 m/s²
(C) Double, become 19.6 m/s² instead
(D) Stay the same at 9.8 m/s² always
cards.back:
(B) Quadruple (4×), become ~39.2 m/s²

Gravitation & Fluids — g = GM/R². Mass M unchanged; radius R → R/2 means R² → R²/4. So g → 4g = 39.2 m/s². Inverse-square dependence on R. Conversely, if Earth's radius doubled (M same), g would become g/4. (If mass also changed proportionally to volume, the answer differs — but the question specifies mass unchanged.)

cards.front:
Kepler's THIRD LAW states that the square of the orbital period is proportional to:

(A) Cube of the semi-major axis (T² ∝ a³)
(B) Square of the semi-major axis (T² ∝ a²)
(C) First power of orbit radius (T² ∝ a)
(D) Mass of the orbiting body itself
cards.back:
(A) Cube of the semi-major axis (T² ∝ a³)

Gravitation & Fluids — Kepler's 3 LAWS of planetary motion: 1st (Orbit Law) — planets move in ELLIPSES with Sun at one focus. 2nd (Area Law) — line from sun to planet sweeps equal areas in equal times (planet faster when closer). 3rd (Period Law) — T² ∝ a³ (where a = semi-major axis). For our solar system, Earth: T = 1 yr, a = 1 AU. Mars: T ≈ 1.88 yr, a ≈ 1.52 AU; check: 1.88² ≈ 3.53; 1.52³ ≈ 3.51 ✓. Newton derived Kepler's laws from gravitation. Distractor 4 — period independent of orbiting body's mass (Galileo's principle for free fall extended to gravity).

cards.front:
KEPLER'S THIRD LAW states T² ∝ ?, where T is the orbital period:

(A) a (semi-major axis)
(B) a³
(C) a²
(D) 1/a
cards.back:
(B) a³

Gravitation & Fluids — Kepler's 3rd law: T² = (4π²/GM) × a³ → T² ∝ a³. Hence inner planets (smaller a) have much shorter years; outer planets take far longer (Neptune: 165 years). cube of semi-major axis.

cards.front:
PRESSURE is defined as:

(A) Mass times acceleration (F=ma)
(B) Force per unit area (F/A)
(C) Energy per unit time (work rate)
(D) Mass per unit volume (density)
cards.back:
(B) Force per unit area (F/A)

Why heavy trucks have wide tires: distribute weight over large area → less pressure on road. Distractor 1 = Newton's 2nd law. Distractor 3 = power. Distractor 4 = density.

(A) 10 kPa (much lower value)
(B) 101 kPa (1 atm = 760 mm Hg)
(C) 10,000 kPa (much higher value)
(D) Zero Pa (vacuum at sea level)
cards.back:
(B) 101 kPa (1 atm = 760 mm Hg)

cards.front:
ARCHIMEDES' PRINCIPLE states that:

(A) Heavy objects always sink in liquid
(B) Buoyant force = weight of displaced fluid
(C) Pressure rises with depth always
(D) Liquids exert force in all directions
cards.back:
(B) Buoyant force = weight of displaced fluid

Gravitation & Fluids — ARCHIMEDES' principle: any object IMMERSED in fluid experiences UPWARD BUOYANT force = weight of fluid DISPLACED. Discovered by Archimedes in his bath (~250 BCE — he reportedly ran naked through Syracuse shouting 'EUREKA!'). Used to test if king's crown was pure gold (gold of given mass displaces less water than alloyed gold). FLOATING — buoyant force ≥ weight; SINKING — buoyant force < weight. Density of object < fluid density → floats. Steel ships float because hollow shape displaces water > ship's weight.

cards.front:
PASCAL's LAW states that:

(A) Heavier fluids exert more pressure than lighter ones at all depths
(B) Pressure applied to enclosed fluid is transmitted equally everywhere
(C) Liquids cannot be compressed at all under any condition
(D) Hot fluids expand into cooler ones over time slowly
cards.back:
(B) Pressure applied to enclosed fluid is transmitted equally everywhere

Gravitation & Fluids — PASCAL's LAW (Blaise Pascal, ~1646): pressure applied to enclosed fluid is transmitted UNDIMINISHED in ALL DIRECTIONS, equally to all parts of the fluid + walls. APPLICATIONS: HYDRAULIC SYSTEMS — small force on small piston → large force on big piston (mechanical advantage = ratio of areas). Used in: hydraulic brakes (cars), hydraulic jacks (lifting cars), hydraulic press, JCB / excavator arms, hydraulic lifts. Force out = (Area out / Area in) × Force in.

Why is it EASIER TO SWIM in SEA WATER than in fresh water?

(A) Sea is calmer than rivers normally
(B) Sea water is denser → more buoyancy
(C) Sea water has currents to help swim
(D) Sea is shallow at most coastal areas
cards.back:
(B) Sea water is denser → more buoyancy

Also: hot air balloons + ships work on similar principle (less dense than surrounding fluid → float).

cards.front:
ICE FLOATS on water because:

(A) Ice is colder than water (lower temp)
(B) Ice is less dense than liquid water
(C) Ice is solid (denser than liquid usually)
(D) Air bubbles are inside the ice always
cards.back:
(B) Ice is less dense than liquid water

Gravitation & Fluids — ICE density = 0.917 g/cm³; LIQUID WATER density = 1.000 g/cm³. UNUSUAL — water EXPANDS when freezing (most substances contract). Hydrogen bonding creates open hexagonal lattice in ice → less dense. So ice floats with ~10% above + 90% below water. CRITICAL for life: ice forms on top of lakes/rivers, insulating water below → fish + aquatic life survive winter. Without this property, water bodies would freeze from bottom up + kill marine life. ANOMALOUS EXPANSION OF WATER — water is densest at 4°C (not 0°C); above + below 4°C it's less dense.

cards.front:
Pressure of a fluid at depth h is given by formula:

(A) P = h × A (height times area)
(B) P = ρgh (density × g × depth)
(C) P = m × g (just weight only) here
(D) P = F × t (force × time) wrongly
cards.back:
(B) P = ρgh (density × g × depth)

ALSO must add atmospheric pressure if open to air: P_total = P_atm + ρgh. WHY a swimmer's ear hurts at deep end: pressure increases with depth. Each ~10 m of water adds ~1 atm of pressure. (A) A fuel
(B) A coolant / moderator of temperature swings
(C) An electrical insulator

cards.front:
The temperature at which the readings of the Celsius and Fahrenheit scales coincide is:

(A) 0°
(B) −40°
(C) 100°

cards.back:
(B) −40°

cards.back:
(B) Latent heat

cards.front:
Consider the following statements. 1. The FIRST law of thermodynamics is the principle of conservation of energy: ΔU = Q − W. 2. The SECOND law introduces the concept of entropy and states heat cannot spontaneously flow from cold to hot. 3. The THIRD law says the entropy of a perfect crystal at absolute zero is zero. 4. The ZEROTH law states that if two systems are each in thermal equilibrium with a third, they are in equilibrium with each other. Which are correct?

(A) 1 and 2 only
(B) 1, 2 and 4 only
(C) 1, 2, 3 and 4
(D) 2, 3 and 4 only
cards.back:
(C) 1, 2, 3 and 4

Heat & Thermodynamics — All four laws stated correctly. The Zeroth law (named after First/Second were already established) grounds the concept of temperature. Second law drives arrow of time and Carnot cycle efficiency limit.

cards.front:
A metal rod of length 100 cm at 20 °C is heated to 120 °C. The linear expansion coefficient is 1.2 × 10⁻⁵ /°C. Its new length is:

(A) 100.012 cm
(B) 100.12 cm
(C) 101.2 cm
(D) 100.0012 cm
cards.back:
(B) 100.12 cm

Heat & Thermodynamics — ΔL = L₀ × α × ΔT = 100 × 1.2×10⁻⁵ × (120 − 20) = 100 × 1.2×10⁻⁵ × 100 = 0.12 cm. New length = 100.12 cm.

cards.front:
HEAT transfer by the movement of molecules in a FLUID (liquid or gas) is called:

(A) Conduction
(B) CONVECTION
(C) Radiation
(D) Reflection
cards.back:
(B) CONVECTION

Heat & Thermodynamics — THREE MODES of HEAT TRANSFER: (1) CONDUCTION — heat flows through direct molecular contact in a SOLID (or between touching objects); hot particles vibrate faster → transfer energy to adjacent particles. Good conductors: metals (Cu, Ag, Al — sea of free electrons), diamond. Poor conductors (insulators): wood, plastic, air, wool, silica aerogel. (2) CONVECTION — in FLUIDS (liquids + gases): heated fluid EXPANDS, becomes LESS DENSE, RISES; cooler fluid sinks. Natural convection — no pump (sea breezes, hot air balloons, boiling water). Forced convection — pumps + fans (car radiator, central heating). Drives OCEAN CURRENTS (thermohaline circulation), atmospheric winds (Hadley cells), weather systems. Cannot happen in VACUUM or SOLIDS. (3) RADIATION — transfer via ELECTROMAGNETIC WAVES (infrared); NO medium required — works in VACUUM; Sun's energy reaches Earth via radiation across 150 million km. Described by STEFAN-BOLTZMANN LAW: P = σAT⁴ (A = area, T = absolute temperature, σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W/m²K⁴). BLACK BODY radiates most; shiny SILVER radiates least. KIRCHHOFF'S law: good absorbers are good emitters. THERMOS FLASK uses all three controls — double-walled silvered vacuum flask: vacuum stops conduction + convection; silver coating reflects radiation. EXAMPLES: conduction = touching a hot pan; convection = boiling water; radiation = warming under the Sun. Why clothes are black in winter (absorb more Sun radiation)/white in summer (reflect). hot fluid rises (less dense), cool fluid sinks; drives sea breezes, weather, boiling water.

cards.front:
The FIRST LAW of THERMODYNAMICS states that:

(A) Entropy of an isolated system never decreases
(B) ENERGY can neither be CREATED nor DESTROYED, only converted from one form to another
(C) Absolute zero cannot be reached
(D) Two bodies in thermal equilibrium have equal temperatures
cards.back:
(B) ENERGY can neither be CREATED nor DESTROYED, only converted from one form to another

Heat & Thermodynamics — FIRST LAW of THERMODYNAMICS = Law of CONSERVATION OF ENERGY applied to thermodynamic systems. Formulation: ΔU = Q − W; where ΔU = change in internal energy; Q = heat added TO the system; W = work done BY the system. Energy is neither created nor destroyed — only transformed. EXAMPLES: (a) heat given to gas → raises internal energy + does work (pushing piston); (b) mechanical work done on gas → raises internal energy (compression heats gas — diesel engine ignition); (c) electrical energy → heat (resistance heater); → light + sound (speakers + LEDs). HISTORICAL: formulated by James Prescott JOULE (1843-1847 paddle-wheel experiment showing mechanical work ≡ heat; mechanical equivalent of heat ~4.18 J/cal); ROBERT MAYER, HERMANN HELMHOLTZ, RUDOLF CLAUSIUS (~1850). DEBUNKED perpetual motion MACHINE of the FIRST KIND (gives more energy output than input — impossible). RELATED LAWS: (a) ZEROTH LAW — if A ≡ B thermally + B ≡ C, then A ≡ C (defines temperature); formulated later but numbered 'zero' so it's logically prior. (b) SECOND LAW — entropy of isolated system never decreases (time's arrow, Clausius/Kelvin — no heat engine converts 100% heat to work, no refrigerator works with no input; MAX EFFICIENCY = Carnot = 1 − Tc/Th). (c) THIRD LAW — absolute zero unattainable (Walther Nernst, 1906). Second law is why HEAT ENGINES (IC engines, turbines) have efficiency <100% — the 'Carnot limit' in a steam turbine: η = 1 − Tcold/Thot; boiler 900K, condenser 300K → Carnot η ≈ 66%, actual ~35%.

cards.front:
The temperature at which a liquid CHANGES to VAPOUR at atmospheric pressure is called its:

(A) Melting point
(B) BOILING POINT
(C) Freezing point
(D) Dew point
cards.back:
(B) BOILING POINT

Heat & Thermodynamics — BOILING POINT — temperature at which the VAPOUR PRESSURE of a liquid EQUALS the external (atmospheric) pressure, allowing BUBBLES to form throughout the liquid. For WATER at 1 atm = 100°C = 373.15 K = 212°F. LOWERED at HIGH ALTITUDE: (a) Darjeeling/Shimla (~2000 m) water boils at ~93°C; (b) Mt Everest summit (8848 m) ~72°C — can't cook rice/dal properly; (c) solution: PRESSURE COOKER (raises pressure → higher boiling point → faster cooking). On Everest, pressure cooker is essential. At 2 atm, water boils at ~120°C. CONVERSELY, pure distilled water in open container can BOIL AT ROOM TEMPERATURE in vacuum chamber. MELTING POINT — solid-to-liquid transition; for ice = 0°C at 1 atm. FREEZING POINT same as melting point for pure substances. DEW POINT — temperature at which water vapour in air begins to condense; humidity indicator. LATENT HEAT: extra heat needed to cause PHASE CHANGE without temperature change. (a) Latent heat of fusion of ice = 80 cal/g (or 334 kJ/kg); (b) latent heat of vaporisation of water = 540 cal/g (or 2260 kJ/kg) — very high, which is why SWEATING cools us efficiently (evaporation takes a lot of heat from skin). SPECIFIC HEAT CAPACITY: water = 4186 J/kg·K — very HIGH (why coastal climates are moderate, water heats/cools slowly); iron = 450; air = 1005. Water's anomalous expansion: densest at 4°C (why ice floats, lakes freeze from top, aquatic life survives winter). for water, 100 °C at 1 atm.

cards.front:
A thermos flask prevents heat loss primarily through:

(A) Magnetic shielding
(B) A VACUUM between double walls (stops conduction + convection) + silvered surfaces
(C) Sound absorption
(D) Metal lining that absorbs heat
cards.back:
(B) A VACUUM between double walls (stops conduction + convection) + silvered surfaces

Heat & Thermodynamics — THERMOS FLASK — or VACUUM FLASK, invented by SIR JAMES DEWAR (1892) for cryogenic experiments; commercialised by THERMOS GmbH (Berlin, 1904). DESIGN: double-walled glass or metal bottle with: (1) VACUUM between the two walls — eliminates CONDUCTION (no matter to conduct) + CONVECTION (no fluid to circulate). (2) SILVERED inner + outer surfaces of the double wall — REFLECT thermal INFRARED radiation back to the contents (minimising radiation loss). (3) CORK/plastic stopper with low thermal conductivity — reduces heat escape through the top. (4) Outer plastic/metal casing — protects the fragile vacuum wall from impact. PERFORMANCE: good flask keeps hot drinks ~70°C after 12 hours; cold drinks near 4°C for a day. EVERYDAY variants: Camper's Hydro Flask, Milton, Cello, Milton Thermosteel, Eagle (Indian brands). SAME PRINCIPLE used in: (a) cryogenic Dewars for liquid nitrogen (-196°C) + liquid helium (-269°C); (b) space telescope insulation (JWST); (c) insulation for LNG tankers. THERMODYNAMIC CONCEPT: near-perfect ISOLATED SYSTEM — no heat exchange with surroundings; a familiar toy example of adiabatic containment. ESCAPE ROUTES even in a perfect thermos: (a) residual gas in imperfect vacuum; (b) thin glass/metal thermal bridge at the seal; (c) radiation if silvering degraded. GLASS VACUUM flasks DANGEROUS if broken — implode. Modern STAINLESS STEEL vacuum flasks safer. reflects radiation.

SAME PRINCIPLE used in: (a) cryogenic Dewars for liquid nitrogen (-196°C) + liquid helium (-269°C); (b) space telescope insulation (JWST); (c) insulation for LNG tankers. THERMODYNAMIC CONCEPT: near-perfect ISOLATED SYSTEM — no heat exchange with surroundings; a familiar toy example of adiabatic containment. ESCAPE ROUTES even in a perfect thermos: (a) residual gas in imperfect vacuum; (b) thin glass/metal thermal bridge at the seal; (c) radiation if silvering degraded. GLASS VACUUM flasks DANGEROUS if broken — implode. Modern STAINLESS STEEL vacuum flasks safer. reflects radiation.

cards.front:
The 'LATENT HEAT of FUSION' of ICE is:

(A) 100 cal/g
(B) 80 cal/g (334 kJ/kg)
(C) 540 cal/g
(D) 1 cal/g
cards.back:
(B) 80 cal/g (334 kJ/kg)

Heat & Thermodynamics — LATENT HEAT — heat absorbed or released during a PHASE CHANGE at constant temperature. For WATER: (a) LATENT HEAT OF FUSION (ice → water) = ~80 CAL/G = 334 J/g = 334 kJ/kg at 0°C. (b) LATENT HEAT OF VAPORISATION (water → steam) = 540 cal/g = 2260 J/g = 2260 kJ/kg at 100°C. (c) Latent heat of sublimation (ice → steam directly) = sum of both ~620 cal/g. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCES: (1) Ice cools drinks VERY efficiently — even after it reaches 0°C, it needs 80 cal/g to MELT, absorbing lots of heat from the drink. (2) COOLING by EVAPORATION — sweat needs ~540 cal/g to evaporate from skin — massive cooling effect. Why fans feel cool (enhance evaporation). Why desert coolers work (dry air takes up moisture + cools by vaporisation). (3) STEAM BURNS WORSE than hot water burns at same temperature — when 100°C steam condenses on skin, it releases 540 cal/g of latent heat ON TOP of cooling from 100°C to body temp. (4) CLOUDS forming release latent heat → warm atmosphere + drive convection, hurricanes, thunderstorms. (5) AIR CONDITIONERS + refrigerators USE latent heat — refrigerant evaporates in the cold coil (absorbs heat from room), condenses in the hot coil outside (releases heat). CALCULATIONS: melting 1 kg ice at 0°C → 1 kg water at 0°C needs 334 kJ; heating 1 kg water from 0→100°C needs 4186 × 100 = 418.6 kJ; boiling 1 kg water at 100°C to steam needs 2260 kJ. Total for 1 kg ice → steam = 334 + 418.6 + 2260 ≈ 3013 kJ. heat required to melt 1 gram of ice at 0°C without changing temperature.

cards.front:
WATER reaches its MAXIMUM DENSITY at:

(A) 0°C (freezing point)
(B) 4°C
(C) 100°C
(D) 25°C
cards.back:
(B) 4°C

Heat & Thermodynamics — WATER'S ANOMALOUS EXPANSION — unlike most substances, water's DENSITY does NOT monotonically increase as temperature drops. Between 4°C and 0°C water EXPANDS (density decreases) as it cools. DENSITY: peaks at ~1.000 g/cm³ at 4°C; drops to ~0.9998 at 0°C (liquid); drops abruptly to ~0.917 at 0°C (solid ice). So ICE is LIGHTER than cold water → FLOATS. REASON: WATER MOLECULES form HYDROGEN BONDS via their polar O-H bonds. In solid ice, molecules arrange in an OPEN HEXAGONAL lattice with large gaps (required by H-bond geometry) → lower density. Below 4°C, clusters of tetrahedral 'ice-like' structures start to form in the liquid, expanding it. Above 4°C, normal thermal expansion dominates. CONSEQUENCES — CRUCIAL FOR LIFE: (1) LAKES + RIVERS freeze TOP-DOWN: cold water at 4°C sinks + stays at bottom (densest); water at 0°C floats up + freezes as ICE on surface. The ice layer INSULATES the liquid beneath, keeping it at 4°C → AQUATIC LIFE SURVIVES winter. Without this anomaly, lakes would freeze SOLID bottom-up → aquatic life would die + climate would be very different. (2) FROST DAMAGE to crops + pipes: water expands ~9% on freezing → bursts pipes, cracks rocks, shatters ceramics. (3) GLACIERS + ICEBERGS float on seas → ~90% underwater (hence 'tip of the iceberg'). (4) Drops of water freeze + expand in plant cells → killing tropical crops. Agricultural relevance: frost-tolerance breeding; chilling injury. OTHER anomalous liquids: bismuth, antimony, silicon, gallium all EXPAND on freezing. Most substances contract on cooling + expand on heating. ANOMALOUS expansion; below 4°C water EXPANDS as it cools; why ice floats + lakes freeze from top down.

cards.front:
A BIMETALLIC STRIP (used in thermostats + fire alarms) works because:

(A) Metals conduct equally
(B) DIFFERENT metals EXPAND BY DIFFERENT AMOUNTS when heated, causing the strip to BEND
(C) Metals emit light when heated
(D) Metals melt at room temperature
cards.back:
(B) DIFFERENT metals EXPAND BY DIFFERENT AMOUNTS when heated, causing the strip to BEND

Heat & Thermodynamics — BIMETALLIC STRIP — two strips of different metals (usually BRASS + INVAR, or BRASS + IRON, or COPPER + STEEL) riveted together along their length. When heated, the two metals expand at DIFFERENT RATES (different LINEAR EXPANSION COEFFICIENTS α). The strip bends TOWARDS the LOW-EXPANSION metal. Typical α values: brass = 19 × 10⁻⁶ /K; iron = 12 × 10⁻⁶ /K; invar (Fe-Ni alloy) = 1.2 × 10⁻⁶ /K (invented by Guillaume 1896, Nobel 1920). USES: (1) THERMOSTATS in electric irons, geysers, ovens, refrigerators, AC units — the bend breaks/makes an electrical contact at the set temperature. (2) FIRE ALARMS — strip bends at high temp → closes the alarm circuit. (3) MECHANICAL CLOCK compensation for temperature drift. (4) Bimetallic THERMOMETERS (dial type). LINEAR EXPANSION: ΔL = L₀ × α × ΔT. AREA expansion coefficient = 2α; VOLUME expansion coefficient = 3α. WHY EXPANSION: increased temperature → atoms vibrate with larger amplitude → average inter-atomic distance increases slightly → solid grows. In engineering: EXPANSION JOINTS in bridges (steel expands ~1 cm per 10m per 50°C change), railway tracks (gap between rails — 'clickety-clack'), pipelines, concrete slabs — all accommodate thermal expansion. Hot-water bottles / overhead wires sag in summer + taut in winter. INVAR: designed for NIL expansion → precision instruments, watches, aircraft + space; Superinvar (Fe-Ni-Co) has even less. SPECIAL: water between 0-4°C has NEGATIVE volume expansion coefficient. closing/opening an electrical circuit.

cards.front:
THIRD LAW of THERMODYNAMICS states that:

(A) Energy is conserved
(B) Absolute ZERO (0 K = −273.15 °C) cannot be REACHED by any finite number of operations
(C) Entropy always increases
(D) Heat flows from hot to cold
cards.back:
(B) Absolute ZERO (0 K = −273.15 °C) cannot be REACHED by any finite number of operations

Heat & Thermodynamics — THIRD LAW OF THERMODYNAMICS — formulated by WALTHER NERNST (1906; Nobel 1920). Two equivalent statements: (a) Entropy S of a PERFECT CRYSTAL at ABSOLUTE ZERO (0 K) is EXACTLY ZERO (minimum, unique configuration). (b) Absolute zero is UNATTAINABLE — can only approach asymptotically; each successive reduction in temperature takes more energy than the previous. COLDEST temperatures achieved: (a) Vostok, Antarctica NATURAL record: −89.2°C (surface, 1983); (b) DOMA Ridge, Antarctica: −98°C (from satellite, 2018). (c) LAB: Bose-Einstein condensates cooled to ~38 pK (picokelvin = 10⁻¹² K) — MIT + Leiden experiments. Nanokelvin in atomic magnetometers + quantum computers. DEEP SPACE: cosmic microwave background ~2.725 K. BOOMERANG NEBULA (5000 ly away) ~1 K — coldest known NATURAL place due to rapid adiabatic expansion from dying star. (Lower than CMB!). IMPLICATIONS: (1) HEAT ENGINES: Kelvin-Planck statement of 2nd law implies no engine has 100% efficiency; Carnot η = 1 − Tc/Th; only at Tc = 0 K could η = 100% — but 3rd law forbids it. Universe never gives us absolute-zero sinks. (2) QUANTUM mechanics: as T→0, particles don't come to rest — ZERO-POINT ENERGY remains (a quantum effect — Heisenberg uncertainty requires residual motion). (3) Superconductivity, superfluidity, Bose-Einstein + Fermi condensation all occur near absolute zero. Chemistry: standard entropies tabulated starting from S(0K) = 0. Astrobiology: habitable zone of planets sensitive to lower bound of liquid water. entropy of a perfect crystal at 0 K equals zero.
cards.option3: Heat flows from hot to cold

cards.front:
The LARGE specific heat capacity of water (~4186 J/kg·K) is responsible for:

(A) Making water light
(B) MODERATING climate near large water bodies
(C) Making water transparent
(D) Making ice float
cards.back:
(B) MODERATING climate near large water bodies

Heat & Thermodynamics — SPECIFIC HEAT CAPACITY (c) — heat needed to raise 1 kg of a substance by 1 K (or 1°C). WATER'S c = 4186 J/(kg·K) = 1 cal/(g·K) = 4.186 kJ/(kg·K) — EXCEPTIONALLY HIGH (2nd highest of common substances, after liquid ammonia). REASON for high c of water: H-bonds take lots of energy to partially break as water heats up. CONSEQUENCES + applications: (1) CLIMATE MODERATION: oceans absorb heat in summer + release slowly in winter → COASTAL climates are milder (Mumbai, Chennai vs Nagpur). Ocean acts as thermal buffer for the planet — slows global warming (oceans absorbed ~90% of excess heat from CO₂ forcing). (2) COOLANT in engineering: car RADIATORS use water to absorb engine heat without boiling; nuclear reactor cooling; industrial chillers. (3) HOT WATER BOTTLE keeps warm longer than any other common substance. (4) COOKING slow with water — takes time to heat; good for even cooking of rice, dal. (5) HUMAN BODY is ~60% water — buffers body temperature despite metabolic heat generation; sweating (evaporation) cools us. (6) STEAM heating systems in buildings + industry. COMPARISON: specific heats (J/kg·K): water 4186; ice 2100; steam 2010; air 1005; aluminium 900; iron 450; copper 385; gold 128; lead 128; sand 830; marble 880; glass 840; ethanol 2420; sea water 3850 (slightly less due to salts). Good DELETE cooling fluid choice depends on both specific heat + boiling point + viscosity + corrosion. slow heating + slow cooling of oceans; why coastal cities have less extreme temperatures than inland.

cards.front:
A PRESSURE COOKER cooks FASTER than an open pot because:

(A) It cools the food first
(B) Higher pressure inside RAISES the BOILING POINT of water to ~120 °C, so food cooks faster at higher temperature
(C) It uses less heat
(D) It releases nitrogen gas
cards.back:
(B) Higher pressure inside RAISES the BOILING POINT of water to ~120 °C, so food cooks faster at higher temperature

Heat & Thermodynamics — PRESSURE COOKER — exploits the fact that BOILING POINT RISES WITH PRESSURE. Standard atmospheric pressure = 1 atm (101.325 kPa); water boils at 100°C. Pressure cookers operate at ~1.5-2 atm (gauge pressure 15 psi on top of 1 atm atmospheric). This raises water's boiling point to ~120°C — which: (a) cooks food ~3× FASTER (chemical reaction rate roughly doubles for every 10°C rise, Q10 rule, Arrhenius equation); (b) makes tough meats + dal tender faster; (c) reduces fuel + time consumption ~40-70%. INVENTED by FRENCH physicist DENIS PAPIN (1679) — his 'steam digester' / 'Digester of Bones'. SAFETY: (a) WEIGHTED VALVE on lid whistles at set pressure — excess steam escapes; (b) SAFETY FUSE (rubber or metal) melts / ruptures at emergency overpressure preventing explosion; (c) GASKET seals the lid; replace if torn. HIGH-ALTITUDE cooking: essential above 2000m where boiling point drops below 95°C + food barely cooks; Himalayan treks always use pressure cookers. OTHER applications of pressure-boiling relation: (1) autoclaves (medical sterilisers) — 121°C at 15 psi for 15 min kills heat-resistant spores. (2) Retort pouches + canning — high temp under pressure sterilises food. (3) Geyser (hot spring) water often exceeds 100°C underground due to overlying rock pressure; flashes to steam when pressure drops on surface (e.g., Yellowstone geysers). REVERSE: water in VACUUM boils at room temperature → used in vacuum distillation (alcohol manufacture, pharma). 'ENGINEERING TOILET BRAIN HACK': Le Chatelier's principle — increased pressure shifts vapor-liquid equilibrium toward liquid phase, requiring higher T to boil.

cards.front:
The TEMPERATURE at which water FREEZES on the Celsius scale is:

(A) 32 °C is the freezing point
(B) 0 °C is the freezing point
(C) 100 °C is the freezing point
(D) 273 °C is the freezing point
cards.back:
(B) 0 °C is the freezing point

Heat & Thermodynamics — Water freezes at 0 °C (= 32 °F = 273.15 K). Boils at 100 °C (= 212 °F = 373.15 K). Conversion: F = C × 9/5 + 32; K = C + 273.15. ABSOLUTE ZERO = −273.15 °C = 0 K (theoretical lowest temperature, no thermal motion). Distractor 32 = freezing in Fahrenheit. Distractor 273 = absolute zero in Celsius (negative).

(A) Heats up + cools quickly always
(B) Resists temperature change well
(C) Cannot conduct heat through it
(D) Boils at a very low temperature

Heat & Thermodynamics — High specific heat of water → resists temperature change. Important consequences: (1) OCEANS act as climate moderator (slow to heat/cool); (2) coastal climates milder than inland; (3) water in body helps regulate temperature; (4) cooling agent in radiators, power plants. Sand specific heat ~0.84 J/g·°C — low → deserts cold at night, hot in day. Mostly water on Earth's surface = stable climate. Distractor 1 = opposite of high specific heat.

cards.front:
LATENT HEAT of vaporization is the heat needed to:

(A) Raise the temperature of liquid by 1°C
(B) Convert liquid to vapour without temp rise
(C) Cool a vapour into a liquid form again
(D) Convert solid into liquid form by melting
cards.back:
(B) Convert liquid to vapour without temp rise

Two types: LATENT HEAT OF FUSION (solid → liquid; for water = 334 J/g, used for ice melting); LATENT HEAT OF VAPORIZATION (liquid → vapour; for water = 2260 J/g, very high — keeps body cool via sweat evaporation; steam burns are bad — releases lots of energy on condensing).
