cards.front:
MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging) for medical scanning works by:

(A) Hydrogen nuclei aligning + flipping in magnetic field
(B) X-rays scanning the patient body too alone
(C) Ultrasonic sound waves bouncing off alone
(D) Radioactive injection + gamma rays (option here)
cards.back:
(A) Hydrogen nuclei aligning + flipping in magnetic field

Electricity & Magnetism — MRI — Strong magnetic field (1.5-7 T) aligns HYDROGEN nuclei in body's water; radio pulses flip them; signals during return reveal tissue type. NO IONISING RADIATION (safer than X-ray, CT). Best for SOFT TISSUES (brain, spinal cord, joints, organs). Limitation: people with metal implants (pacemakers, certain stents) can't get MRI. Inventors of clinical MRI: Lauterbur + Mansfield (Nobel 2003). Compare: X-RAY (electromagnetic, bones); CT (multiple X-rays, 3D); ULTRASOUND (sound, fetus + soft); PET (radioactive tracer); ECG (heart); EEG (brain).

A COMPASS works because Earth has:

(A) Magnetic field aligning the needle
(B) Strong gravity pulling on iron
(C) Electric field that orients compass
(D) Atmosphere swirling in N direction
cards.back:
(A) Magnetic field aligning the needle

Electricity & Magnetism — COMPASS NEEDLE = small magnet aligning with Earth's field → points ~N-S. INVENTED in CHINA ~11th century (lodestone — natural magnet, magnetite). Revolutionised SEA NAVIGATION + global trade. MAGNETIC NORTH ≠ TRUE NORTH; difference = MAGNETIC DECLINATION (varies geographically + over decades). Currently magnetic N pole near 86°N in Arctic, drifting toward Russia at ~50 km/year! Modern GPS replaced compass for navigation, but compass remains BACKUP (no battery, works always; used by hikers, ships, aircraft). GYRO compass — used in ships, points to TRUE north regardless of magnetic field.

Cutting a bar magnet in half results in:

(A) Two smaller magnets, each with N + S poles
(B) One N-pole magnet + one S-pole only
(C) Two non-magnetic pieces of metal
(D) Doubled-strength single magnet.
cards.back:

Electricity & Magnetism — MAGNETIC MONOPOLES DON'T EXIST (in classical physics). Each piece retains BOTH poles, no matter how small. FUNDAMENTAL: ∇·B = 0 (one of Maxwell's 4 equations). Distractor 3 — partial truth for outdoor lightning rods, but indoor earthing is for fault current. Distractor 4 — false.

(B) Have free electrons that can move under an applied field

Electricity & Magnetism — Conductors (metals) — outermost electrons are loosely bound, can drift under an applied electric field → carry current. Insulators (rubber, plastic, glass, dry wood) — electrons are tightly bound to atoms; minimal flow. Semiconductors (silicon, germanium) — intermediate conductivity, controllable via doping. Distractor 1 — both have electrons; the difference is mobility. Distractor 3 — weight is unrelated. Distractor 4 — false; conductors usually conduct heat well TOO, but cooling rate depends on many factors.

cards.front:
A capacitor's primary function in an electrical circuit is to:

(A) Generate a steady supply of direct current
(B) Store electrical energy in an electric field temporarily
(C) Convert AC to DC using internal rectifier diodes
(D) Amplify a small voltage signal coming from the source
cards.back:
(B) Store electrical energy in an electric field temporarily

Electricity & Magnetism — Capacitor — two conductors separated by an insulator (dielectric). Stores energy as charge separation: U = ½CV². Capacitance C = Q/V (farads). Used for: smoothing power supplies, blocking DC while passing AC, timing circuits, energy storage in flash bulbs / defibrillators. Distractor 1 = battery / cell role. Distractor 3 = rectifier role. Distractor 4 = transistor / amplifier role.

cards.option2: Convert AC to DC using internal rectifier diodes

cards.front:
Lightning rods on tall buildings work primarily by:

(A) Repelling lightning back up into the cloud above
(B) Providing a low-resistance path to safely earth the strike
(C) Producing a counter-current that cancels the lightning
(D) Absorbing the lightning's energy into a internal coil
cards.back:
(B) Providing a low-resistance path to safely earth the strike

Electricity & Magnetism — Lightning rod — sharp metal point at the highest point of a building, connected by a thick conductor to the ground. When lightning strikes, the rod offers the path of least resistance, conducting the current safely to earth without flowing through the building. Invented by Benjamin Franklin (1752). The 'sharp point' helps initiate corona discharge that ionises the air, often draining the cloud's charge gradually before a sudden strike. Distractor 1 — rods don't repel. Distractor 3 — no counter-current is produced. Distractor 4 — capacitor-style absorption isn't how rods work.

cards.front:
The SI unit of magnetic field strength (B, magnetic flux density) is:

(A) Newton
(B) Tesla
(C) Weber
(D) Henry
cards.back:
(B) Tesla

Electricity & Magnetism — Tesla (T) — magnetic flux DENSITY, named after Nikola Tesla. 1 T = 1 Wb/m² = 1 N/(A·m). Earth's magnetic field at the surface ≈ 25-65 µT. Refrigerator magnet ~5 mT. Hospital MRI ~1.5-3 T. Strongest steady lab field ~45 T. Other related units — Weber (Wb) = magnetic FLUX (= T·m²); Henry (H) = inductance (= Wb/A); Gauss (CGS, 1 T = 10⁴ Gauss).

cards.front:
Magnetic field lines around a bar magnet:

(A) Start from south pole and end at north
(B) Form closed loops; emerge from N pole, enter S pole outside the magnet, run S→N inside
(C) Start and end at infinity
(D) Are always straight lines
cards.back:
(B) Form closed loops; emerge from N pole, enter S pole outside the magnet, run S→N inside

Electricity & Magnetism — Magnetic field lines form closed loops — no monopoles in classical magnetism (Maxwell's 2nd equation: ∇·B = 0). Outside magnet: from N to S; inside: from S to N. Lines never cross. Density of lines indicates field strength. The 'isolated magnetic monopole' has been hypothesised (Dirac, 1931) but never observed experimentally despite decades of searches.

cards.front:
The geographic North Pole of Earth is actually the:

(A) Magnetic North Pole of Earth
(B) Magnetic South Pole of Earth (since opposite poles attract — a compass north points there)
(C) Has no relation to magnetism
(D) Both Magnetic North and Magnetic South simultaneously
cards.back:
(B) Magnetic South Pole of Earth (since opposite poles attract — a compass north points there)

Electricity & Magnetism — A compass needle's NORTH end points to geographic North → that point must be a MAGNETIC SOUTH (opposites attract). So the geographic North Pole is technically a magnetic 'south' pole, and vice versa. The terminology 'Magnetic North Pole' commonly used in geomagnetic context is a convention. Earth's magnetic field also drifts ('polar wandering') and reverses on geological timescales (last full reversal ~780,000 years ago). Magnetic field generated by molten outer-core convection — 'geodynamo'.

cards.front:
Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction states that an EMF is induced in a circuit:

(A) When current flows through it
(B) When the magnetic flux through it changes with time
(C) Only in DC circuits
(D) Only when temperature changes
cards.back:
(B) When the magnetic flux through it changes with time

Electricity & Magnetism — Faraday's Law: EMF = −dΦ_B/dt where Φ_B is magnetic flux. The minus sign represents Lenz's law (induced EMF opposes the change). Discovered 1831 by Michael Faraday and independently by Joseph Henry. Forms the basis of generators, transformers, induction cooktops, electric motors. AC generators rotate a coil in a magnetic field — flux varies sinusoidally → AC EMF. DC generators add a commutator to flip current direction every half-cycle.

cards.front:
Lenz's law gives the:

(A) Magnitude of magnetic flux
(B) Direction of induced current — opposes the cause that produced it
(C) Speed of light in matter
(D) Newton's third law of motion
cards.back:
(B) Direction of induced current — opposes the cause that produced it

Electricity & Magnetism — Lenz's law (1834) — the induced current direction is such that it opposes the change in magnetic flux that produced it. This is the minus sign in Faraday's Law (EMF = −dΦ/dt). Consistent with energy conservation — 'free' induced current would violate it. Practical example: dropping a magnet through a copper pipe — induced eddy currents oppose its fall, creating drag. Used in regenerative braking, induction cooktops, eddy-current brakes.

cards.front:
Materials that are STRONGLY attracted to magnets and can be permanently magnetised are called:

(A) Diamagnetic
(B) Ferromagnetic (Fe, Ni, Co, Gd, alloys)
(C) Paramagnetic
(D) Antiferromagnetic
cards.back:
(B) Ferromagnetic (Fe, Ni, Co, Gd, alloys)

Electricity & Magnetism — Three basic magnetic categories — Ferromagnetic (Fe, Ni, Co, Gd, Dy, alloys like alnico, neodymium magnets) — strongly attracted, can retain magnetisation. Paramagnetic (Al, Pt, O₂) — weakly attracted, no retention. Diamagnetic (water, copper, gold, bismuth) — weakly REPELLED. Above the Curie temperature (Fe ~1043 K, Ni 627 K, Co 1394 K), ferromagnetic materials become paramagnetic. Antiferromagnetic — atomic magnetic moments align oppositely, cancel out (e.g., MnO).

cards.front:
An electromagnet differs from a permanent magnet because:

(A) It is made of plastic
(B) Its magnetism exists only when current flows through the coil; can be turned on/off
(C) It is always weaker than a bar magnet
(D) It does not need any iron core
cards.back:
(B) Its magnetism exists only when current flows through the coil; can be turned on/off

Electricity & Magnetism — Electromagnet = solenoid (coil of insulated wire) wound around a soft-iron core. Magnetic field exists ONLY when current flows. Strength can be varied by current; can be very strong (MRI, particle accelerators, scrap-yard cranes). Soft iron is preferred (low retentivity → loses magnetism quickly when current stops; ideal for switchable devices). Permanent magnet uses high-coercivity materials (steel, neodymium-iron-boron) that retain magnetism without external current. Maglev trains use electromagnets for both lift and propulsion.
cards.option2: It is always weaker than a bar magnet
cards.option3: It does not need any iron core

cards.front:
A magnet has NORTH + SOUTH poles. The fundamental law of magnetism states:

(A) Like poles attract
(B) LIKE POLES REPEL, UNLIKE POLES ATTRACT
(C) Only repulsion occurs
(D) Poles have no attraction
cards.back:
(B) LIKE POLES REPEL, UNLIKE POLES ATTRACT

Electricity & Magnetism — MAGNETISM — fundamental phenomenon of nature. KEY PROPERTIES: (1) MAGNETS have 2 POLES — NORTH-SEEKING + SOUTH-SEEKING. (2) LIKE poles REPEL; UNLIKE poles ATTRACT (analogous to electric charges, but magnetic MONOPOLES don't exist — cutting a magnet in half gives 2 complete magnets each with N + S). (3) Magnet ATTRACTS ferromagnetic materials (IRON, NICKEL, COBALT, their alloys, rare-earth neodymium) — these become induced magnets. (4) EARTH is a giant magnet; compass needle aligns N-S. Geographic NORTH is actually MAGNETIC SOUTH (a compass N-pole points to geographic N because unlike poles attract). TYPES of MAGNETIC MATERIALS: (a) FERROMAGNETIC — strongly attracted; retain magnetism; Fe, Ni, Co, Gd, Dy + alloys; examples alnico, neodymium (NdFeB, strongest common magnet), ferrites. Curie temperature (above which becomes paramagnetic): Fe 770°C, Ni 358°C, Co 1115°C. (b) PARAMAGNETIC — weakly attracted; Al, Pt, Mg, Li, Na, O₂ liquid; attraction disappears when field removed. (c) DIAMAGNETIC — weakly REPELLED by magnetic field; Cu, Bi, C, Au, Ag, water, most materials. (d) ANTIFERROMAGNETIC — neighbouring spins cancel (Cr, MnO, FeO). (e) FERRIMAGNETIC — like antiferro but net magnetic moment (magnetite Fe₃O₄, most ferrites). MAGNETIC FIELD (B): region around magnet / current-carrying conductor where magnetic force is experienced. UNITS: SI — TESLA (T) = Wb/m² = kg/(A·s²); CGS — GAUSS (G), 1 T = 10,000 G. Earth's field ~0.5 G = 5 × 10⁻⁵ T; fridge magnet ~5 mT; MRI machine 1.5-7 T; LHC magnets 8 T; strongest lab field ~45 T (continuous, National High Magnetic Field Laboratory, Florida). MAGNETIC FIELD LINES — direction of compass needle + closeness = field strength; FORM CLOSED LOOPS (no monopoles means no sources/sinks); go from N to S outside + S to N inside. ELECTRO-MAGNETISM (Oersted 1820, Ampere, Faraday, Maxwell) — electricity + magnetism are UNIFIED phenomena. Moving charges produce magnetic fields; changing magnetic fields produce electric fields (Faraday's law). MAXWELL's 4 EQUATIONS unify E + M = CLASSICAL ELECTROMAGNETISM. One of physics's crowning achievements. LIGHT is an EM wave (Maxwell 1865). RELATIVITY: magnetism is a RELATIVISTIC EFFECT of moving charges (Einstein 1905). magnetic monopoles do not exist; always dipole (N + S pair inseparable).

cards.front:
OERSTED's EXPERIMENT (1820) demonstrated that:

(A) Magnets attract iron
(B) ELECTRIC CURRENT PRODUCES A MAGNETIC FIELD
(C) Magnetic fields produce light
(D) Electrons have spin
cards.back:
(B) ELECTRIC CURRENT PRODUCES A MAGNETIC FIELD

Electricity & Magnetism — HANS CHRISTIAN OERSTED (1777-1851, Danish physicist) — in April 1820, during a lecture demonstration at Copenhagen University, accidentally noticed that a COMPASS NEEDLE DEFLECTED when he switched on an electric current in a nearby wire. This was the FIRST observed connection between ELECTRICITY + MAGNETISM — founded the field of ELECTROMAGNETISM. RIGHT-HAND THUMB RULE (Maxwell's RH rule): for a straight current-carrying wire, point RIGHT THUMB in direction of CURRENT, FINGERS CURL in direction of MAGNETIC FIELD. B field forms CONCENTRIC CIRCLES around the wire. For SOLENOID/COIL, RH rule: fingers curl in current direction, thumb points to N pole. AMPERE'S LAW (André-Marie Ampère, 1820s, soon after Oersted) — mathematical formulation; magnetic field around a long wire: B = μ₀I/(2πr), where μ₀ = permeability of free space = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A. BIOT-SAVART LAW (Jean-Baptiste Biot + Félix Savart, 1820) — dB = (μ₀/4π)(I dL × r̂)/r². FARADAY (1831) — REVERSE: a CHANGING MAGNETIC FIELD INDUCES an EMF / electric current in a nearby conductor — FARADAY's LAW of ELECTROMAGNETIC INDUCTION. Basis of GENERATORS, TRANSFORMERS, INDUCTION motors, induction cooktops. LENZ's LAW (1834) — the induced current opposes the change in flux (consequence of conservation of energy). MAXWELL (1864-73) — UNIFIED electricity + magnetism in 4 equations: (1) GAUSS's law for E; (2) Gauss's law for B (no monopoles); (3) FARADAY's law; (4) AMPERE-MAXWELL law (with displacement current). Predicted EM waves travelling at speed of light — light IS an EM wave! HERTZ (1887) — experimentally produced + detected EM waves (radio waves) confirming Maxwell. TESLA + EDISON + others — developed practical AC + DC systems (War of Currents). MARCONI (1895-1901) — wireless radio communication using EM waves. APPLICATIONS of Oersted's discovery are EVERYWHERE: motors (electricity → motion), generators (motion → electricity), transformers, loudspeakers (audio to vibration), microphones (vibration to audio), MRI (magnetic resonance imaging), induction cookers, wireless charging, maglev trains, particle accelerators (LHC), all of modern electronics. Without electromagnetism → no industrial civilization.

cards.front:
EARTH's MAGNETIC POLES are:

(A) Fixed at geographic poles
(B) Near but NOT at geographic poles
(C) Non-existent
(D) Located at equator
cards.back:
(B) Near but NOT at geographic poles

Electricity & Magnetism — EARTH's MAGNETIC FIELD ('GEOMAGNETIC FIELD') — generated by DYNAMO EFFECT in Earth's OUTER CORE — convection of molten iron + nickel alloy + Earth's rotation create + sustain the field. FIELD STRENGTH: ~25-65 µT at surface (~0.25-0.65 G); strongest at magnetic poles (70 µT), weakest near magnetic equator (25 µT). Varies with location, altitude, time. MAGNETIC POLES: distinct from GEOGRAPHIC POLES. (1) MAGNETIC NORTH POLE (where a compass N-pole points to — technically called magnetic SOUTH because unlike poles attract, but conventionally 'Magnetic North'). Currently located in ARCTIC OCEAN near SIBERIA + moving rapidly TOWARDS Russia — ~55 KM/YEAR (accelerated since 1990s from ~15 km/yr). Current position (2025) near 86°N, 172°E. Located in Canadian Arctic before 1990s, now moved northwest. Updated regularly in WORLD MAGNETIC MODEL (WMM, NOAA/British Geological Survey, 5-year cycle; 2020 model updated early due to rapid movement). (2) MAGNETIC SOUTH POLE — near coast of East Antarctica; also drifts ~5 km/yr. DIFFERENCE from geographic: MAGNETIC VARIATION (DECLINATION) — angle between magnetic + true north; varies by location; important for navigation. INCLINATION (DIP) — angle field makes with horizontal; 0° at magnetic equator, 90° at poles. GEOMAGNETIC REVERSALS — the N + S poles have FLIPPED POSITIONS ~200 times over geological history. Last reversal: Brunhes-Matuyama reversal, ~780,000 years ago. Typical reversal takes 1000-10,000 years; during which field weakens dramatically. We are currently experiencing field weakening (~9% weaker in 200 years — SOUTH ATLANTIC ANOMALY growing) — possible indicator of imminent reversal (could be geologically 'imminent' = within millennia). PALAEOMAGNETISM — records of past polarity preserved in volcanic + sedimentary rocks; led to discovery of PLATE TECTONICS + SEAFLOOR SPREADING (Harry Hess, Vine-Matthews-Morley, 1960s). CONSEQUENCES of Earth's field: (1) DEFLECTS solar wind + cosmic rays into VAN ALLEN BELTS (protects biosphere from radiation); without it, atmosphere + water would strip (like Mars did 4 Ga ago when its dynamo stopped). (2) AURORAE BOREALIS + AUSTRALIS — solar wind particles funneled to magnetic poles, excite atmospheric atoms → glow green (O), red (O), pink (N). (3) NAVIGATION — magnetic compass, bird migration + turtle navigation use magnetic field. (4) RADIO communication — ionosphere + magnetic field reflect radio waves. GEOMAGNETIC STORMS — solar CMEs disturb field; can cause aurora at low latitudes, knock out satellites + power grids (1989 Quebec blackout). SPACE WEATHER monitored by agencies. DRIFT ~55 km/yr; Magnetic N pole currently in Arctic Ocean near Siberia; poles have REVERSED multiple times in history.

cards.front:
A TRANSFORMER works on the principle of:

(A) Static electricity
(B) MUTUAL ELECTROMAGNETIC INDUCTION
(C) Ohm's law alone
(D) Hall effect
cards.back:
(B) MUTUAL ELECTROMAGNETIC INDUCTION

Electricity & Magnetism — TRANSFORMER — static electrical device that TRANSFERS ELECTRICAL ENERGY between two circuits via ELECTROMAGNETIC INDUCTION. Can step UP or step DOWN voltage (works only for AC, not DC). INVENTED by WILLIAM STANLEY (1885, USA), based on Michael Faraday + Joseph Henry's discoveries. STRUCTURE: (1) PRIMARY COIL (input); (2) SECONDARY COIL (output); (3) LAMINATED IRON CORE (soft iron, laminated to reduce eddy current losses). Windings insulated. PRINCIPLE: AC in primary creates OSCILLATING MAGNETIC FLUX in core → flux links secondary coil → induces EMF in secondary (Faraday's law). Voltage RATIO = TURNS RATIO: V_s / V_p = N_s / N_p. Ideal transformer: power conserved (P_p = P_s): V_p × I_p = V_s × I_s. STEP-UP: more turns on secondary → higher output voltage. STEP-DOWN: fewer turns on secondary → lower output voltage. LOSSES (real transformers 95-99% efficient): (1) COPPER LOSSES (I²R in windings, reduce by thicker wire). (2) IRON LOSSES: (a) Hysteresis losses (reduce with soft iron core); (b) EDDY CURRENT LOSSES (reduce with laminated core + silicon steel). (3) FLUX leakage. (4) Skin effect at HV. USES of TRANSFORMERS: (1) POWER TRANSMISSION — step-up at generation (11 kV → 220/400/765 kV for long-distance transmission, reduces I²R losses); step-down at distribution (400 kV → 33 kV → 11 kV → 230/415 V). Transformers at every substation. (2) ELECTRONICS — step-down transformers in chargers, AC adapters, doorbell transformers. (3) WELDING — high current, low voltage. (4) X-ray machines, induction furnaces, ignition coils of cars. WHY AC, NOT DC: transformers work ONLY with CHANGING flux (AC inherently); DC does not produce changing flux (unless chopped by electronics). AC's advantage in distribution = easy voltage transformation. TRANSMISSION: AC (3-phase, 50 Hz in India, 60 Hz USA) dominates; HVDC (High Voltage DC) now common for LONG-distance point-to-point transmission (lower losses, no reactive power issues) — India has 7+ HVDC links (Rihand-Dadri, Champa-Kurukshetra, Raigarh-Pugalur etc.). TATAR VS EDISON 'War of Currents' (1880s-90s) — Tesla's AC won over Edison's DC for distribution (Niagara Falls power station 1895, Westinghouse). INDIAN POWER: 11 kV, 33 kV, 66 kV, 132 kV, 220 kV, 400 kV, 765 kV, ±800 kV HVDC, ±1,200 kV UHVAC (experimental). Household supply: 230V RMS (325V peak) AC at 50 Hz single-phase + 400V 3-phase for industries. AC primary generates changing flux; secondary coil (different turns) produces transformed voltage per turn ratio.

cards.front:
An ELECTRIC MOTOR converts:

(A) Sound to electricity
(B) ELECTRICAL ENERGY to MECHANICAL energy
(C) Heat to electricity
(D) Light to mechanical motion
cards.back:
(B) ELECTRICAL ENERGY to MECHANICAL energy

Electricity & Magnetism — ELECTRIC MOTOR — converts ELECTRICAL ENERGY to MECHANICAL energy (rotational). Inverse of GENERATOR. Based on PRINCIPLE that a current-carrying CONDUCTOR in a MAGNETIC FIELD experiences a FORCE (F = IL × B, vector form). FLEMING'S LEFT HAND RULE (for motors): thumb = Motion (force), forefinger = (magnetic) Field, middle = Current; arranged mutually perpendicular (left hand). Thumb → force on wire. BASIC DC MOTOR: rectangular coil (armature) pivoted in magnetic field (permanent magnet or field coil); current fed via commutator + brushes; current direction reverses every half turn → torque always in same direction → continuous rotation. TYPES of MOTORS: (1) DC MOTORS — commutator-based; subdivided into (a) series-wound (high starting torque; traction — old trains); (b) shunt-wound (constant speed); (c) compound; (d) permanent magnet (PMDC). Used in battery-operated devices, cars (starter), toys. (2) AC INDUCTION MOTORS — Tesla's invention 1887; most common industrial motor worldwide. Rotor inductively coupled to rotating magnetic field of stator (no brushes). Subdivided: squirrel-cage (simple, cheap, robust, widely used in fans, pumps, compressors) + wound-rotor (slip-ring, for high-torque start). (3) SYNCHRONOUS MOTORS — rotor locks to rotating field frequency; constant speed regardless of load; used in clocks (till quartz replaced them), generators, high-precision drives. (4) STEPPER MOTORS — rotate in discrete steps; used in printers, CNC, robotics. (5) BRUSHLESS DC (BLDC) — permanent magnet rotor, electronic commutation; quieter, more efficient; cars, drones, e-bikes, fans. (6) SERVO MOTORS — precise position control; robotics, industrial automation. FLEMING'S RIGHT HAND RULE (for generators): thumb = motion, forefinger = field, middle = induced current (right hand). Mnemonic: motor = left, generator = right. GENERATOR / DYNAMO — converts MECHANICAL → ELECTRICAL; based on FARADAY'S LAW of electromagnetic induction (changing flux through coil → EMF). Power plants (thermal, hydro, nuclear, wind) use generators to produce electricity. DC generators = dynamos; AC generators = alternators. ELECTRIC VEHICLES (EV) use motors (typically AC synchronous PM or BLDC) + BATTERIES instead of ICE + petrol. Modern EV motors reach 97%+ efficiency (vs ICE engines ~25%). Regenerative braking recovers kinetic energy back to battery. INDIA EV push: FAME-II subsidy, state EV policies, PM-Drive scheme 2024, Tata Nexon EV, Mahindra eVerito, Ola + Ather e-scooters, Atto 3 MG, + growth expected 30% EV by 2030. current-carrying coil in magnetic field experiences force (Fleming's LEFT HAND rule).

cards.front:
ELECTROMAGNETIC WAVES travel in VACUUM at a speed of:

(A) 340 m/s (sound)
(B) 3 × 10⁸ m/s (speed of LIGHT in vacuum, c = 299,792,458 m/s exactly — defines the metre); all EM waves (radio to gamma) share this speed
(C) 30,000 km/s
(D) 1 m/s
cards.back:
(B) 3 × 10⁸ m/s (speed of LIGHT in vacuum, c = 299,792,458 m/s exactly — defines the metre); all EM waves (radio to gamma) share this speed

Electricity & Magnetism — SPEED OF LIGHT (c) in VACUUM = 299,792,458 METRES/SECOND exactly (defined, not measured, since 1983 SI redefinition — metre is defined as the distance light travels in 1/299,792,458 s). Approximately 3 × 10⁸ m/s = 300,000 km/s = 186,000 miles/s. PROPERTIES: (1) FASTEST possible speed in universe (per Einstein's special relativity 1905). (2) SAME in ALL INERTIAL frames (Michelson-Morley experiment 1887 disproved aether; Einstein axiom). (3) Same speed for ALL EM waves in vacuum — radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, UV, X-rays, gamma rays. (4) SLOWER in media — refractive index n = c/v > 1 for ordinary media. Water n≈1.33, glass ~1.5, diamond ~2.4. Cherenkov radiation = particles exceeding c/n in medium (like blue glow in nuclear reactors). ELECTROMAGNETIC SPECTRUM (in order of INCREASING frequency / DECREASING wavelength): (1) RADIO WAVES — λ > 1m, used in AM/FM radio, TV, mobile (GSM, 4G, 5G). ELF, VLF, LF, MF, HF, VHF, UHF. (2) MICROWAVES — λ 1m-1mm; satellite, radar, mobile (cm-wave, mm-wave 5G), MICROWAVE OVEN (2.45 GHz heats water via dipole rotation). (3) INFRARED (IR) — λ 1mm-700nm; heat radiation, night-vision, remote controls, fiber-optic communication (1.3/1.55 μm windows in silica glass). (4) VISIBLE LIGHT — λ 700-400 nm; ROYGBIV (Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Blue, Indigo, Violet); our eyes evolved for this band (Sun's peak emission). (5) ULTRAVIOLET (UV) — λ 400-10 nm; sunburn, vitamin D synthesis, sterilisation, forensics; UV-A/B/C. Ozone absorbs UV-C + most UV-B. (6) X-RAYS — λ 10nm-0.01nm; medical imaging (Röntgen 1895), security screening, CT scans. (7) GAMMA RAYS — λ < 0.01nm; nuclear decay, gamma-ray bursts (most energetic events in universe), radiotherapy. ENERGY: E = hν = hc/λ (Planck's constant h = 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ Js) — higher frequency = higher photon energy; gamma + X-rays are ionising (can damage DNA → cancer); UV above 290nm as well; visible + lower = non-ionising. MEASUREMENT of c: (1) ROEMER (1676) via Jupiter's moons — first measurement. (2) FIZEAU + FOUCAULT (1850s) — rotating mirror. (3) MICHELSON (1920s) — interferometer. (4) Modern: cavity resonance, laser interferometry. EVENTUALLY FIXED by definition 1983. Light takes: 8.3 min from Sun, 1.3 s from Moon, 4.2 yrs from Proxima Centauri, 2.5 MY from Andromeda.

cards.front:
MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING (MRI) uses:

(A) X-rays
(B) STRONG MAGNETIC FIELD (1.5-7 Tesla) + RADIO WAVES to image soft tissues; NO ionising radiation; based on NMR principle
(C) Gamma rays
(D) Ultrasound
cards.back:
(B) STRONG MAGNETIC FIELD (1.5-7 Tesla) + RADIO WAVES to image soft tissues; NO ionising radiation; based on NMR principle

Electricity & Magnetism — MRI (MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING) — non-invasive medical imaging technique. PRINCIPLE: NUCLEAR MAGNETIC RESONANCE (NMR) — discovered by FELIX BLOCH + EDWARD PURCELL (Nobel Physics 1952). HOW IT WORKS: (1) PATIENT placed in STRONG MAGNETIC FIELD — typical clinical 1.5 T or 3 T (2100-4500× Earth's field); research MRI up to 10.5 T (Minnesota, 2023); 11.7 T INUMAC (France, 2019). (2) Hydrogen NUCLEI (protons — abundant in water + fat in body, 63% of body H₂O) ALIGN with magnetic field (most parallel, some anti-parallel). (3) RADIO FREQUENCY (RF) pulse at the LARMOR FREQUENCY (42.58 MHz/Tesla for proton; so 63.9 MHz for 1.5T, 127.7 MHz for 3T) causes protons to ABSORB energy + tip out of alignment. (4) When RF pulse off, protons RELAX BACK to alignment, emitting RF signal (T1 + T2 relaxation times — tissue-specific; differ for fat vs water vs muscle vs tumor). (5) Signal + position mapped via GRADIENT COILS + computer Fourier reconstruction = IMAGE. ADVANTAGES over CT/X-RAY: (a) NO IONISING RADIATION (safe for repeated use + pregnant women); (b) SUPERB SOFT TISSUE contrast — brain, spinal cord, muscles, cartilage, organs; (c) MULTIPLANAR imaging (any slice orientation); (d) FUNCTIONAL MRI (fMRI) can see brain activity via BOLD signal. DISADVANTAGES: (a) EXPENSIVE (machines $1-3 million; scan $200-2000); (b) SLOW scans 30-60 min; (c) NOISY (gradient coil banging); (d) Claustrophobic bore; (e) CONTRAINDICATED in patients with metal implants (pacemakers, some clips, cochlear implants — though MR-conditional implants increasingly available); (f) less good for bones (use CT). NOBEL PRIZES: Medicine 2003 to Paul LAUTERBUR + Peter MANSFIELD for MRI development (1970s). Chemistry 2002 to Kurt WÜTHRICH + Fenn + Tanaka for NMR application to biomolecules. FUNCTIONAL MRI (fMRI) — measures blood oxygenation level (BOLD); maps brain activity; core neuroscience tool since 1990s. OTHER IMAGING (India + world): (1) X-RAY / RADIOGRAPHY (1895, Röntgen) — bones, chest, dental; (2) CT / CAT SCAN (1971, Hounsfield + Cormack, Nobel 1979) — cross-sectional X-ray; brain injuries, cancers. (3) ULTRASOUND — sonar waves; pregnancy, abdomen. (4) PET SCAN (Positron Emission Tomography) — radioactive tracers; cancer staging + brain + heart. (5) SPECT — like PET but cheaper isotopes. (6) NUCLEAR bone scan, thyroid scan. (7) Endoscopy — cameras through openings. INDIA has ~5,000 MRI machines (USA ~13,000), radiology infrastructure still inadequate for 140 crore people; telemedicine + AI reading help.

cards.front:
A COMPASS needle always points approximately:

(A) East-West
(B) NORTH-SOUTH
(C) Upward
(D) Randomly
cards.back:
(B) NORTH-SOUTH

Electricity & Magnetism — COMPASS — freely-pivoting MAGNETIZED NEEDLE that aligns with Earth's MAGNETIC FIELD. Needle's N-POLE (north-seeking pole) points towards GEOGRAPHIC NORTH — which is technically near the MAGNETIC SOUTH pole (unlike poles attract; the 'North Magnetic Pole' is actually the S-pole of Earth's magnetic dipole). INVENTED: in China, between 200 BCE-100 CE using LODESTONE (natural magnetite Fe₃O₄ — 'magnesian stone'). Used first for fortune-telling (feng shui), then navigation by 1000 CE (Song Dynasty). Spread to Europe by 12th c. (Alexander Neckam 1190 described it). Enabled AGE OF EXPLORATION — Columbus, Vasco da Gama, Magellan. EARTH's FIELD — produces DECLINATION (angle between magnetic + true N) + INCLINATION (angle with horizontal). Declination varies by location + over time (updated in World Magnetic Model). For navigation, maps give local magnetic declination to convert compass → true bearing. TYPES of COMPASS: (1) MAGNETIC compass — traditional, uses Earth's field; cheap, no power; but affected by local magnetic anomalies + interference. (2) GYROCOMPASS — uses gyroscope + Earth's rotation; finds TRUE NORTH (no declination); used in ships + aircraft; not affected by magnetic field but needs power. (3) GPS compass — computes heading from GPS speed/vector. (4) SOLID STATE electronic (magnetometer) — in smartphones, drones, AR/VR; Hall effect or magnetoresistive sensors. USES of COMPASS: (1) NAVIGATION — maritime, aviation, hiking, military; (2) SURVEYING + mapping; (3) alignment of solar panels + dishes; (4) Islamic prayer direction (Qibla to Mecca); (5) Feng Shui; (6) Search + rescue; (7) Mobile apps (Google Maps arrow, Pokémon Go direction). BIRD + ANIMAL MAGNETORECEPTION — many animals can sense Earth's magnetic field: HOMING pigeons, MONARCH butterflies (annual 3000-km migration), sea TURTLES (return to natal beaches after decades), SHARKS, SALMON, bees, bats. Mechanism debated: (a) MAGNETITE crystals (in beak of pigeons, trout noses); (b) CRYPTOCHROME proteins in eye (quantum biology — radical pair mechanism). Research frontier. HUMANS may also have weak magnetoreception — Caltech study 2019 showed brain responses but no conscious perception. CUSTOM ETHICS: cattle + deer face NS axis while grazing (Begall et al. 2008). MAGNETIC STORMS can make compasses erratic; sailors knew this. ASTRONAUTS: compasses don't work in space (no Earth magnetic field beyond Van Allen belts); use gyros + star trackers.

cards.front:
MAGLEV (magnetic levitation) trains utilise:

(A) Steam power
(B) MAGNETIC FIELDS to LIFT + PROPEL trains without physical contact; zero friction on wheels; Japan Chuo Shinkansen achieved 603 km/h
(C) Superconducting cables buried underground
(D) Electrostatic charge
cards.back:
(B) MAGNETIC FIELDS to LIFT + PROPEL trains without physical contact; zero friction on wheels; Japan Chuo Shinkansen achieved 603 km/h

Electricity & Magnetism — MAGLEV (MAGNETIC LEVITATION) — transport technology that uses MAGNETIC FORCES to LIFT + PROPEL vehicles WITHOUT physical contact with the track. Advantages: (1) NO friction from wheels (only air resistance); (2) HIGH SPEEDS (500+ km/h); (3) Smooth, quiet ride; (4) Low maintenance (no wheel/track wear). Disadvantages: (1) COSTLY infrastructure ($20-50M/km); (2) Specialized tracks; (3) Power-intensive. TYPES: (1) EMS (Electromagnetic Suspension) — ELECTROMAGNETS on train attracted UPWARD to iron rails; active control (feedback) since unstable by Earnshaw's theorem; e.g., TRANSRAPID (Germany — Shanghai Maglev; bankrupt). (2) EDS (Electrodynamic Suspension) — SUPERCONDUCTING magnets on train + induced currents in track coils REPEL (Lenz's law); more stable at high speed; Japan's SCMaglev (Chuo Shinkansen). (3) INDUCTRACK — permanent magnet arrays (Halbach) on train + passive coils in track; no superconductor needed; new approach. (4) LINEAR INDUCTION MOTOR for propulsion — stator along track, train acts as rotor; interaction with rail coils + train magnets provides thrust. OPERATIONAL MAGLEV LINES (world): (1) SHANGHAI MAGLEV (China, 30 km airport line, 431 km/h top; operational 2004). (2) CHUO SHINKANSEN Maglev (Japan, Tokyo-Nagoya under construction; 505 km/h design speed; record 603 km/h in 2015 manned test). (3) LINIMO (Japan, 9 km commuter line, 100 km/h). (4) Incheon Airport Maglev (S. Korea, 6 km, 110 km/h). (5) CHANGSHA Maglev (China, 18.5 km, 100 km/h). (6) BEIJING S1 maglev line (10 km). INDIA: proposals + studies for Mumbai-Nagpur, Mumbai-Delhi, Mumbai-Pune etc.; MUMBAI-AHMEDABAD bullet train (high-speed rail, not maglev — Shinkansen tech) under construction (Japanese collab, due 2028). No operational maglev in India yet. HYPERLOOP — proposed ultrafast (1000+ km/h) tube transport by Elon Musk (2013 white paper); combines maglev + vacuum tube. Virgin Hyperloop tested 2020 (472 km/h). Several hyperloop companies (Hardt, Zeleros, TransPod, Hyperloop TT) in development; Virgin Hyperloop scaled back 2022. Maharashtra + others explored Pune-Mumbai hyperloop (now on hold). HIGH-SPEED RAIL (HSR) in India: MUMBAI-AHMEDABAD (508 km, 320 km/h, 12 stations, due 2028 — Japan International Cooperation funded ₹1.08 lakh crore) — first bullet train. Future corridors: Delhi-Varanasi, Delhi-Ahmedabad, Mumbai-Hyderabad, Chennai-Bengaluru-Mysuru, Delhi-Amritsar, etc.

cards.front:
The SI unit of MAGNETIC FIELD STRENGTH (Magnetic Flux Density) is:

(A) Gauss
(B) TESLA (T)
(C) Newton
(D) Weber
cards.back:
(B) TESLA (T)

Electricity & Magnetism — MAGNETIC FIELD / FLUX DENSITY (B) — SI unit TESLA (T). NAMED AFTER NIKOLA TESLA (1856-1943), Serbian-American inventor + electrical genius; adopted 1960 by CGPM. DEFINITION: 1 T = 1 WEBER per square METRE (Wb/m²) = 1 kg/(A·s²) = 1 V·s/m². Alternative definition: 1 T is magnetic field that exerts 1 NEWTON force on a 1-metre wire carrying 1 AMPERE perpendicular to it (F = BIL). CGS unit: GAUSS (G); 1 T = 10,000 G. Earth's field ~25-65 µT = 0.25-0.65 G. TYPICAL MAGNETIC FIELD STRENGTHS: (1) Neurons' magnetic field (MEG): femtotesla (10⁻¹⁵ T). (2) Intergalactic: nT (10⁻⁹). (3) Earth's surface: ~30-60 µT. (4) Refrigerator magnet: 1-5 mT (10⁻³ T). (5) Surface of sunspot: 0.15 T. (6) Neodymium (NdFeB) magnet: 1-1.4 T. (7) Typical MRI: 1.5-7 T. (8) Research MRI: up to 11.7 T. (9) LHC dipole magnets: 8.3 T. (10) Strongest continuous lab magnet: 45 T (National High Magnetic Field Lab, Florida). (11) Strongest pulsed: ~1,200 T (Japan, milliseconds). (12) Neutron star surface: 10⁸-10¹⁰ T; magnetar (extreme neutron star): 10¹⁰-10¹¹ T (most magnetic objects in universe; 1 T on magnetar surface would distort atoms). RELATED MAGNETIC SI UNITS: (1) WEBER (Wb) = MAGNETIC FLUX = T·m² = V·s. Named after Wilhelm Eduard Weber. Flux Φ = B × A (for uniform field perpendicular to area A). (2) HENRY (H) = INDUCTANCE = V·s/A = Wb/A. Named after Joseph Henry. (3) AMPERE-TURN = MAGNETOMOTIVE FORCE. (4) Reluctance (R) = A·turns/Wb. GAUSS WAS THE CGS UNIT — 100 years of use (1830s-1960s). Many practitioners still prefer Gauss for small fields (e.g., Earth's). 'GAUSSMETER' still common in testing. MAGNETIC FIELD INTENSITY (H) — separate quantity; H = B/μ (in medium); SI unit = Ampere/metre (A/m); measures field without magnetic response of material. PERMEABILITY (μ) of free space (μ₀) = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A ≈ 1.257 × 10⁻⁶ exact value (was exact pre-2019 SI redefinition; now measured with small uncertainty). Relative permeability μ_r = μ/μ₀; for iron 200-5000; soft iron for transformer cores. PROGRESSION: magnets get stronger — NdFeB (1984) + SmCo best permanent magnets; superconducting coils (NbTi, Nb3Sn) enable high-field MRI + accelerators + fusion (ITER's 13 T toroidal field coils — world's largest superconducting magnet). named after Nikola Tesla; 1 T = Wb/m² = kg/(A·s²); CGS unit Gauss, 1 T = 10,000 G.

cards.front:
If a bar magnet is broken into two pieces, each piece will:

(A) Become a single isolated north or south pole
(B) Behave as a complete magnet with both N and S poles
(C) Lose its magnetism completely on breaking
(D) Reverse the original direction of its magnetic field
cards.back:
(B) Behave as a complete magnet with both N and S poles

Electricity & Magnetism — Magnetic monopoles have NEVER been observed. Every piece of a broken magnet becomes a smaller bar magnet with its own N and S poles. Repeating the cut yields more, smaller magnets — fundamental property of matter at the dipole level. Distractor 1 = monopole, hypothetical / unobserved. Distractor 3 — breaking does not destroy domain alignment in ferromagnets. Distractor 4 — direction does not flip.
cards.option1: Become a single isolated north or south pole
cards.option2: Lose its magnetism completely on breaking
cards.option3: Reverse the original direction of its magnetic field

cards.front:
Magnetic field lines, by convention, run:

(A) From the south pole to the north pole outside the magnet
(B) From north pole to south pole outside the magnet
(C) Always in straight horizontal lines through the magnet
(D) From the centre of the magnet outward to infinity
cards.back:
(B) From north pole to south pole outside the magnet

Electricity & Magnetism — Outside a magnet, field lines emerge from N pole and enter S pole; inside, they go S → N (forming closed loops). Lines never cross. Density of lines = strength of field. Distractor 1 reverses direction (a common confusion). Distractor 3 — lines curve, they don't go straight. Distractor 4 — lines form closed loops, do not go to infinity.
cards.option1: From the south pole to the north pole outside the magnet
cards.option2: Always in straight horizontal lines through the magnet
cards.option3: From the centre of the magnet outward to infinity

cards.front:
A freely-suspended magnetic needle aligns roughly along the north-south direction because:

(A) Earth has its own magnetic field acting on the needle
(B) Earth's gravity pulls the needle toward true geographic north
(C) The needle's mass is greatest at one of its ends
(D) Wind currents blow the needle into a fixed direction
cards.back:
(A) Earth has its own magnetic field acting on the needle

Electricity & Magnetism — Earth behaves like a giant bar magnet (slightly tilted from its rotation axis). The magnetic needle aligns with Earth's magnetic field lines. The needle's geographic 'north' end (called the N-pole) actually points to Earth's MAGNETIC SOUTH POLE (which is near geographic north) — that's why opposite poles attract. Distractor 2 — gravity acts vertically downward, not horizontally toward north. Distractor 3 — mass distribution is irrelevant for orientation. Distractor 4 — wind has no role indoors.
cards.option1: Earth's gravity pulls the needle toward true geographic north
cards.option2: The needle's mass is greatest at one of its ends
cards.option3: Wind currents blow the needle into a fixed direction

cards.front:
An electromagnet is generally constructed by:

(A) Permanently magnetising a hard steel cylinder
(B) Winding insulated wire around a soft iron core
(C) Heating a piece of iron near a permanent magnet
(D) Cooling iron filings with liquid nitrogen at low temperature
cards.back:
(B) Winding insulated wire around a soft iron core

Electricity & Magnetism — Electromagnet — current through a coil produces a magnetic field; placing a soft-iron core inside concentrates and amplifies the field by orders of magnitude. Removing current → field disappears (key advantage over permanent magnets — controllable). Used in electric bells, relays, MRI scanners, scrap-yard cranes, motors. SOFT iron is preferred over hard steel because soft iron loses magnetism quickly when current is off (low retentivity); steel retains residual magnetism, making the device less switchable.

cards.option2: Heating a piece of iron near a permanent magnet
cards.option3: Cooling iron filings with liquid nitrogen at low temperature

cards.front:
Materials like iron, cobalt, and nickel that are STRONGLY ATTRACTED by magnets are classified as:

(A) Diamagnetic — like copper, water and bismuth
(B) Ferromagnetic — strongly attracted, can be magnetised
(C) Paramagnetic — weakly attracted, like aluminium
(D) Non-magnetic — completely unaffected by any field
cards.back:
(B) Ferromagnetic — strongly attracted, can be magnetised

Electricity & Magnetism — FERROMAGNETIC: iron, cobalt, nickel, gadolinium — domains align with external field; can be permanently magnetised; strong attraction. PARAMAGNETIC: aluminium, magnesium, oxygen, platinum — weak attraction; doesn't retain magnetism. DIAMAGNETIC: copper, water, gold, bismuth, silver — slight repulsion (induce opposing field). The Curie temperature is the point above which a ferromagnet becomes paramagnetic.

cards.option3: Non-magnetic — completely unaffected by any field

cards.front:
Earth's magnetic field protects us from harmful solar wind. The region of space carved out by this field is called the:

(A) Stratosphere — a layer rich in ozone gas
(B) Magnetosphere — extends thousands of km outward
(C) Ionosphere — important for radio-wave reflection
(D) Heliosphere — a region centred on the Sun itself
cards.back:
(B) Magnetosphere — extends thousands of km outward

Electricity & Magnetism — MAGNETOSPHERE — Earth's magnetic field forms a teardrop-shaped cavity in the solar wind, deflecting charged particles. Charged particles trapped in this region form the Van Allen radiation belts. When solar particles do enter at the polar cusps, they cause AURORAE (Northern + Southern Lights). Distractor 1 = atmospheric layer with ozone. Distractor 3 = ionised upper atmosphere. Distractor 4 = the Sun's own magnetic-field bubble.

cards.option3: Heliosphere — a region centred on the Sun itself

cards.front:
Above which temperature does a ferromagnet (e.g., iron) lose its ferromagnetism and behave only as a paramagnet?

(A) The Boyle temperature, around 27 °C
(B) The Curie temperature, ~770 °C for iron
(C) The Boiling point of iron, around 2860 °C
(D) The Critical temperature of liquefaction
cards.back:
(B) The Curie temperature, ~770 °C for iron

Electricity & Magnetism — Curie temperature (after Pierre Curie). At this point, thermal agitation overcomes the alignment of magnetic domains; the material loses spontaneous magnetisation. Iron: 770 °C. Cobalt: 1115 °C (highest of pure elements). Nickel: 358 °C. Above Curie temp, ferromagnet → paramagnet. Used in some thermal switches, electrical cookers (rice cookers detect end-of-cooking when bottom heats past Curie point of a sensor magnet). Distractor 1 — Boyle temp is a gas-law concept. Distractor 3 — boiling point is much higher and unrelated. Distractor 4 — Critical temp is for fluid liquefaction, different physics.
cards.option2: The Boiling point of iron, around 2860 °C

cards.front:
A freely suspended magnetic needle always comes to rest pointing approximately:

(A) East to west
(B) North to south
(C) Towards the Sun
(D) Straight down
cards.back:
(B) North to south

Electricity & Magnetism — A suspended magnet aligns with Earth's magnetic field, which runs roughly north-south. The magnet's 'N-seeking' pole points to the geographic North (near which lies Earth's magnetic South Pole — because opposite poles attract). The small angular difference between geographic and magnetic north is called 'magnetic declination'. Mariner's compasses exploit this alignment.

cards.front:
The magnetic north pole of the Earth is located near the:

(A) Geographic north pole
(B) Geographic south pole
(C) Equator
(D) Tropic of Cancer
cards.back:
(B) Geographic south pole

Electricity & Magnetism — Counter-intuitive but true — Earth's north-seeking compass pole is attracted to the Arctic, so the magnetic S-pole of Earth is near the geographic North Pole, and Earth's magnetic N-pole is near the geographic South Pole. Unlike poles attract. The magnetic poles wander and have flipped many times in geological history (records preserved in cooled lava).

cards.front:
A temporary magnet — produced only when electric current flows through a coil around an iron core — is called an:

(A) Permanent magnet
(B) Electromagnet
(C) Diamagnet
(D) Paramagnet
cards.back:
(B) Electromagnet

Electricity & Magnetism — An electromagnet — coil + soft iron core — behaves as a strong magnet only while current flows, and loses magnetism when switched off. Used in electric bells, motors, MRI machines, magnetic cranes lifting scrap. Permanent magnets (alloys like neodymium-iron-boron) retain magnetism indefinitely. Diamagnets are weakly repelled by external fields (copper, bismuth). Paramagnets weakly align with them (aluminium).

Diamagnets are weakly repelled by external fields (copper, bismuth). Paramagnets weakly align with them (aluminium).

cards.front:
Which of the following materials is ferromagnetic (strongly magnetic)?

(A) Copper
(B) Iron
(C) Aluminium
(D) Wood
cards.back:
(B) Iron

Electricity & Magnetism — Iron — and its siblings nickel and cobalt, plus some rare earths (gadolinium) — are ferromagnetic; they can be strongly magnetised. Copper is diamagnetic (weakly repelled). Aluminium is paramagnetic (weakly attracted). Wood is essentially non-magnetic. The mnemonic 'iron, nickel, cobalt + few rare earths' covers the room-temperature ferromagnets encountered in everyday physics.

cards.front:
The SI unit of magnetic flux density (also called the strength of the magnetic field) is the:

(A) Ampere
(B) Tesla
(C) Weber
(D) Henry
cards.back:
(B) Tesla

Electricity & Magnetism — Tesla (T) is the SI unit of magnetic flux density — named after Nikola Tesla. Earth's field ≈ 5 × 10⁻⁵ T; a fridge magnet ≈ 10⁻² T; MRI machines ≈ 1-3 T. Weber (Wb) is the unit of total magnetic flux (through a surface). Henry (H) is the unit of inductance. Ampere is the unit of electric current.

cards.front:
Hans Christian Oersted's famous 1820 experiment showed that:

(A) A magnet exerts a force on another magnet
(B) A current-carrying wire produces a magnetic field around it
(C) Light has the same speed in all media
(D) Objects fall at the same rate in a vacuum
cards.back:
(B) A current-carrying wire produces a magnetic field around it

Electricity & Magnetism — Oersted (1820) found that a compass needle near a current-carrying wire deflects — showing that electricity and magnetism are linked. This single observation founded the subject of electromagnetism. It was followed in 1831 by Faraday's discovery that a changing magnetic field can induce an electric current (electromagnetic induction) — the basis for generators and transformers.

cards.option2: Light has the same speed in all media
cards.option3: Objects fall at the same rate in a vacuum

cards.front:
The rule used to find the direction of the magnetic field around a current-carrying straight conductor is:

(A) Fleming's left-hand rule
(B) Right-hand thumb rule
(C) Fleming's right-hand rule
(D) Lenz's rule
cards.back:
(B) Right-hand thumb rule

Electricity & Magnetism — Right-hand thumb rule (sometimes called Maxwell's / Ampere's rule) — hold the wire in the right hand with the thumb pointing along the direction of the current; the curl of the fingers gives the direction of the magnetic field lines around the wire. Fleming's left-hand rule — force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field (motor rule). Fleming's right-hand rule — direction of induced current in a conductor moving in a field (generator rule). Lenz's law fixes the direction of induced current (opposes the change causing it).

Fleming's right-hand rule — direction of induced current in a conductor moving in a field (generator rule). Lenz's law fixes the direction of induced current (opposes the change causing it).

cards.front:
Like poles of two magnets:

(A) Attract
(B) Repel
(C) Neither attract nor repel
(D) First attract, then repel
cards.back:
(B) Repel

Electricity & Magnetism — Like poles REPEL, unlike poles ATTRACT. This is the basic law of magnetism (Gilbert). Gauss's law for magnetism says magnetic monopoles don't exist — N and S always come together.

(A) Geographic North Pole (exactly)
(B) Geographic South Pole

cards.back:

cards.front:
The principle on which an ELECTRIC GENERATOR works is:

(A) Ohm's law
(B) Electromagnetic induction
(C) Coulomb's law
(D) Gauss's law
cards.back:
(B) Electromagnetic induction

Electricity & Magnetism — Generator — rotates a coil in a magnetic field → changing flux → induced EMF per Faraday's law (1831). Converts mechanical → electrical energy. Motor is the reverse (electrical → mechanical) based on the same underlying physics but force on current-carrying conductor.

The SI unit of MAGNETIC flux is:

cards.front:
The direction of an INDUCED current is given by:

(A) Ohm's law
(B) Lenz's law
(C) Ampere's circuital law
(D) Newton's third law
cards.back:
(B) Lenz's law

Electricity & Magnetism — Lenz's law — induced current flows in a direction such that it OPPOSES the change in magnetic flux that caused it. Consequence of energy conservation. Manifested as the 'minus' sign in Faraday's law: ε = −dΦ/dt. induced current opposes the change causing it.

The speed of light (and of all EM waves) in vacuum is approximately:

(A) 3 × 10⁵ m/s
(B) 3 × 10⁸ m/s

cards.front:
LASER stands for:

(A) Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation
(B) Light Activation by Spontaneous Emission of Rays
(C) Linear Amplification by Steady Emission of Radiation
(D) Light Amplification by Storage of Electric Rays
cards.back:
(A) Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation

Modern Physics — LASER = Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation. Predicted theoretically by Einstein (1917) — concept of stimulated emission. First built by Theodore MAIMAN (1960) using ruby crystal. Laser light has 4 special properties: COHERENT (all photons in phase), MONOCHROMATIC (single wavelength), DIRECTIONAL (very narrow beam), INTENSE (concentrated energy).

cards.front:
The KEY PRINCIPLE behind laser action is:

(A) Spontaneous emission from excited atoms
(B) Stimulated emission from excited atoms
(C) Photoelectric effect from metal surface
(D) Compton scattering from charged particle
cards.back:
(B) Stimulated emission from excited atoms

Modern Physics — STIMULATED EMISSION (Einstein 1917): an incoming photon of right energy hits an atom in EXCITED state → atom emits an IDENTICAL photon (same frequency, phase, direction). This amplifies the light. Requires POPULATION INVERSION — more atoms in excited state than ground state (achieved by 'pumping' — optical, electrical, chemical). Distractor 1 = how lamps work (random). Distractor 3 = Einstein's photoelectric effect (different phenomenon).

(B) Of a single specific wavelength
(C) Visible to the human eye easily

HOLOGRAPHY (3D image storage on 2D film) was made possible by which technology?

(A) Ordinary white-light photography process
(B) Coherent laser light recording the wavefront
(C) Electron microscopy at very high resolution
(D) X-ray imaging of internal structure layers
cards.back:

Modern Physics — HOLOGRAPHY — invented by Dennis GABOR (1947, Nobel 1971) in theory; made practical only after the invention of LASER. Used in: security on credit cards, currency notes, ID cards (Indian Rupee notes have holographic strip); art; data storage (research). Without laser's coherence, holograms can't form.

cards.front:
FIBRE-OPTIC COMMUNICATION (used for high-speed internet) relies on:

(A) Reflection of laser light off mirrors only
(B) Total internal reflection of laser pulses in fibre
(C) Refraction of light at lens surfaces only
(D) Diffraction of light passing through slits
cards.back:
(B) Total internal reflection of laser pulses in fibre

Modern Physics — Fibre-optic cables — thin glass/plastic strands that carry digital data as PULSES of LASER LIGHT. Principle: TOTAL INTERNAL REFLECTION (TIR) — when light hits the core-cladding boundary at angle > critical angle, it is totally reflected (no loss to outside). This lets light travel KILOMETRES with minimal attenuation. Faster + more bandwidth than copper. Underseas cables connect continents (~99% of intercontinental data flows via fibre). India's BharatNet aims to connect 250,000+ panchayats by fibre.

cards.front:
EINSTEIN's most FAMOUS equation E = mc² expresses:

(A) Energy proportional to volume
(B) MASS-ENERGY EQUIVALENCE
(C) Force equation only
(D) Gravity + light interaction
cards.back:
(B) MASS-ENERGY EQUIVALENCE

Modern Physics — E = mc² — most famous equation in physics; expresses MASS-ENERGY EQUIVALENCE. Formulated by ALBERT EINSTEIN (1905) in his paper 'Does the inertia of a body depend upon its energy content?' — one of 4 papers in his 1905 'MIRACLE YEAR' (ANNUS MIRABILIS): (1) Photoelectric effect (Nobel 1921); (2) Brownian motion (proof of atoms); (3) Special Relativity (E = mc²); (4) PhD thesis. MEANING: (1) MASS + ENERGY are INTERCHANGEABLE forms of the same thing. (2) c² = (3 × 10⁸)² = 9 × 10¹⁶ m²/s² — IMMENSE factor. (3) Tiny mass → HUGE energy. (4) 1 GRAM of mass = 9 × 10¹³ J = 25 million kWh = enough for a small town for year. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCES: (1) NUCLEAR FISSION — splitting heavy nuclei (U-235, Pu-239) releases energy because fragments have slightly less total mass than original (mass defect). 1 kg U-235 fission releases ~80 TJ (enough for ~30,000 homes for a year). (2) NUCLEAR FUSION — fusing light nuclei (H → He in stars) releases MUCH more energy per kg. The SUN converts ~4 million TONNES of mass to energy PER SECOND via p-p chain (solar output 3.8 × 10²⁶ W). (3) ANTIMATTER annihilation — 1 g each of matter + antimatter = 180 TJ (~ 40 kilotons of TNT). Most efficient energy conversion. (4) EXPLAINS why rest mass of atoms < sum of constituent nucleon masses (mass defect = binding energy). SPECIAL RELATIVITY — Einstein's 1905 theory. 2 POSTULATES: (1) Laws of physics SAME in all INERTIAL reference frames. (2) SPEED OF LIGHT in vacuum is SAME for ALL observers, regardless of motion of source or observer. CONSEQUENCES (all confirmed experimentally): (1) TIME DILATION — moving clocks tick SLOWER. Moving at 0.99c, time passes ~1/7. Twin paradox — 1 twin stays, 1 travels near-c returns younger. Cosmic ray muons' survival disproportionately long = time dilation in action. GPS satellites corrected for both Special + General Relativity effects. (2) LENGTH CONTRACTION — moving objects appear shorter along motion axis. (3) SIMULTANEITY is RELATIVE — events simultaneous in one frame not in another. (4) MASS INCREASE with velocity — relativistic mass (m = m₀/√(1-v²/c²)); at c, mass → infinity (hence c is speed limit). (5) MASS-ENERGY EQUIVALENCE (E² = (mc²)² + (pc)²; E = mc² when p=0 for rest). GENERAL RELATIVITY (1915) — gravity = spacetime curvature. Predictions: perihelion of Mercury, gravitational lensing (Eddington 1919), gravitational waves (LIGO 2015), black holes (M87* 2019), expanding universe (Hubble 1929), GPS corrections (38 µs/day), frame-dragging (Gravity Probe B). QUANTUM MECHANICS (1900-30s) + GENERAL RELATIVITY are two PILLARS of modern physics — both WELL-TESTED but INCOMPATIBLE at extreme conditions (Planck scales, singularities). Quest for QUANTUM GRAVITY / THEORY OF EVERYTHING (TOE): string theory, loop quantum gravity, causal dynamical triangulation — no winner yet. EINSTEIN's LIFE: Born Ulm Germany 1879; patent clerk Bern 1902-09; Zurich + Berlin professor; NOBEL 1921 (photoelectric effect, not relativity — too controversial at time); emigrated to USA 1933 (Nazi persecution — Einstein was Jewish); Princeton professor till 1955 death (age 76). Advocated nuclear weapons vs Nazis (Einstein-Szilard letter 1939 to FDR → Manhattan Project); later peace activist. Most famous image: tongue out (1951 birthday photo by Arthur Sasse). small mass can convert to HUGE energy (c² = 9 × 10¹⁶); basis of nuclear power + bombs + stars' energy.

cards.front:
The PHOTOELECTRIC EFFECT, explained by Einstein (Nobel 1921), demonstrated that LIGHT is:

(A) Only a wave
(B) PARTICLE-LIKE (as PHOTONS with energy E = hf) in addition to wave behaviour; foundational for QUANTUM mechanics + 'wave-particle duality'
(C) Only sound
(D) A type of magnetism
cards.back:
(B) PARTICLE-LIKE (as PHOTONS with energy E = hf) in addition to wave behaviour; foundational for QUANTUM mechanics + 'wave-particle duality'

Modern Physics — PHOTOELECTRIC EFFECT — when LIGHT hits a metal surface, it can EJECT ELECTRONS. Observed 1887 by HEINRICH HERTZ; quantitative study by PHILIPP LENARD (Nobel 1905). PUZZLE: classical wave theory of light PREDICTED: (a) any light frequency should eject electrons (intensity matters); (b) KE of ejected electrons should depend on INTENSITY. OBSERVATION: (a) BELOW a THRESHOLD FREQUENCY, NO electrons ejected regardless of intensity. (b) ABOVE threshold, electron KE depends on FREQUENCY (NOT intensity); intensity only affects NUMBER of electrons. (c) Emission is INSTANTANEOUS even for weak light. EINSTEIN's EXPLANATION (1905): LIGHT consists of DISCRETE PACKETS / QUANTA called PHOTONS; each photon has ENERGY E = hf (h = Planck constant, f = frequency). Light is 'PARTICLE-LIKE' + electron absorbs ONE photon at a time. If E_photon > WORK FUNCTION (φ — minimum energy to free electron from metal) → electron ejected with KE = hf - φ. Threshold frequency f₀ = φ/h. Nobel Prize 1921 for this (not relativity!). SIGNIFICANCE: (1) Cemented QUANTIZATION of light energy (extended Planck's 1900 blackbody quantization of thermal radiation). (2) Start of QUANTUM MECHANICS. (3) WAVE-PARTICLE DUALITY — light is BOTH wave + particle depending on experiment. Later extended to matter (DE BROGLIE 1924 — matter waves; confirmed by Davisson-Germer 1927 electron diffraction). (4) Technology — solar cells, photomultiplier tubes, photodetectors, digital cameras. QUANTUM MECHANICS — theory of atoms + molecules + subatomic particles. KEY DEVELOPMENTS: (1) PLANCK 1900 — blackbody radiation; energy quantized E = hf. Nobel 1918. (2) EINSTEIN 1905 — photoelectric effect. (3) RUTHERFORD 1911 — gold foil experiment → nuclear atom (alpha scattering; most atom empty space with dense nucleus). (4) BOHR 1913 — H atom model; electrons in quantized orbits; emit/absorb photons when jumping levels. Nobel 1922. (5) DE BROGLIE 1924 — matter waves; λ = h/p; Nobel 1929. (6) HEISENBERG 1925 — matrix mechanics; UNCERTAINTY PRINCIPLE (1927) — Δx·Δp ≥ ℏ/2; can't know position + momentum precisely simultaneously. Nobel 1932. (7) SCHRÖDINGER 1926 — WAVE equation; wavefunctions; probability amplitudes. Schrödinger's cat thought experiment (1935). Nobel 1933. (8) DIRAC 1928 — relativistic QM; predicted ANTIMATTER (positron discovered 1932); Dirac equation. Nobel 1933. (9) PAULI EXCLUSION PRINCIPLE (1925) — 2 electrons can't occupy same quantum state (key for atomic structure + periodic table). Nobel 1945. (10) BORN 1926 — probabilistic interpretation of wavefunction (Copenhagen interpretation). Nobel 1954. (11) FEYNMAN + SCHWINGER + TOMONAGA — Quantum Electrodynamics (QED, 1940s-50s). Nobel 1965. (12) WEINBERG + SALAM + GLASHOW — Electroweak unification (Nobel 1979). (13) GELL-MANN — quarks, Standard Model (1964; Nobel 1969). (14) Higgs — Higgs mechanism (1964; Nobel 2013 with Englert after Higgs boson discovery CERN 2012). STANDARD MODEL of particle physics — 17 fundamental particles: 6 QUARKS (up, down, charm, strange, top, bottom) + 6 LEPTONS (electron, muon, tau + 3 neutrinos) + 4 FORCE CARRIERS (photon, W + Z bosons, gluon) + HIGGS boson (mass-giving). QUANTUM COMPUTING — based on superposition + entanglement; IBM Condor 1,121 qubits 2023; Google Sycamore supremacy 2019. POTENTIAL TRANSFORMATIONAL for crypto + drug discovery + materials.

cards.front:
The NUCLEUS of an ATOM was DISCOVERED by:

(A) J.J. Thomson
(B) ERNEST RUTHERFORD (1911)
(C) Niels Bohr
(D) Chadwick
cards.back:
(B) ERNEST RUTHERFORD (1911)

Modern Physics — ERNEST RUTHERFORD (1871-1937, New Zealand-born British) — 'FATHER OF NUCLEAR PHYSICS'. Won NOBEL PRIZE in CHEMISTRY 1908 (not Physics!) for INVESTIGATIONS INTO DISINTEGRATION OF ELEMENTS + chemistry of radioactive substances. Famously quipped about getting a chemistry Nobel — 'I have dealt with many different transformations with various time-periods, but the QUICKEST transformation I have met was my own, from physicist to chemist!' GOLD FOIL EXPERIMENT (1909-11) — Rutherford + HANS GEIGER + ERNEST MARSDEN at Manchester. Shot ALPHA PARTICLES (He-4 nuclei; 2 protons + 2 neutrons) at a thin GOLD FOIL (~1 atom thick). EXPECTED (per J.J. Thomson's PLUM PUDDING atomic model — atom as diffuse positive matter with electrons embedded like raisins): alpha particles should pass through slightly deflected. OBSERVED: (1) MOST (99.9%+) passed STRAIGHT through. (2) SOME deflected at small angles. (3) A FEW (~1 in 8,000) deflected at LARGE angles (>90°). (4) SOME even BOUNCED BACK. Rutherford: 'It was almost as incredible as if you fired a 15-inch shell at a piece of tissue paper + it came back + hit you'. CONCLUSION — RUTHERFORD'S NUCLEAR MODEL (1911): (1) Most of atom is EMPTY SPACE (hence most alphas pass through). (2) Mass + POSITIVE charge concentrated in a TINY DENSE NUCLEUS at centre (<1/10,000 of atom's size). (3) ELECTRONS orbit around nucleus (like planets around sun). (4) Atom is ELECTRICALLY NEUTRAL overall. Later: nucleus contains PROTONS (discovered by Rutherford 1919 via alpha + N-14 → O-17 + proton) + NEUTRONS (discovered by JAMES CHADWICK 1932 via alpha + Be-9 → C-12 + neutron; Nobel 1935). ATOMIC STRUCTURE: (1) NUCLEUS — protons (positive) + neutrons (neutral); held together by STRONG NUCLEAR FORCE (overcomes proton-proton repulsion at short range 1-3 fm). NUCLEUS size ~10⁻¹⁵ m (1 fm = femtometre). Mass = 99.9% of atom. (2) ELECTRONS — orbit nucleus; negative charge; mass 1/1836 of proton. Atom size ~10⁻¹⁰ m (0.1 nm = 1 angstrom). Ratio atom/nucleus ~100,000 (if nucleus = 1 cm marble, atom = 1 km across). (3) Atom is mostly EMPTY SPACE. ATOMIC NUMBER Z = # protons = # electrons (uncharged atom); determines element identity. MASS NUMBER A = protons + neutrons. ISOTOPES = same Z, different A (different neutron counts). ATOMIC MODELS chronology: (1) DALTON 1808 — atoms indivisible billiard balls. (2) THOMSON 1897 — discovered electron (cathode rays); PLUM PUDDING model. (3) RUTHERFORD 1911 — nuclear model. (4) BOHR 1913 — ELECTRONS in QUANTIZED ORBITS. Emit/absorb light at specific frequencies (explains H spectrum). (5) SOMMERFELD 1916 — elliptical orbits + quantum numbers. (6) DE BROGLIE 1924 — electrons as waves. (7) SCHRÖDINGER 1926 — WAVE MECHANICS; electrons as PROBABILITY CLOUDS (orbitals); 4 quantum numbers (n, l, m_l, m_s). Current accepted model. RUTHERFORD's OTHER contributions: (1) Coined term 'alpha' + 'beta' decay. (2) First artificial NUCLEAR TRANSMUTATION (1919). (3) Predicted neutron (Chadwick's teacher). (4) McGill + Manchester + Cavendish Cambridge labs. Mentored Bohr + Chadwick + Soddy + Hahn + Oppenheimer + others. Died 1937 (Baron Rutherford of Nelson). Element 104 RUTHERFORDIUM (Rf) named after him. GOLD FOIL experiment with alpha particles; found most matter is empty space + dense positively-charged NUCLEUS at center.

cards.front:
The FIRST NUCLEAR REACTOR (CP-1, Chicago Pile-1) was built by:

(A) Einstein
(B) ENRICO FERMI's team
(C) Oppenheimer alone
(D) Marie Curie
cards.back:
(B) ENRICO FERMI's team

Modern Physics — ENRICO FERMI (1901-54) — Italian-American physicist; 'ARCHITECT OF THE NUCLEAR AGE'. Nobel Physics 1938 for NEUTRON-INDUCED RADIOACTIVITY + discovery of trans-uranic elements. Emigrated to USA 1938 (his wife Jewish + rising Fascism). CHICAGO PILE-1 (CP-1) — 1st man-made self-sustaining NUCLEAR CHAIN REACTION achieved 2 DECEMBER 1942 (3:25 PM) beneath Stagg Field (disused squash court), University of Chicago. FERMI's team included Herbert Anderson + Walter Zinn + Leo Szilard + Eugene Wigner + many others. DESIGN: 5.6-metre-wide pile of URANIUM OXIDE + URANIUM METAL slugs embedded in 385 TONS of GRAPHITE BLOCKS (graphite = moderator, slows neutrons). CADMIUM CONTROL RODS regulated reaction. Operated briefly (0.5 W power) to demonstrate criticality; shut down safely after 28 min. CHAIN REACTION: (1) U-235 nucleus absorbs neutron → splits into lighter nuclei (Ba + Kr + etc.) + releases 2-3 neutrons + energy; (2) those neutrons trigger more fissions → chain reaction. If each fission causes on average ≥1 more fission = 'critical mass' sustained. At >1 = supercritical (bomb). U-235 has ~0.7% abundance in natural uranium; U-238 99.3% (doesn't easily fission but absorbs neutrons → Pu-239 for bombs). MANHATTAN PROJECT (1942-46) — US government secret program to build atomic bomb before Nazis. HEAD: Major General LESLIE GROVES (military) + J. ROBERT OPPENHEIMER (scientific director at Los Alamos). 130,000+ workers; ~$2B (~$30B today). Key sites: Los Alamos (NM, weapon design), Oak Ridge (TN, U-235 enrichment), Hanford (WA, plutonium production), Chicago Metallurgical Lab, Trinity Site (NM). FIRST NUCLEAR TEST — TRINITY — 16 JULY 1945 at Alamogordo NM; plutonium implosion device; 20 kilotons yield; OPPENHEIMER quoted Bhagavad Gita: 'NOW I AM BECOME DEATH, DESTROYER OF WORLDS' (actually uttered in a 1965 TV interview; contemporaneous was 'it worked'). NUCLEAR BOMBS dropped on Japan: (1) 6 AUGUST 1945 — 'LITTLE BOY' (U-235 gun-type) on HIROSHIMA; 15 kilotons; ~140,000 dead by year end. (2) 9 AUGUST 1945 — 'FAT MAN' (Pu-239 implosion) on NAGASAKI; 21 kt; ~70,000 dead. Japan surrendered 15 Aug (VJ Day 2 Sep 1945). ONLY 2 NUCLEAR WEAPONS ever used in warfare. AFTERMATH: (1) OPPENHEIMER turned against H-BOMB (fusion weapon); security clearance revoked 1954 (restored posthumously 2022). (2) COLD WAR nuclear arms race; USSR test 1949 (Joe-1); UK 1952; France 1960; China 1964; India 1974 (Smiling Buddha) + 1998 (Operation Shakti 5 tests); Pakistan 1998 (Chagai); N Korea 2006. (3) NON-PROLIFERATION TREATY (NPT) 1968 — 5 'nuclear weapon states' (P5) + others pledge non-proliferation. India + Pakistan + Israel NEVER signed; N Korea withdrew 2003. (4) NUCLEAR POWER — civilian commercialisation from 1956 (UK Calder Hall first commercial reactor). NUCLEAR TREATIES: NPT 1968; PTBT 1963; SALT I + II 1972 + 1979; START I + II + new START; CTBT 1996 (not in force; India + Pakistan + others haven't signed); NSG waiver India 2008; JCPOA Iran deal 2015 (Trump left 2018, now defunct). INDIA's NUCLEAR: 3-STAGE programme (Bhabha) — PHWR + FBR + Thorium reactors. ~7.5 GW nuclear capacity; 22 operational reactors; Kudankulam, Kaiga, Tarapur, Kakrapar, Narora, Rawatbhata, Kalpakkam. 2 December 1942 at University of Chicago; first self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction; Manhattan Project; Nobel 1938.

cards.front:
MARIE CURIE is the ONLY person to win Nobel Prizes in TWO DIFFERENT SCIENCES. Her prizes were in:

(A) Physics (1903) + Chemistry (1911)
(B) Chemistry + Medicine
(C) Physics + Literature
(D) Medicine + Peace
cards.back:
(A) Physics (1903) + Chemistry (1911)

Modern Physics — MARIE SKŁODOWSKA-CURIE (7 Nov 1867 – 4 July 1934) — Polish-born French physicist + chemist. FIRST WOMAN to win NOBEL PRIZE + ONLY PERSON to win NOBEL in 2 DIFFERENT SCIENCES + FIRST PERSON + ONLY WOMAN to WIN 2 NOBELS. NOBEL 1: PHYSICS 1903 — with HENRI BECQUEREL + PIERRE CURIE (her husband) for discovery of RADIOACTIVITY. Becquerel discovered 1896 that uranium salts emit invisible rays (spontaneous radiation; called 'Becquerel rays' → 'radioactivity' coined by Marie 1898). Curies showed thorium is also radioactive; isolated 2 new elements. NOBEL 2: CHEMISTRY 1911 — for DISCOVERY + ISOLATION of RADIUM (Ra, atomic number 88) + POLONIUM (Po, 84; named after her native POLAND). Radium's 1 GRAM of pure Ra took 4 YEARS of painstaking processing from TONS of pitchblende ore (mostly uranium, trace radium). Worked in miserable shed lab. BACKGROUND: born Warsaw under Russian occupation; barred from higher education there (girls); went to Paris 1891 (Sorbonne); met Pierre Curie 1894; married 1895. ACHIEVEMENTS: (1) Coined 'radioactivity'. (2) Isolated 2 elements. (3) Research during WWI — mobile X-ray units ('petites Curies') to battlefields; trained 150 women operators; X-rayed 1 million+ wounded. (4) Paris + Warsaw Radium Institutes founded. (5) Father + mother + daughter + son-in-law all Nobel laureates — FAMILY of 5 Nobels! Daughter IRÈNE JOLIOT-CURIE shared 1935 Nobel Chemistry with husband FRÉDÉRIC JOLIOT — for ARTIFICIAL RADIOACTIVITY (induced radioactive isotopes). PIERRE died tragically 1906 (run over by horse-drawn wagon Paris). DEATH: 1934 from APLASTIC ANAEMIA due to long-term RADIATION exposure (her notebooks still radioactive today; kept in lead-lined box at Bibliothèque Nationale). Buried in PANTHEON Paris (first woman to be buried there on merit, 1995). Nickname: 'Madame Curie'; 'Brains are more valuable than beauty'. RADIOACTIVITY — phenomenon by which unstable atomic NUCLEI spontaneously EMIT radiation to achieve stability. 3 TYPES: (1) ALPHA (α) DECAY — helium-4 nucleus (2 protons + 2 neutrons) emitted; heavy nucleus → lighter + alpha. Stopped by paper. Examples: U-238 → Th-234 + α; Rn-222 decay. Highly ionising, damaging if inhaled. (2) BETA (β) DECAY — high-energy electron (β−) OR positron (β+) emitted from nucleus. β−: neutron → proton + e⁻ + antineutrino. β+: proton → neutron + e⁺ + neutrino. Penetrates skin; stopped by aluminium. Examples: C-14 → N-14 + e⁻ (used in carbon dating). (3) GAMMA (γ) — high-energy PHOTON (EM radiation); usually accompanies alpha or beta; nucleus de-excites. Most penetrating (needs lead / concrete). Gamma knife for medicine. HALF-LIFE — time for half of radioactive atoms to decay. Varies hugely: U-238 4.5 billion years; C-14 5,730 yr; Ra-226 1,600 yr; I-131 8 days; F-18 110 min (PET scan). APPLICATIONS: (1) MEDICAL — X-rays, CT, PET, radiotherapy (gamma knife, cobalt-60, cyberknife); nuclear medicine (Tc-99m 85% of scans). (2) CARBON DATING — C-14/C-12 ratio in organic material dates back 50,000 years (Nobel 1960 Libby). (3) Nuclear power. (4) Food irradiation. (5) Smoke detectors (Am-241). (6) Industrial gauging + welding inspection. (7) Radiodating (U-Pb ~billions of years). HEALTH HAZARDS: ionising radiation damages DNA + causes cancer. Units: Bq (activity = 1 decay/sec), Gy (absorbed dose J/kg), Sv (biological effect). Background = 2-3 mSv/yr; CT scan ~10 mSv; chest X-ray 0.1 mSv; lethal whole-body acute = 4-6 Sv. for RADIOACTIVITY (with Henri Becquerel + Pierre Curie) + isolation of RADIUM + POLONIUM.

Buried in PANTHEON Paris (first woman to be buried there on merit, 1995). Nickname: 'Madame Curie'; 'Brains are more valuable than beauty'. RADIOACTIVITY — phenomenon by which unstable atomic NUCLEI spontaneously EMIT radiation to achieve stability. 3 TYPES: (1) ALPHA (α) DECAY — helium-4 nucleus (2 protons + 2 neutrons) emitted; heavy nucleus → lighter + alpha. Stopped by paper. Examples: U-238 → Th-234 + α; Rn-222 decay. Highly ionising, damaging if inhaled. (2) BETA (β) DECAY — high-energy electron (β−) OR positron (β+) emitted from nucleus. β−: neutron → proton + e⁻ + antineutrino. β+: proton → neutron + e⁺ + neutrino. Penetrates skin; stopped by aluminium. Examples: C-14 → N-14 + e⁻ (used in carbon dating). (3) GAMMA (γ) — high-energy PHOTON (EM radiation); usually accompanies alpha or beta; nucleus de-excites. Most penetrating (needs lead / concrete). Gamma knife for medicine. HALF-LIFE — time for half of radioactive atoms to decay. Varies hugely: U-238 4.5 billion years; C-14 5,730 yr; Ra-226 1,600 yr; I-131 8 days; F-18 110 min (PET scan). APPLICATIONS: (1) MEDICAL — X-rays, CT, PET, radiotherapy (gamma knife, cobalt-60, cyberknife); nuclear medicine (Tc-99m 85% of scans). (2) CARBON DATING — C-14/C-12 ratio in organic material dates back 50,000 years (Nobel 1960 Libby). (3) Nuclear power. (4) Food irradiation. (5) Smoke detectors (Am-241). (6) Industrial gauging + welding inspection. (7) Radiodating (U-Pb ~billions of years). HEALTH HAZARDS: ionising radiation damages DNA + causes cancer. Units: Bq (activity = 1 decay/sec), Gy (absorbed dose J/kg), Sv (biological effect). Background = 2-3 mSv/yr; CT scan ~10 mSv; chest X-ray 0.1 mSv; lethal whole-body acute = 4-6 Sv. for RADIOACTIVITY (with Henri Becquerel + Pierre Curie) + isolation of RADIUM + POLONIUM.

cards.front:
The HIGGS BOSON, the 'GOD PARTICLE', was experimentally CONFIRMED at:

(A) NASA Houston
(B) CERN, Switzerland
(C) ISRO Bengaluru
(D) Tokyo
cards.back:
(B) CERN, Switzerland

Modern Physics — HIGGS BOSON — fundamental particle in Standard Model of particle physics; popularly called 'GOD PARTICLE' (term from Leon Lederman's 1993 book title; not liked by physicists as it misleads). PROPOSED 1964 theoretically by 6 physicists in 3 separate papers (PRL 1964): (1) PETER HIGGS (UK) — 'Broken Symmetries + Masses of Gauge Bosons'. (2) FRANÇOIS ENGLERT + ROBERT BROUT (Belgium). (3) Gerald Guralnik + C.R. Hagen + Tom Kibble (UK-USA). All independently. EXPLAINED the 'HIGGS MECHANISM' — how FUNDAMENTAL PARTICLES acquire MASS via interaction with an all-pervading QUANTUM FIELD called the HIGGS FIELD. Without Higgs field, fundamental particles would be massless (like photons) + universe couldn't form atoms/matter. Particles interacting more strongly with field = more MASSIVE (top quark heaviest; electron light; photon massless since doesn't interact). KEY PROPERTY: unlike other known fields (EM, gravity, etc.), Higgs field has NON-ZERO VALUE even in vacuum ('vacuum expectation value' = 246 GeV). Excitations of this field = Higgs boson. DISCOVERY: 4 JULY 2012 announced at CERN (European Organisation for Nuclear Research, Geneva, founded 1954). LARGE HADRON COLLIDER (LHC) — 27-km circular particle accelerator underground on France-Switzerland border; world's LARGEST + most powerful; proton-proton collisions at 13 TeV. TWO INDEPENDENT EXPERIMENTS: (1) ATLAS + (2) CMS (Compact Muon Solenoid) — both observed particle consistent with Higgs at mass ~125 GeV (~133× proton mass). Peter Higgs present in room emotional tears; said 'it's incredible that this has happened in my lifetime'. NOBEL PRIZE in PHYSICS 2013 → ENGLERT + HIGGS (Brout had died 2011; Nobel rules no posthumous). Indian contribution: SATYENDRA NATH BOSE (1894-1974) derived statistics for BOSONS — particles with INTEGER spin that can occupy same quantum state. PHOTON, GLUON, W, Z, HIGGS are all BOSONS. FERMIONS = half-integer spin (electrons, quarks, leptons) — obey PAULI EXCLUSION. BOSON named after S.N. Bose — he worked with Einstein (Bose-Einstein statistics + Bose-Einstein condensate). TRAGEDY: Bose never won Nobel (his statistical work predated prize developments). Higgs boson DECAYS very fast (~10⁻²² s) to lighter particles — detected indirectly via decay products. STANDARD MODEL — 17 particles: (a) 6 QUARKS (up, down, charm, strange, top, bottom) + antiparticles — make up protons + neutrons + exotic hadrons. (b) 6 LEPTONS (electron, muon, tau + 3 neutrinos). (c) 4 FORCE-CARRIER BOSONS — photon (EM), gluon (strong, 8 types), W + Z (weak). (d) HIGGS (mass). NOT included in SM: GRAVITY (GR not unified with QM); DARK MATTER; DARK ENERGY. LHC OTHER achievements: (1) Top quark precision mass measurement. (2) Confirmed W boson. (3) No supersymmetric particles found (SUSY theory on hold). (4) Pentaquarks + tetraquarks discovered. (5) Quark-gluon plasma studies. FUTURE: LHC HL-LHC (High Luminosity upgrade 2029+). Proposed Future Circular Collider (FCC) at CERN = 100 km ring. China CEPC proposed. Muon colliders + linear colliders proposed. CERN members = ~23 European states; INDIA is ASSOCIATE MEMBER (since 2017). India contributed key components to CMS + ATLAS + TIFR / VECC / BARC / IIT scientists involved. CMS Higgs observation paper had 50+ Indian authors. INDIA at CERN is part of diplomatic + scientific strategy. via LARGE HADRON COLLIDER on 4 July 2012; gives other particles MASS via Higgs Mechanism; Higgs + Englert Nobel 2013.
