cards.front:
The BIG BANG THEORY states that our UNIVERSE began:

(A) 10,000 years ago
(B) ~13.8 BILLION YEARS AGO from an extremely hot, dense state
(C) 100 years ago
(D) 1 million years ago
cards.back:
(B) ~13.8 BILLION YEARS AGO from an extremely hot, dense state

Modern Physics — BIG BANG THEORY — prevailing cosmological model of observable UNIVERSE's origin + evolution. Universe BEGAN from extremely HOT + DENSE + tiny state ~13.8 BILLION YEARS AGO (precisely 13.787 ± 0.020 Gyr per Planck 2018 data) + has been EXPANDING ever since. 'BIG BANG' term coined 1949 by FRED HOYLE (dismissively on BBC radio; he preferred steady-state theory) but stuck. THEORY DEVELOPMENT: (1) 1917 — EINSTEIN's General Relativity equations could describe expanding/contracting universe; he added COSMOLOGICAL CONSTANT to force static universe. Later called it 'biggest blunder'. (2) 1922 — ALEXANDER FRIEDMANN (Russian) derived expanding universe solutions from GR. (3) 1927 — GEORGES LEMAÎTRE (Belgian Catholic priest + physicist) proposed 'primeval atom' theory — first big bang idea. Published before Hubble's observation. (4) 1929 — EDWIN HUBBLE observed galaxies RECEDING with velocities proportional to distance (Hubble's Law, v = H₀·d; now known as Hubble-Lemaître Law); proved UNIVERSE is EXPANDING. (5) 1948 — GAMOW, ALPHER, HERMAN predicted the COSMIC MICROWAVE BACKGROUND (CMB) — residual heat from Big Bang should be detectable as ~5 K radiation. (6) 1964 — ARNO PENZIAS + ROBERT WILSON (Bell Labs) accidentally DISCOVERED CMB (2.7 K microwave background in all directions) — strong evidence for Big Bang. Nobel 1978. BIG BANG TIMELINE: (1) t=0 SINGULARITY (untreatable by current physics; needs quantum gravity). (2) 10⁻⁴³ s (Planck time) — earliest physics can speak. (3) 10⁻³⁶ to 10⁻³² s — INFLATION EPOCH (Guth 1980) — universe expanded 10²⁶ × in instant; smoothed + flat. (4) 10⁻¹² s — quark epoch. (5) 10⁻⁶ s — QUARKS combine into protons + neutrons (HADRON epoch). (6) 1 s — 3 BILLION K; neutrinos decouple. (7) 3 MIN — BIG BANG NUCLEOSYNTHESIS: protons + neutrons form LIGHT NUCLEI (75% H, 25% He, trace Li, D); universe cools to billion K. (8) 380,000 YR — RECOMBINATION: electrons + nuclei form ATOMS; universe becomes transparent → CMB photons escape (the 'photon decoupling'). (9) 100-200 MILLION YR — first stars form (Population III, huge, short-lived). (10) 1 BILLION YR — first galaxies + quasars. (11) 9 BILLION YR — Sun + Solar System form. (12) 10 BILLION YR (~4 BILLION YR ago) — Earth forms + life begins. (13) 13.8 BILLION YR — NOW. EVIDENCE for BIG BANG: (1) Hubble REDSHIFT — galaxies receding; redshift ∝ distance; expansion. (2) CMB — uniform 2.725 K microwave glow. Mapped in detail by COBE 1992, WMAP 2001, PLANCK 2009-18 satellites. Tiny anisotropies (~10⁻⁵) = seeds of galaxy formation. (3) ABUNDANCE of LIGHT ELEMENTS — ~75% H + 25% He + traces Li + D match big bang nucleosynthesis predictions. (4) Large-scale galaxy structure. (5) CMB spectrum = near-perfect blackbody. HOT TOPICS: (1) DARK MATTER (~27% of universe) — invisible mass; seen via gravity (galaxy rotation curves, CMB, lensing). Candidate: WIMPs, axions; not detected directly. (2) DARK ENERGY (~68%) — mysterious force driving ACCELERATING expansion (discovered 1998 via Type Ia supernovae; Nobel 2011 Perlmutter + Schmidt + Riess). Possibly EINSTEIN's cosmological constant reinstated. (3) ORDINARY MATTER only 5%. (4) HUBBLE TENSION — different H₀ measurements disagree (local supernovae ~73 vs CMB ~67 km/s/Mpc) — unresolved. (5) Multiverse, inflation details, quantum gravity, black holes. UNIVERSE may end in BIG FREEZE (heat death), BIG RIP, BIG CRUNCH — depends on dark energy evolution. OBSERVABLE UNIVERSE ~93 BILLION LY across (bigger than 13.8 Gly × c due to expansion). still EXPANDING (confirmed by Hubble 1929); CMB + galactic redshift + element abundances = pillars of evidence.

cards.front:
HEISENBERG's UNCERTAINTY PRINCIPLE states that:

(A) Energy is always conserved
(B) The MORE precisely POSITION of a particle is determined, the LESS precisely its MOMENTUM can be known (Δx·Δp ≥ ℏ/2); fundamental quantum limitation
(C) Temperature can never reach zero
(D) Entropy always increases
cards.back:
(B) The MORE precisely POSITION of a particle is determined, the LESS precisely its MOMENTUM can be known (Δx·Δp ≥ ℏ/2); fundamental quantum limitation

Modern Physics — HEISENBERG's UNCERTAINTY PRINCIPLE (1927) — FUNDAMENTAL QUANTUM-mechanical LIMITATION: you CANNOT simultaneously know BOTH POSITION (x) + MOMENTUM (p = mass × velocity) of a particle with ARBITRARY PRECISION. FORMULATION: Δx · Δp ≥ ℏ/2, where ℏ = h/2π = 1.055 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s (reduced Planck constant). If position precisely known (Δx small), momentum UNCERTAIN (Δp large), + vice versa. NOT a measurement-LIMITATION but a fundamental feature of QUANTUM REALITY. Similar pair: energy-time (ΔE · Δt ≥ ℏ/2). PROPOSED by WERNER HEISENBERG (German, age 25) in 1927 paper 'Über den anschaulichen Inhalt der quantentheoretischen Kinematik + Mechanik'. Nobel 1932 (at 31). Part of the 'COPENHAGEN INTERPRETATION' of quantum mechanics (with Bohr + Born). IMPLICATIONS: (1) CLASSICAL determinism (Newton: know all positions+momenta → predict everything) is IMPOSSIBLE. (2) Electrons don't have fixed 'orbits' — only PROBABILITY clouds (orbitals). (3) VACUUM is 'quantum foam' — brief particle-antiparticle pairs appear + annihilate via energy-time uncertainty. (4) Tunnel effect — particle can penetrate barriers impossible classically (alpha decay, scanning tunneling microscope, transistors). (5) ZERO-POINT ENERGY — even at 0 K, particles have residual motion. (6) Atomic stability — why electrons don't spiral into nucleus (which classical physics predicted). Uncertainty stabilises atoms. (7) HUMAN limits on knowledge. EXAMPLE: electron in atom; if you try to know its position exactly (photon high-energy to 'see' it), photon kicks electron away (momentum uncertain). ANALOGIES: flashlight in dust-storm — beam disturbs what you're observing. NOT mere experimental difficulty; intrinsic to nature. RELATED QUANTUM CONCEPTS: (1) WAVE-PARTICLE DUALITY — light + electrons behave as both waves + particles (famous DOUBLE-SLIT experiment: interference patterns even when 1 electron at a time → 'particles interfere with themselves'). (2) SUPERPOSITION — particle in combination of states till measured; Schrödinger's cat (both alive + dead). (3) MEASUREMENT collapse — observation 'collapses' superposition. (4) ENTANGLEMENT — 2+ particles correlated; measuring one instantly affects other regardless of distance (Einstein called 'spooky action at a distance'; EPR paradox 1935; Bell's inequalities 1964; experimental verification by Aspect 1982 onwards; Nobel 2022 Aspect + Clauser + Zeilinger). Basis of QUANTUM COMPUTING + QUANTUM CRYPTOGRAPHY. QUANTUM COMPUTING — uses qubits (0, 1, or superposition); can solve certain problems (factoring, optimization, simulation) exponentially faster. IBM, Google, Microsoft, Amazon + startups. IBM CONDOR 1,121 qubits 2023; aim for ERROR-CORRECTED quantum computers by 2030s. INDIA's National Quantum Mission (2023, ₹6,000 crore) — 4 hubs: IISc + TIFR + IIT Madras + IIT Bombay. QUANTUM CRYPTOGRAPHY — QKD (Quantum Key Distribution) uses entanglement for provably secure comms. Chinese Micius satellite 2016 demonstrated space-based QKD. INDIA tested QKD ground-to-ground (ISRO + DRDO). HEISENBERG's OTHER contributions: (a) Matrix mechanics (first formulation of QM 1925, with Born + Jordan). (b) Heisenberg model of magnetism. (c) Nuclear physics (S-matrix). (d) Controversial role in Nazi Germany's uranium project during WWII (debate continues — did he try to build bomb or sabotage?). COPENHAGEN INTERPRETATION — standard; wave function is probability amplitude; measurement collapses; observer role central. COMPETING: Many-Worlds (Everett 1957), pilot wave (Bohm), QBism, GRW (objective collapse).

cards.front:
The FIRST NUCLEAR POWER PLANT in INDIA is:

(A) Kudankulam
(B) TARAPUR Atomic Power Station (TAPS), Maharashtra
(C) Narora
(D) Kalpakkam
cards.back:
(B) TARAPUR Atomic Power Station (TAPS), Maharashtra

Modern Physics — TARAPUR ATOMIC POWER STATION (TAPS) — INDIA's 1ST NUCLEAR POWER PLANT. LOCATION: Tarapur, Palghar district, Maharashtra (on Arabian Sea coast). OPERATED by NUCLEAR POWER CORPORATION of INDIA LIMITED (NPCIL, est 1987). UNITS 1 + 2: Boiling Water Reactors (BWR) — 160 MW each; commissioned 28 Oct 1969 as TAPS-1 + 2. Built via US-India tech transfer (GE designed); after 1974 Pokhran-I, USA cut fuel supply; France supplied till 1983; then Russia, China (for Chinese-made MOX pellets briefly). UNITS 3 + 4: Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors (PHWR) 540 MW each; commissioned 2005-06 — INDIA-built indigenously. Thus TAPS has 4 reactors; total 1,400 MW. One of oldest operational BWRs in world (60-year life expected). INDIAN NUCLEAR POWER PLANTS (2024): 22 OPERATIONAL REACTORS + more under construction. (1) TARAPUR (MH, 4 reactors, 1,400 MW). (2) RAWATBHATA (Rajasthan, 6 reactors, 1,180 MW — PHWRs + 1 under decommissioning). (3) MADRAS / KALPAKKAM (TN, 2 reactors, 440 MW + the PFBR Fast Breeder under commissioning Aug 2024; + under-construction BHAVINI). (4) NARORA (UP, 2 × 220 MW PHWR). (5) KAKRAPAR (Gujarat, 4 reactors, 1,340 MW; latest 700 MW PHWR commissioned 2023; indigenous). (6) KAIGA (Karnataka, 4 × 220 MW). (7) KUDANKULAM (TN, 2 × 1000 MW VVER Russian, operational; 4 more under construction; largest in India when done). Total INSTALLED nuclear capacity: ~7.5 GW (2024). AIM: 22.4 GW by 2031; 100 GW by 2047 (VisionViksit Bharat). 3-STAGE NUCLEAR PROGRAMME of INDIA — formulated by Dr HOMI BHABHA 1950s; India's unique path due to LOW URANIUM but ABUNDANT THORIUM reserves. (1) STAGE 1 — Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors (PHWR) using NATURAL URANIUM (U-235 0.7%); generates electricity + PRODUCES plutonium (Pu-239) as byproduct. Most current Indian reactors are PHWR type. Mature + deployed. (2) STAGE 2 — FAST BREEDER REACTORS (FBR) using Pu-239 fuel; BREED more fissile material than they consume (Pu-239 + Th-232 → U-233). PFBR (Prototype FBR, 500 MW, Kalpakkam) achieved first criticality + power generation AUG 2024 — historic milestone; 30+ years in making, led by BHAVINI + IGCAR. (3) STAGE 3 — THORIUM REACTORS using U-233 (bred from Th-232 in Stage 2). India has 25% of world's thorium — 2nd largest. Long-term self-sufficient nuclear energy. AHWR (Advanced Heavy Water Reactor, 300 MW Thorium-based) being designed at BARC; pilot coming. SMALL MODULAR REACTORS (SMR) — India announced 2024 Budget focus; 10 SMRs (100-300 MW each) planned; BSMR design by BARC 2027+. cards.front:
The FOUR FUNDAMENTAL FORCES of NATURE are:

(A) Only gravity + friction
(B) GRAVITY, ELECTROMAGNETISM, STRONG NUCLEAR (binds nuclei), WEAK NUCLEAR (beta decay); unified in Standard Model except gravity
(C) Wind + water + earth + fire
(D) Heat + sound + light + motion
cards.back:
(B) GRAVITY, ELECTROMAGNETISM, STRONG NUCLEAR (binds nuclei), WEAK NUCLEAR (beta decay); unified in Standard Model except gravity

Modern Physics — FUNDAMENTAL FORCES (INTERACTIONS) of NATURE — all natural phenomena reducible to 4: (1) STRONG NUCLEAR FORCE — STRONGEST; binds QUARKS into PROTONS + NEUTRONS (via GLUONS) + binds protons + neutrons into NUCLEI (via residual strong force / pions). Strength = 1 (reference); range ~1 femtometre (10⁻¹⁵ m) — very SHORT. Charge = 'color' (red, green, blue, anti-colors). Carrier: GLUON (massless, 8 types). Described by QCD (Quantum Chromodynamics). Most fundamental strong force — without it, no atomic nuclei could exist. (2) ELECTROMAGNETISM — 2nd strongest. Attracts/repels charged particles; basis of electricity + magnetism + LIGHT + chemistry (atomic bonding) + friction + elasticity + normal force + all non-nuclear/gravitational daily phenomena. Strength = 1/137 (fine structure constant); range = INFINITE. Charge: electric (positive + negative). Carrier: PHOTON (massless). Described by QED (Quantum Electrodynamics — Feynman-Schwinger-Tomonaga, Nobel 1965); beautiful theory matching experiment to 12 decimal places (most precisely tested theory ever). (3) WEAK NUCLEAR FORCE — 3rd strongest. RESPONSIBLE for BETA DECAY + radioactive decay + energy production in SUN (hydrogen fusion pp-chain involves weak interaction). Strength = 10⁻⁶ of strong; range ~10⁻¹⁸ m. Charge: 'weak isospin' + 'weak hypercharge'. Carriers: W⁺ + W⁻ + Z⁰ BOSONS (MASSIVE — ~80-91 GeV each; hence short range). Unified with EM into ELECTROWEAK theory by GLASHOW + SALAM + WEINBERG (Nobel 1979); UNIFIED at high energies (~100 GeV); separated at low energies due to Higgs mechanism (spontaneous symmetry breaking). (4) GRAVITY — WEAKEST by far. Strength = 10⁻³⁸ (compared to strong). Range = INFINITE. ATTRACTIVE ONLY (no repulsive gravity known — important). Acts on MASS (+ energy, per GR). Carrier: hypothetical GRAVITON (spin-2, massless; not experimentally detected; gravitational waves = classical manifestation). GENERAL RELATIVITY describes gravity as SPACETIME CURVATURE — not a force in usual QFT sense. UNIFYING gravity with other 3 = HOLY GRAIL of physics (string theory, loop quantum gravity, causal dynamical triangulation — no complete theory yet). DESPITE being weakest, gravity dominates astronomy because: (a) ALWAYS ATTRACTIVE; (b) EM cancels (charges balance); (c) range unlimited (strong + weak short-range); (d) accumulates to huge scales. HIERARCHY PROBLEM — why is gravity so weak compared to other forces? Active research. GRAND UNIFIED THEORIES (GUT) — attempt to unify strong + electromagnetic + weak at very high energies (~10¹⁶ GeV; proton decay predicted — not observed). SUPERSYMMETRY + STRING theories attempt full unification including gravity — not confirmed. FORCE UNIFICATIONS HISTORY: (1) Newton 1687 — terrestrial + celestial gravity unified. (2) Maxwell 1864 — electricity + magnetism unified as electromagnetism. (3) Glashow-Salam-Weinberg 1967-73 — weak + EM = electroweak (confirmed CERN 1983). (4) Proposed: strong + electroweak = GUT; GUT + gravity = TOE. Fundamental forces ACT at different scales: gravity dominates cosmos; EM dominates chemistry + biology + technology; strong + weak dominate nuclei. Dark energy (behind accelerating expansion) may be EINSTEIN's COSMOLOGICAL CONSTANT — nature of gravity at largest scales. OBSERVABLES: gravitational waves (LIGO 2015), Higgs boson (CERN 2012), black hole images (EHT 2019 M87*, 2022 Sgr A*), galactic + cosmic scale phenomena testing GR. Dark MATTER + energy (95% of universe) remain mysterious.

cards.front:
RADIOACTIVITY was discovered by:

(A) Marie Curie
(B) Henri Becquerel
(C) Ernest Rutherford
(D) Wilhelm Röntgen
cards.back:
(B) Henri Becquerel

Modern Physics — Henri Becquerel (1896) discovered radioactivity in uranium salts accidentally — they fogged a photographic plate kept in a drawer. Marie and Pierre Curie later isolated polonium and radium. Rutherford identified alpha, beta rays. Röntgen discovered X-rays (1895). Nobel Physics 1903 shared: Becquerel + Curies.

cards.front:
The three radioactive emissions (in order of penetrating power, least to greatest) are:

(A) Alpha < Beta < Gamma
(B) Gamma < Beta < Alpha
(C) Alpha < Gamma < Beta
(D) Beta < Alpha < Gamma
cards.back:
(A) Alpha < Beta < Gamma

Modern Physics — Alpha (helium nucleus, +2) — stopped by paper. Beta (fast electron, −1) — stopped by aluminium sheet. Gamma (high-energy EM) — needs thick lead or concrete. Ionising power is the REVERSE order (alpha most ionising, gamma least).

cards.front:
The famous mass-energy equivalence relation is:

(A) E = mc
(B) E = mc²
(C) E = m/c²
(D) E = m + c²
cards.back:
(B) E = mc²

Modern Physics — Einstein's 1905 special relativity — E = mc². Tiny mass converts to enormous energy (c² ≈ 9 × 10¹⁶ J/kg). Basis for nuclear fission (atom bomb, reactors) and fusion (Sun, stars, H-bomb).

cards.front:
The source of the SUN's energy is:

(A) Nuclear fission
(B) Nuclear fusion
(C) Chemical combustion
(D) Gravitational collapse
cards.back:
(B) Nuclear fusion

Modern Physics — Sun fuses hydrogen into helium in its core (proton-proton chain, ~15 million K). 620 million tonnes H → He every second, losing ~4.3 million tonnes as energy (E=mc²). Fusion = combining nuclei. Fission = splitting heavy nuclei (U-235, Pu-239 in reactors/bombs). hydrogen → helium.

cards.front:
The PHOTOELECTRIC EFFECT (for which Einstein won Nobel 1921) demonstrated that:

(A) Light has wave nature only
(B) Light has particle (photon) nature
(C) Atoms have a nucleus
(D) Matter has wavelike properties
cards.back:
(B) Light has particle (photon) nature

Modern Physics — Einstein 1905: light acts as particles (photons) with energy E = hν. Explained why photoelectric emission depends on FREQUENCY, not intensity. Kicked off quantum mechanics. (Matter-wave hypothesis came from de Broglie 1924; nuclear discovery from Rutherford 1911.). exists in quanta of energy hν.

cards.front:
The ATOMIC NUCLEUS was discovered by Ernest Rutherford in his famous:

(A) Cathode ray experiment
(B) Gold-foil / alpha-scattering experiment (1911)
(C) Oil-drop experiment
(D) Photoelectric experiment
cards.back:
(B) Gold-foil / alpha-scattering experiment (1911)

Modern Physics — Rutherford (1911) — fired alpha particles at thin gold foil. Most passed through; a few bounced back sharply. Concluded the positive charge is concentrated in a tiny, dense nucleus. J.J. Thomson — cathode rays → electron. Millikan — oil-drop (electron charge).

(A) France and Germany
(B) France and Switzerland
(C) Italy and Switzerland
(D) Austria and Switzerland
cards.back:
(B) France and Switzerland

Modern Physics — LHC — 27 km underground ring at CERN, straddling the French-Swiss border near Geneva. In July 2012 LHC experiments (ATLAS + CMS) announced the discovery of the Higgs boson (Nobel 2013 for Higgs + Englert).

cards.front:
NUCLEAR FISSION involves:

(A) Two light nuclei joining into a heavier one
(B) A heavy nucleus splitting into two lighter ones
(C) Electrons jumping between energy levels
(D) Atoms combining at very low temperature
cards.back:
(B) A heavy nucleus splitting into two lighter ones

Modern Physics — Fission = a heavy nucleus (e.g., U-235, Pu-239) absorbs a neutron, becomes unstable, splits into 2 lighter nuclei + 2-3 neutrons + huge energy. The released neutrons can trigger further fissions → CHAIN REACTION. Used in: atomic bombs (uncontrolled), nuclear reactors (controlled). Discovered by HAHN, STRASSMANN, MEITNER (1938). E = mc² — mass defect → energy. Distractor 1 = fusion (opposite).

cards.front:
NUCLEAR FUSION (the energy source of the Sun) involves:

(A) Heavy nucleus splitting into smaller ones
(B) Light nuclei combining into a heavier one
(C) Electrons absorbing thermal radiation
(D) Neutrons being released from atom
cards.back:
(B) Light nuclei combining into a heavier one

Modern Physics — Fusion: light nuclei (H-1, H-2 deuterium, H-3 tritium) combine → heavier nucleus (He-4) + energy. Sun uses proton-proton chain (4H → He). Requires extremely high temperature (>10⁷ K) to overcome electrostatic repulsion. Releases ~4× more energy per kg than fission. Hydrogen bomb uses fusion (triggered by fission). cards.front:
Einstein's mass-energy equivalence E = mc² implies that:

(A) Mass and energy are unrelated quantities
(B) Small mass converts to enormous energy
(C) Mass increases when objects move slowly
(D) Energy is always conserved at zero mass
cards.back:
(B) Small mass converts to enormous energy

Modern Physics — E = mc² → c (speed of light) ≈ 3 × 10⁸ m/s; c² = 9 × 10¹⁶. So 1 kg of mass → 9 × 10¹⁶ J ≈ 25 billion kWh. In nuclear reactions, the mass of the products is slightly LESS than reactants (mass DEFECT, Δm); the missing mass is converted to energy. 1 kg uranium fission → ~8 × 10¹³ J (about same as 20,000 tons TNT). India's Pokhran tests (1974, 1998) demonstrated this principle.

cards.front:
In an Indian PHWR (Pressurised Heavy Water Reactor), 'heavy water' acts as the:

(A) Fuel for the nuclear chain reaction
(B) Moderator + coolant in reactor core
(C) Control rod to absorb stray neutrons
(D) Shielding from harmful radiation
cards.back:
(B) Moderator + coolant in reactor core

Modern Physics — Heavy water (D₂O) — both moderator (slows fast neutrons to thermal speeds, increasing fission probability) AND coolant (carries heat to steam generators). PHWR uses NATURAL uranium (no enrichment needed) because D₂O moderates better than ordinary water — this is why India chose PHWR — natural uranium independence. India's 18 of 22 reactors are PHWRs (Tarapur, Kakrapar, Kaiga, Rawatbhata). Distractor 1 = uranium fuel. Distractor 3 = boron/cadmium control rods.

(A) Uranium-235, the standard fission fuel
(B) Thorium-232, abundant on India's coasts
(C) Plutonium-239, weapons-grade material
(D) Deuterium, hydrogen heavy isotope only
cards.back:

cards.front:
The CONTROL RODS in a nuclear reactor (made of boron, cadmium) work by:

(A) Speeding up the fission reaction rate
(B) Absorbing neutrons to slow chain reaction
(C) Reflecting neutrons back into the core
(D) Cooling the fuel rods using water flow
cards.back:
(B) Absorbing neutrons to slow chain reaction

Modern Physics — Control rods — made of materials with HIGH neutron-absorption cross-section: boron (B), cadmium (Cd), hafnium (Hf). Inserted DEEPER → fewer neutrons available for fission → reaction slows. Withdrawn → more neutrons → reaction speeds up. SCRAM = emergency rapid insertion of all rods. In Chernobyl disaster (1986), control rod design flaw + operator error caused runaway reaction. Distractor 1 = opposite. Distractor 4 = coolant role.

cards.front:
NUCLEAR FISSION involves:

(A) Splitting heavy nucleus into lighter ones
(B) Joining two light nuclei together
(C) Capturing a free electron in atom
(D) Converting matter to anti-matter
cards.back:
(A) Splitting heavy nucleus into lighter ones

Modern Physics — NUCLEAR FISSION — SPLITTING of a HEAVY NUCLEUS (e.g., URANIUM-235, PLUTONIUM-239) into TWO LIGHTER NUCLEI (fission products) + 2-3 NEUTRONS + ENORMOUS ENERGY (~200 MeV per fission). CHAIN REACTION: each fission releases 2-3 neutrons → trigger more fissions → exponential growth. CRITICAL MASS: minimum mass needed to sustain chain reaction (e.g., U-235 ~50 kg as sphere; reduced to ~15 kg with reflectors). APPLICATIONS: (1) NUCLEAR REACTORS — controlled fission (slow neutrons + control rods). (2) NUCLEAR WEAPONS — uncontrolled fission (atomic bomb). NUCLEAR FUSION — JOINING of light nuclei (e.g., H + H → He). Powers SUN + STARS; theoretically limitless clean energy if commercialized. CONTRAST: FISSION (split) vs FUSION (join). FUSION releases MORE energy/kg than fission. INDIA's NUCLEAR PROGRAMME: started 1948 under HOMI BHABHA ('father of Indian nuclear programme'). KEY MILESTONES: (1) 1956 — APSARA (1st reactor in Asia, BARC, Mumbai). (2) 1969 — TARAPUR (1st commercial nuclear power plant, with USA). (3) 1974 — POKHRAN-I 'Smiling Buddha' nuclear test. (4) 1998 — POKHRAN-II 5 tests. (5) 2008 — INDIA-USA NUCLEAR DEAL. UPSC angle: nuclear policy + Atomic Energy Commission. PYQ FREQUENCY: fission basics in NEET, JEE-Main 1-2× per cycle.

cards.front:
Which of these powers the SUN and stars?

(A) Nuclear fusion (Hydrogen → Helium)
(B) Nuclear fission (heavy element split)
(C) Chemical combustion of gases
(D) Gravitational collapse alone here
cards.back:
(A) Nuclear fusion (Hydrogen → Helium)

Modern Physics — THE SUN — powered by NUCLEAR FUSION in its CORE: HYDROGEN nuclei FUSE into HELIUM, releasing energy. PROCESS: PROTON-PROTON CHAIN (~99% of energy in SUN-like stars): (1) 2H + 2H → He-3 + γ. (2) Multiple steps eventually produce He-4. NET: 4H → He + 2 positrons + 2 neutrinos + 26.7 MeV ENERGY. LARGER STARS use CNO CYCLE (Carbon-Nitrogen-Oxygen catalytic cycle). SOLAR ENERGY: SUN converts ~620 million tonnes of H/sec into ~616 million tonnes of He; ~4 million tonnes of MASS converted to ENERGY (E=mc²) per second! Sun's lifetime fueling: ~5 billion more years. EARTH receives ~1.4 kW/m² of solar power (insolation). FUSION on EARTH (research): (1) TOKAMAK — magnetic confinement; e.g., ITER (France, multinational, target 2035 for first plasma; commercial fusion ~2050). (2) STELLARATOR — alternative magnetic design (Wendelstein 7-X, Germany). (3) INERTIAL CONFINEMENT — laser-fired fuel pellets (NIF, USA — achieved IGNITION Dec 2022). (4) INDIA: SST-1 (Steady State Tokamak-1, Gandhinagar); ITER member-country contributing. ADVANTAGES of fusion over fission: (a) NO long-lived radioactive waste. (b) FUEL is hydrogen — abundant. (c) NO meltdown risk. (d) Massive energy density. CHALLENGES: extreme temperatures (~150 million K) needed; magnetic confinement; net-energy gain elusive (most experiments INPUT > OUTPUT until 2022 NIF breakthrough). UPSC angle: India's energy security + clean energy. PYQ FREQUENCY: Sun = fusion in NEET, NCERT, SSC GA 1× per cycle.

cards.front:
INDIA's first NUCLEAR test was conducted in:

(A) 1974 ('Smiling Buddha', Pokhran)
(B) 1947 (year of independence)
(C) 1962 (China war year)
(D) 1998 (Pokhran-II tests)
cards.back:
(A) 1974 ('Smiling Buddha', Pokhran)

Modern Physics — POKHRAN-I (codenamed 'SMILING BUDDHA' / 'Operation Pokhran' / 'Pokhran-I') — INDIA's FIRST NUCLEAR TEST conducted on 18 MAY 1974 at POKHRAN test range, Rajasthan. PM: INDIRA GANDHI. Lead: HOMI SETHNA (Atomic Energy Commission Chair) + RAJA RAMANNA (Director, BARC). YIELD: ~8 KILOTONS (some estimates 12 kT). DESIGNATED: 'PEACEFUL NUCLEAR EXPLOSION' (PNE) by India — triggered international SANCTIONS but India maintained position. POKHRAN-II (Operation Shakti) — 5 tests conducted 11-13 MAY 1998 under PM ATAL BIHARI VAJPAYEE. 11 May: 3 tests (fission + boosted fission + thermonuclear/H-bomb claim). 13 May: 2 sub-kiloton tests. POKHRAN-II made India a DECLARED NUCLEAR-WEAPON STATE. RESPONSE: Pakistan reciprocated with 6 tests in May-June 1998 ('Chagai-I, II'). USA imposed sanctions; lifted gradually. INDIA-USA NUCLEAR DEAL (123 Agreement) — signed 2008 under Manmohan Singh + George W. Bush; allowed civil nuclear trade. NUCLEAR DOCTRINE of INDIA (declared 2003): (1) NO FIRST USE (NFU) — India will not initiate nuclear strike. (2) MASSIVE retaliation if attacked. (3) Non-use against non-nuclear states. (4) Continue to support GLOBAL DISARMAMENT. INDIA HAS NOT signed NPT (Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty, 1968) — considers it discriminatory. PYQ FREQUENCY: Pokhran tests in UPSC, SSC, NDA modern history 1-2× per cycle.

cards.front:
In a NUCLEAR REACTOR, the role of CONTROL RODS is to:

(A) Absorb neutrons + regulate reaction
(B) Generate fission energy directly
(C) Cool the reactor core constantly
(D) Convert heat to electricity here
cards.back:
(A) Absorb neutrons + regulate reaction

Modern Physics — NUCLEAR REACTOR COMPONENTS: (1) FUEL — typically enriched URANIUM-235 (~3-5% in commercial reactors) or PLUTONIUM-239. Forms FUEL RODS. (2) MODERATOR — slows neutrons (slow neutrons more efficient at causing U-235 fission). Common moderators: WATER (light), HEAVY WATER (D₂O — used in Indian PHWRs), GRAPHITE. (3) CONTROL RODS — ABSORB NEUTRONS to regulate chain reaction. Materials: BORON, CADMIUM, HAFNIUM, INDIUM. INSERT MORE → fewer free neutrons → reaction slows. WITHDRAW → more neutrons → reaction speeds up. EMERGENCY (SCRAM): all rods quickly inserted to halt reaction. (4) COOLANT — removes heat from core (water, gas, liquid sodium). (5) CONTAINMENT — concrete-steel shell prevents radiation leak. (6) STEAM GENERATOR / TURBINE — heat → steam → spins turbine → electricity. INDIA'S NUCLEAR REACTOR FLEET (as of 2024): 22 operational reactors at 7 sites; ~7,500 MW installed capacity. KEY SITES: TARAPUR (Maharashtra, 4 reactors), KAIGA (Karnataka, 4), KUDANKULAM (Tamil Nadu, 2 — Russia-built; more under construction), KAKRAPAR (Gujarat, 4), RAWATBHATA (Rajasthan, 6), NARORA (UP, 2). MOST INDIAN reactors are PHWRs (Pressurized Heavy Water Reactors, 'CANDU'-derived) — use NATURAL uranium + heavy-water moderator. INDIA's 3-STAGE NUCLEAR PROGRAMME (Bhabha Plan): (1) PHWR + natural uranium. (2) FAST BREEDER REACTORS using Pu-239. (3) THORIUM-based reactors (India has world's largest thorium reserves — Kerala beach sands). UPSC angle: nuclear energy + climate change. PYQ FREQUENCY: reactor components in NEET, JEE-Main, UPSC PT 1× per cycle.

cards.front:
Which is INDIA's LARGEST NUCLEAR POWER PLANT (by installed capacity)?

(A) Kudankulam (Tamil Nadu, ~2,000 MW)
(B) Tarapur (Maharashtra, oldest)
(C) Kakrapar (Gujarat, smaller)
(D) Narora (UP, only 2 reactors)
cards.back:
(A) Kudankulam (Tamil Nadu, ~2,000 MW)

Modern Physics — KUDANKULAM NUCLEAR POWER PLANT (KKNPP) — TIRUNELVELI district, TAMIL NADU; INDIA's largest single nuclear plant by capacity. CURRENT: 2 operational VVER-1000 reactors (Russian design); each ~1,000 MW = 2,000 MW total. Under construction: Units 3-6 (each 1,000 MW) — additional 4,000 MW; total planned ~6,000 MW (largest in India when complete). PARTNERSHIP: India + RUSSIA (Rosatom); started 1988 (cooperation MoU); construction Unit 1 began 2002, commissioning 2013. CONTROVERSY: massive PROTESTS by local fishermen + activists (~2011-12) over nuclear-safety concerns; SC dismissed petitions 2013, allowing operation. ALSO IMPORTANT: (1) RAWATBHATA (Rajasthan) — 6 PHWR units, 1,180 MW + Unit 7-8 under construction (1,400 MW). (2) TARAPUR (Maharashtra) — INDIA's OLDEST (commissioned 1969); 4 units total ~1,400 MW. (3) KAIGA (Karnataka) — 4 units, 880 MW. (4) KAKRAPAR (Gujarat) — 4 units, 880 MW. (5) NARORA (UP) — 2 units, 440 MW. INDIA's TOTAL: ~7,500 MW installed; ~3% of total electricity (vs ~10% in some countries; 70% in France). FUTURE TARGETS: 22,480 MW by 2031 (per Nuclear Power Corp). PWR programme: Kudankulam + Jaitapur (Maharashtra, with France) — large reactors. INDIGENOUS PHWR programme: Kakrapar 3-4 (700 MW each) commissioned 2023-24 — India's largest PHWRs. KEY ORGANIZATIONS: NPCIL (Nuclear Power Corp of India Ltd) — operates plants. AERB (Atomic Energy Regulatory Board) — safety. UPSC angle: nuclear power in India's energy mix. PYQ FREQUENCY: Indian nuclear plants in UPSC PT, SSC GA 1× per cycle.

cards.front:
EINSTEIN's MASS-ENERGY equation E = mc² shows that:

(A) Mass and energy are interchangeable
(B) Energy can never be destroyed only
(C) Mass increases with temperature
(D) Light has very high mass always
cards.back:
(A) Mass and energy are interchangeable

Modern Physics — E = mc² (Einstein, 1905, Special Relativity): MASS (m) and ENERGY (E) are EQUIVALENT and INTERCONVERTIBLE; c = speed of light (~3 × 10⁸ m/s). The c² factor is HUGE: 9 × 10¹⁶ m²/s² → 1 kg of mass converts to 9 × 10¹⁶ J ≈ 21.5 MEGATONS of TNT! NUCLEAR REACTIONS: a tiny mass-defect (mass of products < mass of reactants) is converted to enormous energy. KEY EXAMPLES: (1) FISSION: 1 g of U-235 fully fissioned → ~24,000 kWh of energy ≈ ~3 tonnes of coal. (2) FUSION: 1 g of D-T fusion → ~100,000 kWh ≈ 12 tonnes of coal. (3) HIROSHIMA bomb: ~700 mg mass converted, equivalent to ~15 KILOTONS TNT. (4) SUN: converts ~4 million tonnes mass/SECOND (already mentioned). REAL-WORLD VERIFICATION: nuclear reactors + accelerator experiments routinely confirm E=mc². ANNIHILATION: matter + antimatter → pure energy (full E=mc² conversion). 1 g of antimatter would yield 1 g × 2 × c² = ~50 megatons. ANTIMATTER PRODUCTION today: ~10⁻¹² grams/year (rare!). INDIA — BHABHA's HYPOTHESIS (1930s): high-energy cosmic rays carrying particles. EINSTEIN: visited India 1922 (briefly); INDIRA GANDHI's grandfather Motilal Nehru attended. PUBLIC AWARENESS: 'E=mc²' is the most famous equation in science. UPSC angle: science + tech in current affairs; energy-physics fundamentals. PYQ FREQUENCY: E=mc² basics in NEET, JEE-Main, NCERT 1× per cycle.

cards.front:
Which isotope is mostly used as FUEL in commercial nuclear reactors?

(A) Uranium-235 (natural ~0.7%)
(B) Uranium-238 (cannot fission)
(C) Hydrogen-1 (proton only here)
(D) Carbon-12 (stable carbon)
cards.back:
(A) Uranium-235 (natural ~0.7%)

Modern Physics — URANIUM-235 (U-235) — primary fuel for most commercial nuclear reactors. KEY: U-235 is FISSILE (can sustain chain reaction with thermal neutrons); U-238 (more abundant) is NOT fissile but FERTILE (can absorb neutron + decay to PLUTONIUM-239, which IS fissile). NATURAL URANIUM composition: ~99.27% U-238 + ~0.72% U-235 + traces U-234. ENRICHMENT: most reactors need 3-5% U-235 (LWRs); WEAPONS need ~90% (HEU, Highly Enriched). India's PHWRs use NATURAL uranium (no enrichment) thanks to heavy-water moderator. ENRICHMENT METHODS: (1) GASEOUS DIFFUSION (old). (2) GAS CENTRIFUGES (modern; India + Iran + many use this). (3) LASER ENRICHMENT (research). KEY ISOTOPES + ROLES: (1) U-235 — FISSILE (used in reactors + bombs). (2) U-238 — FERTILE (breeder reactor fuel). (3) Pu-239 — FISSILE (weapons-grade; bred from U-238). (4) Th-232 — FERTILE (can breed U-233). (5) U-233 — FISSILE (from Th breeding). INDIA's THORIUM ADVANTAGE: ~25% of world's thorium reserves (Kerala monazite sands; ~5 lakh tonnes). 3-STAGE PROGRAMME aims to use thorium in stage 3. RECENT: KAKRAPAR-3 commissioned 2023 — INDIGENOUS 700 MW PHWR. FUEL RODS: enriched UO₂ pellets stacked in zircaloy tubes; bundle of rods = fuel assembly. SPENT FUEL → cooled in pools → reprocessed (BARC's Tarapur reprocessing). NUCLEAR WASTE: glassified high-level waste; storage at Tarapur, Kalpakkam. UPSC angle: nuclear materials + non-proliferation; India's strategic posture. PYQ FREQUENCY: U-235 in NEET, JEE-Main, NCERT 1× per cycle.

cards.front:
The nucleus of an atom contains:

(A) Electrons and protons
(B) Protons (positive charge) and neutrons (neutral) — collectively called nucleons
(C) Neutrons and electrons
(D) Only protons
cards.back:
(B) Protons (positive charge) and neutrons (neutral) — collectively called nucleons

Modern Physics — Atomic structure: NUCLEUS (protons + neutrons; ~10⁻¹⁵ m, 99.9% of atomic mass); ELECTRONS orbit nucleus (~10⁻¹⁰ m). Atomic number Z = number of protons. Mass number A = protons + neutrons. ISOTOPES — same Z, different A (e.g., ¹H, ²H/D, ³H/T; ²³⁵U, ²³⁸U). Strong nuclear force binds nucleons (~100x electromagnetic; very short range, ~1 fm). Discoveries — Rutherford 1911 (nucleus, α-scattering); Chadwick 1932 (neutron); Anderson 1932 (positron, antimatter); Pauli 1930 / Reines-Cowan 1956 (neutrino).

cards.front:
The half-life of a radioactive substance is:

(A) The total lifetime of the substance
(B) The time taken for HALF of the original radioactive nuclei to decay (a constant for each isotope)
(C) The time it takes to be detected
(D) Half the time of one full radioactive cycle
cards.back:
(B) The time taken for HALF of the original radioactive nuclei to decay (a constant for each isotope)

Modern Physics — Half-life (T½) — time for half the original nuclei to decay. Constant for a given isotope (independent of physical/chemical conditions). After n half-lives, the surviving fraction = (1/2)ⁿ. Decay constant λ = ln 2 / T½. Activity A = λN; measured in becquerel (Bq, 1 decay/s) or curie (Ci = 3.7 × 10¹⁰ Bq).

cards.front:
In nuclear FISSION (used in nuclear reactors and atom bombs):

(A) Two light nuclei fuse to form a heavier nucleus
(B) A heavy nucleus (e.g., U-235) splits into two lighter nuclei + neutrons + energy
(C) An electron is emitted from the nucleus
(D) Atoms simply rearrange chemically
cards.back:
(B) A heavy nucleus (e.g., U-235) splits into two lighter nuclei + neutrons + energy

Modern Physics — FISSION — heavy nucleus splits. Discovered 1938 by Otto Hahn + Lise Meitner + Fritz Strassmann. Example: ²³⁵U + n → ¹⁴¹Ba + ⁹²Kr + 3n + ~200 MeV energy. Released neutrons can trigger further fissions → CHAIN REACTION. Critical mass — minimum mass for sustained chain reaction (uranium-235 ~52 kg sphere; can be smaller with reflector). Atom bomb (uncontrolled chain reaction); nuclear reactor (controlled, with moderator + control rods). Hiroshima 'Little Boy' (Aug 6, 1945) — U-235 gun-type. Nagasaki 'Fat Man' (Aug 9, 1945) — Pu-239 implosion-type. FUSION (opposite) — light nuclei combine; powers stars, hydrogen bomb, tokamak research (ITER). E = mc² governs both.

cards.option2: An electron is emitted from the nucleus

cards.front:
Einstein's famous equation E = mc² describes:

(A) Speed of sound
(B) Mass-energy equivalence — even tiny mass converts to enormous energy (since c² is huge)
(C) Newton's second law
(D) Wave equation
cards.back:
(B) Mass-energy equivalence — even tiny mass converts to enormous energy (since c² is huge)

Modern Physics — E = mc² (c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s). 1 g of matter converted entirely to energy = (10⁻³)(3×10⁸)² = 9 × 10¹³ J ≈ 21,500 tons of TNT (= about Hiroshima yield). In nuclear reactions, only a small fraction (~0.1%) of mass converts. MASS DEFECT — the mass of a nucleus is slightly less than the sum of its individual nucleons; the missing mass appears as binding energy. Iron-56 has the highest binding energy per nucleon — fusion + fission both move toward Fe-56 → release energy. Stars: hydrogen → helium fusion (proton-proton chain in sun, CNO cycle in heavier stars); supernovae produce elements heavier than iron via r-process.

cards.front:
The MOST common moderator used in Indian PHWR (Pressurised Heavy Water Reactor) nuclear reactors is:

(A) Graphite
(B) Heavy water (D₂O)
(C) Light water (H₂O)
(D) Liquid sodium
cards.back:
(B) Heavy water (D₂O)

Modern Physics — MODERATOR — slows down neutrons (fast neutrons → thermal neutrons, more likely to cause fission of U-235). Common moderators: HEAVY WATER (D₂O — used in PHWRs / CANDU; expensive but allows use of natural uranium without enrichment). LIGHT WATER (H₂O — used in PWR/BWR; cheaper but absorbs more neutrons → requires enriched U-235); GRAPHITE (used in earlier UK Magnox + Soviet RBMK; Chernobyl was graphite-moderated). India's nuclear programme — 3-stage: Stage 1 PHWR with natural U; Stage 2 fast breeder with Pu + thorium; Stage 3 thorium-based reactors. Tarapur was the first nuclear power plant (1969, BWR design from US). India has 23 operational reactors (~7,500 MWe, ~3% of grid). Kudankulam (TN) — VVER design with Russia.

cards.front:
When a radioactive nucleus emits an ALPHA particle, the resulting nucleus has:

(A) Same atomic number, same mass number
(B) Atomic number reduced by 2; mass number reduced by 4
(C) Atomic number increased by 1; mass number unchanged
(D) Atomic number reduced by 1; mass number unchanged
cards.back:
(B) Atomic number reduced by 2; mass number reduced by 4

Modern Physics — Alpha (α) particle = helium nucleus (2 protons + 2 neutrons; ⁴₂He). Alpha decay: ᴬ₂X → ᴬ⁻⁴₂₋₂Y + ⁴₂He. Example: ²³⁸U → ²³⁴Th + α. BETA-MINUS (β⁻) decay: a neutron in the nucleus becomes a proton + electron + antineutrino → atomic number INCREASES by 1; mass number unchanged. Example: ¹⁴C → ¹⁴N + e⁻ + ν̄. BETA-PLUS (β⁺): proton → neutron + positron + neutrino → atomic number decreases by 1. GAMMA (γ) decay: high-energy photon emitted; no change in atomic or mass number — nucleus drops from excited to ground state. Penetrating power: α (stopped by paper) < β (stopped by aluminium foil) < γ (needs lead/concrete).

cards.front:
If 8 g of a radioactive substance has a half-life of 4 days, how much will remain after 16 days?

(A) 1 g
(B) 0.5 g
(C) 2 g
(D) 4 g
cards.back:
(B) 0.5 g

Modern Physics — 16 days = 4 half-lives (16 / 4 = 4). After n half-lives, the remaining fraction = (1/2)ⁿ = (1/2)⁴ = 1/16. Remaining = 8 × 1/16 = 0.5 g. Step-wise: Day 0 → 8 g; Day 4 → 4 g; Day 8 → 2 g; Day 12 → 1 g; Day 16 → 0.5 g. Note — the decay is exponential, not linear; after 4 half-lives, ~93.75% has decayed.

cards.front:
Radioactivity was DISCOVERED in 1896 by:

(A) Marie Curie, who later isolated radium
(B) Henri Becquerel, while studying uranium salts
(C) Ernest Rutherford, who studied alpha decay
(D) Albert Einstein, who explained mass-energy
cards.back:
(B) Henri Becquerel, while studying uranium salts

Modern Physics — Henri Becquerel — Paris, 1896. Found that uranium salts emitted rays that fogged photographic plates, even in the dark, without external excitation. MARIE + PIERRE CURIE later (1898) isolated polonium + radium, coined 'radioactivity'. RUTHERFORD distinguished alpha + beta + gamma rays (1899-1903). All four (Becquerel + Curies + Rutherford) won Nobel Prizes; Marie Curie won twice (Physics 1903, Chemistry 1911).

cards.front:
Three types of radioactive emission have characteristic CHARGES:

(A) All three carry positive charge equally
(B) Alpha +2, Beta −1, Gamma uncharged (zero)
(C) Alpha −2, Beta +1, Gamma carries positive charge
(D) All three are completely uncharged in nature
cards.back:
(B) Alpha +2, Beta −1, Gamma uncharged (zero)

Modern Physics — Charges: ALPHA = +2 (helium nucleus, 2 protons + 2 neutrons); BETA-MINUS = −1 (electron); GAMMA = 0 (photon, electromagnetic radiation). Penetrating power inversely related to mass + charge: α (stopped by paper) < β (Al foil) < γ (lead/concrete). Ionising power opposite: α > β > γ. Identifying via deflection in magnetic field: α and β deflect oppositely; γ doesn't deflect.

cards.front:
Carbon-14 dating is used to estimate the age of organic remains. Its half-life is approximately:

(A) 100 years, useful for medieval dating
(B) 5,730 years, useful up to ~50,000 years old
(C) 1 million years, useful for fossil dating
(D) 4.5 billion years, the age of the Earth
cards.back:
(B) 5,730 years, useful up to ~50,000 years old

Modern Physics — Carbon-14 (¹⁴C) — radioactive isotope of carbon. Half-life ~5,730 years. Continuously formed in upper atmosphere (cosmic rays + N-14); incorporated into living organisms. After death, no new ¹⁴C taken in; existing ¹⁴C decays. Measure ¹⁴C/¹²C ratio → estimate time since death. RANGE: ~50,000 years (after that, too little ¹⁴C left to measure). For older artefacts: K-Ar (potassium-argon) for million-year scale; U-Pb for billions of years (rocks, Earth's age). Distractor 4 = U-238 half-life (4.47 billion yrs).

When a nucleus emits an ALPHA particle, its mass number decreases by 4 and atomic number by:

(A) 1 unit (one proton lost from nucleus)
(B) 2 units (two protons lost from nucleus)
(C) 0 units (no proton change in alpha)
(D) 4 units (matches mass number drop)
cards.back:
(B) 2 units (two protons lost from nucleus)

Beta-minus emission: atomic number INCREASES by 1 (neutron → proton + electron + antineutrino), mass number unchanged. Beta-plus / positron emission: atomic number DECREASES by 1. Gamma emission: no change in either.

cards.front:
If 16 g of a radioactive substance is left after 4 half-lives, the original amount was:

(A) 64 g, four times the remaining mass
(B) 256 g, sixteen times the remaining mass
(C) 32 g, two times the remaining mass
(D) 128 g, eight times the remaining mass
cards.back:
(B) 256 g, sixteen times the remaining mass

Modern Physics — After n half-lives, remaining = original × (1/2)ⁿ. 4 half-lives → remaining = 1/16 of original. 16 g = original/16 → original = 256 g. Verify: 256 → 128 (1 HL) → 64 (2) → 32 (3) → 16 (4). Distractor 1 = 64 g would be after 2 HL. Distractor 3 = 32 g after 1 HL. Distractor 4 = 128 g is 1 HL stop short.

cards.front:
Cobalt-60, used in cancer radiotherapy, primarily emits which type of radiation for treatment?

(A) Alpha particles, for surface tumours only
(B) Gamma rays, with high penetrating power
(C) Beta particles, suitable for skin cancers
(D) Neutrons, for boron neutron capture therapy
cards.back:
(B) Gamma rays, with high penetrating power

Modern Physics — Cobalt-60 (Co-60) — emits BETA particles + GAMMA rays. The high-energy GAMMA rays (1.17 + 1.33 MeV) are used in EXTERNAL BEAM RADIOTHERAPY for cancer (high penetration → reach deep tumours). Half-life 5.27 years. Also used in food irradiation (sterilisation), industrial radiography, sterilising medical equipment. Distractor 1 — alpha can't penetrate skin; not used externally. Distractor 3 — beta in some skin therapies but not main Co-60 use. Distractor 4 — different therapy (BNCT, uses boron + thermal neutrons).

cards.front:
The SI unit of radioactivity (decays per second) is the:

(A) Curie (Ci), an older unit of activity
(B) Becquerel (Bq), one decay per second
(C) Sievert (Sv), a unit of dose equivalent
(D) Gray (Gy), a unit of absorbed dose
cards.back:
(B) Becquerel (Bq), one decay per second

Modern Physics — BECQUEREL (Bq) — SI unit of radioactivity = 1 disintegration per second. Named after Henri Becquerel. Older non-SI unit: CURIE (Ci) = 3.7 × 10¹⁰ Bq (activity of 1 g of radium-226). SIEVERT (Sv) — biological dose equivalent (effective biological damage). GRAY (Gy) — absorbed dose (energy/kg deposited in tissue). Annual safe limit for general public: ~1 mSv (excluding natural background ~2.4 mSv).

cards.front:
Which type of radioactive radiation has the highest penetrating power?

(A) Alpha (α)
(B) Gamma (γ)
(C) Beta (β)
(D) Positron
cards.back:

Modern Physics — Gamma rays — massless, no charge, electromagnetic waves of very short wavelength — pass through paper, aluminium, even centimetres of lead. Ionising power inverts — alpha > beta > gamma.

cards.front:
The 'half-life' of a radioactive isotope is the time needed for:

(A) All the atoms to decay
(B) Half of the atoms to decay
(C) The activity to double
(D) One gram to decay
cards.back:
(B) Half of the atoms to decay

Half-lives span many orders of magnitude — Uranium-238: 4.5 billion years (age of the Earth); Carbon-14: 5,730 years (used for dating organic remains); Iodine-131: 8 days (used in thyroid scans). cards.front:
In nuclear FISSION, energy is released when:

(A) Two light nuclei combine
(B) A heavy nucleus splits into lighter ones
(C) An electron absorbs a photon
(D) A gas condenses to a liquid
cards.back:
(B) A heavy nucleus splits into lighter ones

Modern Physics — Fission — a heavy nucleus (e.g., Uranium-235) absorbs a slow neutron and splits into two smaller nuclei + more neutrons + energy. The energy comes from mass-defect — the products weigh slightly less than the reactants; the missing mass is released as energy via E = mc². A single fission of U-235 releases ~200 MeV. Self-sustaining chain reactions power reactors and (uncontrolled) atom bombs. Fusion combines light nuclei (e.g., H → He in the Sun).

cards.front:
Nuclear FUSION — the process that powers the Sun — requires:

(A) Extremely low temperature
(B) Extremely high temperature and pressure
(C) A neutron source
(D) High magnetic flux
cards.back:
(B) Extremely high temperature and pressure

Modern Physics — Fusion needs temperatures of ~15 million K (Sun's core) or ~100-200 million K (in an experimental reactor like ITER) so nuclei have enough kinetic energy to overcome their Coulomb repulsion and get close enough for the strong nuclear force to bind them. Magnetic confinement (tokamaks, stellarators) and inertial confinement (laser implosion) are the two main experimental approaches on Earth. ITER (France, under construction) is the world's largest fusion project.

cards.front:
The radioactive isotope used for carbon dating of archaeological samples is:

(A) Carbon-12
(B) Carbon-14
(C) Carbon-13
(D) Potassium-40
cards.back:
(B) Carbon-14

Modern Physics — C-14 — produced continuously in the upper atmosphere by cosmic rays; absorbed by plants (CO₂) and then animals. After death, no new C-14 is added, and the existing C-14 decays with a half-life of 5,730 years. Measuring the ratio C-14 / C-12 gives the age of organic remains. Useful up to ~50,000 years (7 half-lives; after that, too little C-14 remains to measure). Potassium-argon dating is used for much older (volcanic) rock.

cards.front:
SEMICONDUCTORS like silicon have:

(A) Conductivity higher than copper metal
(B) Conductivity between conductors and insulators
(C) Conductivity equal to glass insulator
(D) Conductivity decreases with increasing temperature
cards.back:
(B) Conductivity between conductors and insulators

Modern Physics — SEMICONDUCTOR — material with conductivity BETWEEN good conductors (Cu, Ag) and good insulators (glass, rubber). Examples: Silicon (Si), Germanium (Ge), GaAs. Energy band gap small (~1.1 eV for Si). Conductivity INCREASES with temperature (opposite to metals — hence 'negative temperature coefficient of resistance'). Adding impurities (DOPING) can drastically change conductivity. Foundation of electronics — diodes, transistors, ICs, solar cells, LEDs all built from semiconductors.

cards.front:
Adding small amounts of impurities to a pure semiconductor (DOPING) is done to:

(A) Decrease its conductivity drastically
(B) Greatly increase its conductivity
(C) Keep its conductivity unchanged
(D) Convert it into an insulator type
cards.back:
(B) Greatly increase its conductivity

Modern Physics — Pure semiconductor (intrinsic Si) — low conductivity. DOPING (~1 part per million) → boosts conductivity by ORDERS of magnitude. Two types: N-TYPE — dope with PENTAVALENT atom (P, As, Sb): 5 valence electrons; 4 bond, 1 free → extra ELECTRONS; e is majority carrier. P-TYPE — dope with TRIVALENT atom (B, Al, Ga, In): 3 valence electrons → leaves a 'HOLE' (missing electron); hole is majority carrier. Combining n + p → P-N JUNCTION = the basic DIODE.
cards.option3: Convert it into an insulator type

cards.front:
A P-N JUNCTION DIODE allows current to flow:

(A) Only when reverse-biased always at all
(B) Mainly when forward-biased (p+, n−)
(C) Equally well in both directions of bias
(D) Only when there is no applied voltage
cards.back:
(B) Mainly when forward-biased (p+, n−)

Modern Physics — DIODE — one-way valve for current. FORWARD BIAS: p-side connected to + terminal, n-side to − terminal → low resistance, current flows easily. REVERSE BIAS: p to −, n to + → very high resistance, almost no current. (At very high reverse voltage, breakdown occurs — Zener / avalanche.) Used as RECTIFIER (AC → DC). Half-wave (1 diode) + full-wave (4 diodes in bridge) rectifiers. Diode symbol: triangle pointing toward bar.

cards.front:
An LED (Light-Emitting Diode) emits light when:

(A) Heated above its critical temperature
(B) Forward-biased; electrons recombine with holes
(C) Reverse-biased till the breakdown level
(D) Lit by sunlight on its outer surface
cards.back:
(B) Forward-biased; electrons recombine with holes

Modern Physics — LED — special diode. When FORWARD-BIASED, electrons + holes recombine at the junction; energy released as PHOTONS (light). Colour depends on semiconductor's BAND GAP: red = GaAsP, green = GaP, blue = InGaN, white = blue LED + yellow phosphor (or 3-LED mix). Inventors of efficient blue LED — Akasaki, Amano, Nakamura (Nobel 2014). Why LED is replacing incandescent: ~10× more efficient (no heat loss), longer life, lower cost. Indian UJALA scheme (2015) sold ~370 million LEDs at low price, big energy saver.

cards.front:
The TRANSISTOR was invented in 1947 at:

(A) Stanford University in California
(B) Bell Labs (Bardeen, Brattain, Shockley)
(C) MIT in Cambridge, Massachusetts
(D) Cambridge University in England UK
cards.back:
(B) Bell Labs (Bardeen, Brattain, Shockley)

Modern Physics — TRANSISTOR — invented at BELL LABS (USA), Dec 1947, by John BARDEEN, Walter BRATTAIN, William SHOCKLEY. Nobel Prize 1956. Replaced vacuum tubes — smaller, cheaper, more reliable, much less power. Started the electronics revolution. Transistor types: BJT (Bipolar Junction — n-p-n or p-n-p), FET (Field-Effect), MOSFET (Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor FET — used in modern ICs). Modern CPU has BILLIONS of MOSFETs (e.g., Apple M-series chip: ~50-100 billion transistors). MOORE'S LAW — transistor count doubles every ~2 years (slowing now).

cards.front:
A SOLAR CELL converts:

(A) Heat energy into electrical energy
(B) Light energy into electrical energy
(C) Mechanical work into electrical energy
(D) Chemical energy into electricity from cells
cards.back:
(B) Light energy into electrical energy

Modern Physics — SOLAR CELL (photovoltaic cell, PV) — converts LIGHT directly into electricity using PHOTOELECTRIC effect. Made of doped silicon (p-n junction). Sunlight photons free electrons; junction's electric field separates them → current flows. Efficiency: typical Si cells ~15-22%. Theoretical max for single junction ~33% (Shockley-Queisser limit). Solar Mission of India: 100 GW solar by 2022 (target met partly), now aiming 500 GW by 2030. Bhadla Solar Park (Rajasthan) — among world's largest. Distractor 1 = thermoelectric. Distractor 4 = battery.

cards.front:
Common P-type DOPANT for silicon (adding 'holes' to it) is:

(A) Phosphorus, the pentavalent element
(B) Boron, the trivalent element
(C) Carbon, also tetravalent like Si
(D) Oxygen, with 6 outer electrons
cards.back:
(B) Boron, the trivalent element

Modern Physics — P-TYPE doping: add TRIVALENT atoms (3 valence electrons) like BORON (B), Aluminium (Al), Gallium (Ga), Indium (In). Creates 'HOLES' — missing electrons that act like positive charge carriers. N-TYPE doping: add PENTAVALENT atoms (5 valence electrons) like PHOSPHORUS (P), Arsenic (As), Antimony (Sb). cards.front:
The SI (Système International) has how many BASE UNITS?

(A) 5
(B) SEVEN
(C) 9
(D) 12
cards.back:
(B) SEVEN

Units & Measurements — THE SEVEN SI BASE UNITS (rebased in 2019 on physical constants): | Quantity | Unit | Symbol | (1) LENGTH = metre (m); (2) MASS = kilogram (kg); (3) TIME = second (s); (4) ELECTRIC CURRENT = ampere (A); (5) TEMPERATURE = kelvin (K); (6) AMOUNT OF SUBSTANCE = mole (mol); (7) LUMINOUS INTENSITY = candela (cd). MNEMONIC: 'Some Kids Must Sail Around To Canada' (S-K-M-S-A-T-C → s, kg, m, s, A, T→K, cd) or 'MKS A K mol cd'. 2019 REDEFINITION: on 20 May 2019 (World Metrology Day), all 7 SI base units were redefined in terms of 7 PHYSICAL CONSTANTS (fixed exact values): (a) Caesium frequency Δνₛ Cs (second); (b) Speed of light c (metre); (c) Planck constant h (kilogram — replaced the last physical artifact, the Sèvres cylinder!); (d) Elementary charge e (ampere); (e) Boltzmann constant k (kelvin); (f) Avogadro number NA (mole); (g) Luminous efficacy Kcd (candela). KILOGRAM was the LAST base unit tied to a physical artefact (IPK — International Prototype of the Kilogram, a 1889 platinum-iridium cylinder in Sèvres, Paris); now defined by Planck's constant via the Kibble balance. SI also has 2 SUPPLEMENTARY units (dimensionless): RADIAN (plane angle) + STERADIAN (solid angle) — now classified as derived. metre, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, mole, candela.

cards.front:
The SI unit of FORCE is:

(A) Joule (J)
(B) NEWTON (N) = kg·m/s² — force required to accelerate a 1 kg mass by 1 m/s²
(C) Watt (W)
(D) Pascal (Pa)
cards.back:
(B) NEWTON (N) = kg·m/s² — force required to accelerate a 1 kg mass by 1 m/s²

Units & Measurements — NEWTON (N) — SI UNIT of FORCE, named after SIR ISAAC NEWTON. DEFINITION: 1 N = force needed to accelerate a 1 kg mass at 1 m/s². Dimensional formula: [M L T⁻²]. EXAMPLES: a 100-gram apple weighs ~1 N on Earth (mg = 0.1 × 9.8 ≈ 0.98 N); a 10 kg mass weighs ~98 N; an adult's body weight (70 kg) ≈ 686 N. KEY DERIVED SI UNITS: (1) JOULE (J) = N·m = kg·m²/s² → ENERGY / WORK (James Prescott Joule). (2) WATT (W) = J/s → POWER (James Watt); 1 horsepower ≈ 746 W. (3) PASCAL (Pa) = N/m² → PRESSURE (Blaise Pascal); atmospheric pressure ~101325 Pa = 1.013 bar = 760 mmHg. (4) HERTZ (Hz) = s⁻¹ → FREQUENCY (Heinrich Hertz). (5) COULOMB (C) = A·s → ELECTRIC CHARGE. (6) VOLT (V) = W/A = J/C → ELECTRIC POTENTIAL. (7) OHM (Ω) = V/A → RESISTANCE. (8) FARAD (F) = C/V → CAPACITANCE. (9) TESLA (T) = Wb/m² → MAGNETIC FLUX DENSITY. (10) WEBER (Wb) = V·s → MAGNETIC FLUX. (11) LUMEN (lm), LUX (lx) → LIGHT. (12) BECQUEREL (Bq), GRAY (Gy), SIEVERT (Sv) → RADIOACTIVITY. All named SI derived units are named after SCIENTISTS. Dyne (CGS) = 10⁻⁵ N; pound-force (Imperial) ≈ 4.448 N.

cards.front:
The SI unit of ELECTRIC CURRENT is the AMPERE (A). After the 2019 redefinition, one ampere is defined in terms of:

(A) Flow between two parallel wires
(B) The FIXED VALUE of the ELEMENTARY CHARGE e = 1.602176634 × 10⁻¹⁹ C; 1 A = flow of (1/e) elementary charges per second
(C) Mass of copper deposited in electrolysis
(D) Faraday's constant
cards.back:
(B) The FIXED VALUE of the ELEMENTARY CHARGE e = 1.602176634 × 10⁻¹⁹ C; 1 A = flow of (1/e) elementary charges per second

Units & Measurements — AMPERE (A) — SI UNIT of ELECTRIC CURRENT, named after ANDRÉ-MARIE AMPÈRE. 2019 REDEFINITION (20 May 2019): The ampere is defined by taking the FIXED NUMERICAL VALUE of the ELEMENTARY CHARGE e to be exactly 1.602176634 × 10⁻¹⁹ C (coulomb), where the coulomb = A·s. So 1 AMPERE = flow of 1/(1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹) = ~6.2415 × 10¹⁸ elementary charges per second. OLD (pre-2019) DEFINITION: 'that constant current which, when maintained in two straight parallel conductors of infinite length + negligible cross-section, placed 1 metre apart in vacuum, produces a force of 2 × 10⁻⁷ N per metre of length between them' (based on Ampere's force law). The old definition tied ampere to μ₀ (permeability of free space, exact by definition = 4π × 10⁻⁷). NEW definition frees μ₀ to be a measured quantity. OHM'S LAW: V = IR. 1 A is a SIGNIFICANT current — lethal through heart can be as low as 50 mA; household mains fuse at 6/16/32 A; 1000 A is industrial welding scale; lightning bolt can carry 30,000 A. MILLIAMPERE (mA) = 10⁻³ A; MICROAMPERE (µA) = 10⁻⁶ A.

cards.front:
The SI unit of PRESSURE is:

(A) Newton (N)
(B) PASCAL (Pa) = N/m²
(C) Bar
(D) Torr
cards.back:
(B) PASCAL (Pa) = N/m²

Units & Measurements — PASCAL (Pa) — SI unit of PRESSURE + STRESS. 1 Pa = 1 N/m² = 1 kg·m⁻¹·s⁻². NAMED after BLAISE PASCAL (1623-1662), French mathematician/physicist. PASCAL IS A SMALL UNIT — atmospheric pressure at sea level ≈ 1,01,325 Pa = 101.325 kPa = 1.013 bar. Common pressure multiples: kilopascal (kPa = 10³ Pa), megapascal (MPa = 10⁶ Pa), gigapascal (GPa = 10⁹ Pa — material strengths). OTHER PRESSURE UNITS: (1) BAR = 10⁵ Pa (meteorology + industry); millibar (mb) = 100 Pa = 1 hPa (weather maps). (2) ATMOSPHERE (atm) = 101,325 Pa. (3) TORR = 1/760 atm ≈ 133.3 Pa (vacuum). (4) mmHg = 1 Torr (blood pressure, barometers — normal BP 120/80 mmHg = 16/10.7 kPa). (5) PSI (pound per square inch) ≈ 6,895 Pa (tire pressure, US industry; car tire ~30 psi). BOYLE'S LAW: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂ (isothermal). PASCAL'S LAW: pressure applied to an enclosed fluid transmits equally in all directions (hydraulic press, brake). ARCHIMEDES' PRINCIPLE: buoyant force = weight of fluid displaced. At Mt Everest summit (8,848m), atm pressure drops to ~33% of sea-level value — why climbers need oxygen. Mariana Trench bottom (~11 km) pressure ~1,100 atm.

cards.front:
One LIGHT-YEAR is approximately equal to:

(A) One trillion kilometres
(B) 9.461 × 10¹² km ≈ 9.46 TRILLION KILOMETRES
(C) 365 million km
(D) Same as 1 astronomical unit
cards.back:
(B) 9.461 × 10¹² km ≈ 9.46 TRILLION KILOMETRES

Units & Measurements — LIGHT-YEAR (ly) — DISTANCE (not time!) that light travels in one Julian year in vacuum. CALCULATION: speed of light c = 299,792,458 m/s ≈ 3 × 10⁸ m/s; seconds in a year = 365.25 × 24 × 3600 = 31,557,600 s; distance = c × t ≈ 9.461 × 10¹⁵ m = 9,461,000,000,000 km ≈ 9.46 TRILLION km ≈ 5.88 trillion miles. EXAMPLES: (a) Sun is ~8.3 LIGHT-MINUTES from Earth (not years). (b) PROXIMA CENTAURI (nearest star to the Sun) is 4.24 ly. (c) MILKY WAY galaxy diameter ~100,000 ly. (d) ANDROMEDA GALAXY (M31) ~2.5 million ly. (e) Observable universe diameter ~93 BILLION ly. OTHER ASTRONOMICAL DISTANCES: (1) ASTRONOMICAL UNIT (AU) = mean Earth-Sun distance = 149,597,870,700 m ≈ 150 million km. 1 ly ≈ 63,241 AU. (2) PARSEC (pc) = 3.26 ly ≈ 3.086 × 10¹⁶ m — distance at which 1 AU subtends 1 arcsecond; used in professional astronomy. 1 kiloparsec (kpc), 1 megaparsec (Mpc). (3) LIGHT-YEAR vs CENTURY in popular media: confusingly used 'I'll wait a light-year' is wrong — light-year is distance. HUBBLE CONSTANT: ~70 km/s/Mpc — measures rate of universe's expansion. REDSHIFT is how distant galaxies are measured. distance light travels in 1 year in vacuum at 3 × 10⁸ m/s.

cards.front:
HORSEPOWER (1 HP, the unit used for engines) equals approximately:

(A) 100 W
(B) 746 W
(C) 1000 W
(D) 1 kilowatt exactly
cards.back:
(B) 746 W

Units & Measurements — HORSEPOWER (HP) — originally defined by JAMES WATT in the 1780s as a way to market his improved steam engines to replace horses. He estimated a pit pony could lift 22,000 foot-pounds/min; multiplied by 1.5 to be safe → 33,000 foot-pounds/min = 550 foot-pounds/sec = 746 W (mechanical HP). VARIANTS: (1) MECHANICAL HP (imperial) = 745.70 W — US + UK engine ratings; (2) METRIC HP (PS / CV / cheval vapeur) = 735.5 W — continental Europe, India, Japan; (3) Electrical HP = 746 W exactly (used for electric motor ratings). DIFFERENCE: manufacturer spec sheets: a car rated 100 PS (metric) = 98.6 HP (mechanical); significant for marketing. EXAMPLES: (a) Peak human sprint ~1.2 HP briefly; sustained cycling ~0.1 HP. (b) Honda Activa ~8 HP; Maruti Alto ~67 HP; Toyota Fortuner ~200 HP; F1 car ~1000 HP. (c) Boeing 777 engine ~100,000 HP each. (d) 1 HP air-conditioner = 1 TON cooling in loose Indian usage (technically 1 ton refrigeration = 3.517 kW = 4.71 HP — i.e., '1 Ton AC' ≈ 3.5 kW, but 'horsepower rating' on inverters uses diff scale). SI UNIT: WATT (W) is the proper SI unit of power; 1 kW = 1000 W. 1 kWh (kilowatt-hour) = energy consumed by 1 kW load for 1 hr = 3.6 MJ — your electricity bill 'unit'. metric HP = 735.5 W; imperial/mechanical HP = 745.7 W.

DIFFERENCE: manufacturer spec sheets: a car rated 100 PS (metric) = 98.6 HP (mechanical); significant for marketing. EXAMPLES: (a) Peak human sprint ~1.2 HP briefly; sustained cycling ~0.1 HP. (b) Honda Activa ~8 HP; Maruti Alto ~67 HP; Toyota Fortuner ~200 HP; F1 car ~1000 HP. (c) Boeing 777 engine ~100,000 HP each. (d) 1 HP air-conditioner = 1 TON cooling in loose Indian usage (technically 1 ton refrigeration = 3.517 kW = 4.71 HP — i.e., '1 Ton AC' ≈ 3.5 kW, but 'horsepower rating' on inverters uses diff scale). SI UNIT: WATT (W) is the proper SI unit of power; 1 kW = 1000 W. 1 kWh (kilowatt-hour) = energy consumed by 1 kW load for 1 hr = 3.6 MJ — your electricity bill 'unit'. metric HP = 735.5 W; imperial/mechanical HP = 745.7 W.

cards.front:
0 KELVIN (absolute zero) corresponds to approximately what Celsius temperature?

(A) 0°C
(B) −273.15 °C
(C) −100°C
(D) −459.67°C
cards.back:
(B) −273.15 °C

Units & Measurements — ABSOLUTE ZERO: the LOWEST possible temperature, where classical molecular motion CEASES (quantum zero-point energy remains). 0 K = −273.15 °C = −459.67 °F. TEMPERATURE SCALE CONVERSIONS: (1) K = °C + 273.15. (2) °C = (°F − 32) × 5/9. (3) °F = °C × 9/5 + 32. KEY POINTS: (a) Water FREEZES at 0°C = 273.15 K = 32°F (at 1 atm). (b) Water BOILS at 100°C = 373.15 K = 212°F (at 1 atm). (c) Human body temp ~37°C = 310.15 K = 98.6°F. (d) Room temp ~25°C = 298.15 K = 77°F. COLDEST NATURAL: Vostok, Antarctica −89.2°C (1983); LOWEST LAB temp: ~38 picokelvin (fraction above 0 K) achieved by Bose-Einstein condensates. DEEP SPACE cosmic microwave background temp ~2.725 K. 3rd LAW OF THERMODYNAMICS: absolute zero is UNATTAINABLE — can approach it asymptotically. ABSOLUTE ZERO was extrapolated by WILLIAM THOMSON (Lord KELVIN) in 1848 — hence K scale. Earlier GAS-LAW data: Charles's Law (V∝T) linearly extrapolated to zero volume at −273°C. RANKINE scale (imperial absolute) rarely used. KELVIN is SI base unit → the only absolute temp in SI; NO 'degree' prefix (write 300 K, not 300°K). Redefined in 2019 via Boltzmann constant k = 1.380649 × 10⁻²³ J/K. theoretical temperature at which particles have minimum vibrational (zero-point) motion.

cards.front:
The unit PARSEC (pc) used in astronomy equals approximately:

(A) 1 light-year
(B) 3.26 LIGHT-YEARS
(C) 100 light-years
(D) 1 astronomical unit
cards.back:
(B) 3.26 LIGHT-YEARS

Units & Measurements — PARSEC (pc) — PAR(allax of one) SEC(ond of arc); the distance at which one astronomical unit subtends an angle of 1 ARCSECOND. 1 pc = 3.0857 × 10¹⁶ m ≈ 3.262 LIGHT-YEARS ≈ 206,265 AU. USE: professional astronomy — galaxies' distances measured in MEGAPARSECS (Mpc = 10⁶ pc) or KILOPARSECS (kpc = 10³ pc). EXAMPLES: (a) Proxima Centauri ≈ 1.301 pc (≈ 4.24 ly); (b) Milky Way radius ≈ 15-20 kpc; (c) Nearest major galaxy (Andromeda M31) ≈ 780 kpc; (d) Observable universe radius ≈ 14,000 Mpc. HUBBLE CONSTANT: ~70 km/s/Mpc. PARALLAX method: measure a star's apparent shift as Earth moves from one side of its orbit to the other (baseline = 2 AU). Tiny angular shift = 1/distance in pc. Only nearby stars (within ~300 pc) have measurable parallax from Earth; GAIA space telescope (ESA, 2013-launched) has mapped parallax for billions of stars to µarcsec precision — current gold standard for stellar distances. BEYOND parallax: STANDARD CANDLES (Cepheid variables' luminosity-period relation — Henrietta Leavitt, 1912; Type Ia supernovae); REDSHIFT (for distant galaxies, Hubble law). ASTRONOMICAL DISTANCES summary: AU (solar system) → ly or pc (stars) → kpc (galaxy) → Mpc (nearby galaxies) → Gpc (cosmological). distance at which 1 AU subtends 1 arcsecond parallax; ≈ 3.086 × 10¹⁶ m.

cards.front:
Match the unit with the quantity measured: (1) TESLA (T); (2) WEBER (Wb); (3) HENRY (H); (4) FARAD (F).

(A) Current, Voltage, Resistance, Power
(B) Magnetic flux density; Magnetic flux; Inductance; Capacitance
(C) Temperature, Radiation, Pressure, Frequency
(D) Luminous intensity, Brightness, Resistance, Charge
cards.back:
(B) Magnetic flux density; Magnetic flux; Inductance; Capacitance

Units & Measurements — ELECTROMAGNETIC SI UNITS: (1) TESLA (T) — MAGNETIC FLUX DENSITY (Wb/m² = kg/(A·s²)); named after NIKOLA TESLA. Earth's magnetic field ~25-65 µT; fridge magnet ~5 mT; MRI machine ~1.5-7 T; LHC magnets ~8 T. (2) WEBER (Wb) — MAGNETIC FLUX (= V·s); named after WILHELM EDUARD WEBER. (3) HENRY (H) — INDUCTANCE (V·s/A = Wb/A); named after JOSEPH HENRY, American physicist who discovered self-inductance. (4) FARAD (F) — CAPACITANCE (C/V); named after MICHAEL FARADAY. Typical capacitors in microfarads (µF) or picofarads (pF); 1 F is very large (supercapacitors). OTHER ELECTRIC UNITS: OHM (Ω, Georg Ohm) = resistance; SIEMENS (S) = 1/Ω = conductance; COULOMB (C, Charles-Augustin de Coulomb) = A·s = charge; VOLT (V, Alessandro Volta) = J/C = potential. LUMINOUS UNITS: CANDELA (cd) = luminous intensity (base unit); LUMEN (lm) = luminous flux = cd·sr; LUX (lx) = lm/m² = illuminance. Reading a book needs ~400 lux; direct sunlight ~100,000 lux. RADIATION UNITS: BECQUEREL (Bq, Henri Becquerel) = 1 decay/sec (activity); CURIE (Ci, old unit) = 3.7 × 10¹⁰ Bq; GRAY (Gy, Louis Harold Gray) = J/kg = absorbed dose; SIEVERT (Sv, Rolf Sievert) = J/kg = equivalent dose (biological effect); banana ~0.1 µSv; dental X-ray ~5 µSv; annual natural background ~3 mSv; lethal ~4 Sv.

cards.front:
The SI PREFIX for 10⁻¹² (one trillionth) is:

(A) Nano (n)
(B) PICO (p) — as in picofarad (pF), picometre (pm), picosecond (ps)
(C) Micro (µ)
(D) Femto (f)
cards.back:
(B) PICO (p) — as in picofarad (pF), picometre (pm), picosecond (ps)

Units & Measurements — SI PREFIX TABLE (magnitude ↑ top, ↓ bottom): | 10²⁴ YOTTA (Y); 10²¹ ZETTA (Z); 10¹⁸ EXA (E); 10¹⁵ PETA (P); 10¹² TERA (T); 10⁹ GIGA (G); 10⁶ MEGA (M); 10³ KILO (k); 10² hecto (h); 10¹ deca (da); 10⁰ BASE UNIT; 10⁻¹ deci (d); 10⁻² centi (c); 10⁻³ MILLI (m); 10⁻⁶ MICRO (µ); 10⁻⁹ NANO (n); 10⁻¹² PICO (p); 10⁻¹⁵ FEMTO (f); 10⁻¹⁸ ATTO (a); 10⁻²¹ ZEPTO (z); 10⁻²⁴ YOCTO (y). 2022 addition (26th CGPM): RONTO (r, 10⁻²⁷), QUECTO (q, 10⁻³⁰), RONNA (R, 10²⁷), QUETTA (Q, 10³⁰). EXAMPLES: (a) PICOSECOND — time for light to travel 0.3 mm; laser pulse timescale. (b) PICOMETRE — atomic scale (H atom radius ~53 pm). (c) PICOFARAD — common capacitor value in electronics. cards.front:
The SI base unit of temperature is the:

(A) Celsius
(B) Kelvin
(C) Fahrenheit
(D) Rankine
cards.back:
(B) Kelvin

Units & Measurements — Kelvin (K) — one of the seven SI base units. Starts at absolute zero (−273.15 °C). Named after Lord Kelvin (William Thomson). The seven SI base units are — metre (length), kilogram (mass), second (time), ampere (current), kelvin (temperature), mole (amount of substance), candela (luminous intensity). Celsius is a SI derived unit; Fahrenheit is the US customary scale.

(B) Joule
(C) Newton

cards.back:

Units & Measurements — Joule (J) — SI unit of energy and work. 1 J = 1 N·m (force × distance). Named after James Prescott Joule. Watt (W) = J/s — unit of power (energy per unit time). Newton — force; Pascal — pressure (N/m²). 1 food calorie = 4,184 J; 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ J.

(B) M L T⁻²

cards.back:

Units & Measurements — Force = mass × acceleration. Dimensions — [M] × [L T⁻²] = [M L T⁻²]. Energy / work = force × distance = [M L² T⁻²]. Pressure = force / area = [M L⁻¹ T⁻²]. Momentum = mass × velocity = [M L T⁻¹]. Useful for dimensional-analysis checks — both sides of any physical equation must have the same dimensions.
